actual: kept, but 'not recognized as a valid pseudo-element' warnings; unknown pseudo-elements count as incompatible with targets (PseudoElement::Custom => return false in is_compatible), so lists get split
root_cause: Pseudo-element enum lacked the new names; added by #930 (v1.29.3). Follow-ups: ::spelling-error/::grammar-error (#1026, v1.30.2), ::search-text (#1213, v1.33.0).
reviewer_lesson: Adding a pseudo-element requires compat data (Feature::...) via build-prefixes.js; otherwise is_compatible treats it as unsupported and splits selector lists for every target.

title: cssmodules-pure-no-check feature
trigger: cssModules.pure with a few intentionally global selectors
actual: pure-mode error
root_cause: Implemented by #898 (v1.29.3): a leading comment containing 'cssmodules-pure-no-check' disables the check (src/stylesheet.rs:172). Maintainer regrets adding linting (pure was added by the Next.js team in #796) and wants no more lint features.
reviewer_lesson: Linting-style options in a compiler need a precise scope (file-leading comment only) and tests that ordinary comments elsewhere do not disable it.

title: `list-style: none` is transpiled to `list-style: outside`
trigger: list-style shorthand containing the ambiguous `none` keyword
actual: list-style:outside (type became disc)
root_cause: 97891d8 ('Fix parsing list-style shorthand', for #867) reordered the shorthand_property! fields so list-style-image parsed before list-style-type; `none` was consumed as Image::None and the type defaulted to disc, then all-default printing emitted `outside`. e3b1e88 replaced the macro parser with a custom ListStyle::parse that counts `none`s and assigns them per spec (src/properties/list.rs). Verified 1.28.2 OK, 1.29.0 broken, 1.29.1+ OK; 1.28.2 also printed `inside none` as `inside`.

regression.evidence: 1.28.2 prints `list-style:none`; 1.29.0 prints `list-style:outside`; fixed same day in v1.29.1 (e3b1e88, commit 4d34f98 'v1.29.1', tag missing); bisect: only 1.29.0

reviewer_lesson: Reordering or rewriting a shorthand parser needs a test matrix of every ambiguous keyword combination (none alone, none+type, none+image, position+none) and a check that omitted-default printing round-trips.

title: :is specificity issue created after compilation
trigger: selector list with different specificities (h1, .h1) containing nested @media declarations, nesting lowered
actual: @media { :is(h1, .h1) {...} } so <h2 class=h1> gets 10px
root_cause: Pre-1.30 lowering wrapped nested declarations in & (=:is(parent list)), which takes the highest specificity of the list. 6c465c1 (v1.30.0) implemented the nested declarations rule: it matches like the parent style rule with the same specificity behavior.

regression.evidence: followed the pre-2024 spec; spec changed with CSSNestedDeclarations

reviewer_lesson: When lowering nesting, compare specificity per original selector; :is() wrapping is only equivalent when every selector in the list has equal specificity.

title: [1.29.x][regression] segfault when require()-ed from a worker thread in Node 22/Linux
trigger: require('lightningcss') only inside a Node worker_thread on Linux, then the worker exits
actual: Segmentation fault in __nptl_deallocate_tsd
root_cause: Rust TLS destructors registered by the unloaded native module (rust-lang/rust#91979), much worse since Rust 1.83 (Devon in tailwindcss#17276). 1.29.0 bumped rustc 1.76.0 -> 1.83.0 (fcc518d) alongside napi 2.15 -> 2.16 (43707c3). Fixed by d302a6b (v1.30.1) linking gnu targets with -Wl,-z,nodelete (.cargo/config.toml). Verified locally: 1.28.2 OK, 1.29.0/1.29.1/1.29.2/1.29.3/1.30.0 segfault, 1.30.1+ OK. Issue is still open; musl and macOS UNVERIFIED (the rustflags only apply to target_env=gnu).

regression.introduced_by: fcc518d rustc 1.76->1.83 (v1.29.0); same release also bumped napi in 43707c3
regression.evidence: reproduced with released binaries: 1.28.2 clean exit, 1.29.0-1.30.0 SIGSEGV, 1.30.1+ clean; reporter: 1.28.x ok, 1.29.x crash

reviewer_lesson: Toolchain and binding bumps need a smoke test that loads the .node only inside a worker thread and lets the worker exit, on every published target.

title: Better (or configurable) order of built-in transpilation vs custom transforms vs CSS modules
trigger: visitor replacing env()/var() expecting built-in transpilation (color-mix, etc.) to run afterwards; renaming idents after CSS modules
expected: entry visitors, then built-in transforms, then exit visitors
actual: replaced values are not transpiled; CSS-modules names applied after visitors
root_cause: napi transform runs stylesheet.visit() before stylesheet.minify() (napi/src/lib.rs:751-761), but any value containing var()/env() was parsed as Property::Unparsed; token replacement in a visitor does not re-parse it into a typed property, so handlers never see it. CSS-modules renaming happens at print time. Workaround: return {property, raw} from a Declaration visitor to force re-parsing. Related open #459; the cross-referenced #1005 (env() visitor saw whitespace already stripped) was fixed by 32f1f52 'Do not remove whitespace in token lists' (v1.31.0).
reviewer_lesson: When a value contains var()/env(), assume all typed transforms are off; a PR that claims to transform such values must show where the token list is re-parsed.

title: compiled output under `@layer` scope does not work well with `*` selector
trigger: unknown at-rule (@apply) nested in a style rule while lowering nesting
expected: maintainer: preprocess @apply before lightningcss; ideally the at-rule stays inside `*`
actual: <=1.32.0 hoisted it to `@layer base { @apply rounded-none; }`, dropping the selector
root_cause: Closed as user error (Tailwind should process @apply first). The hoisting itself was later fixed by #1233 (729e03e, v1.33.0, for #1232): unknown at-rules are printed in place. Verified: 1.28.2-1.32.0 hoist, 1.33.0 keeps `* { @apply ... }`.
reviewer_lesson: Nesting lowering must keep unknown at-rules attached to their parent selector context; check outputs for orphaned at-rules.

title: CSS parsing failure for nested var()
trigger: var(var(--x))
actual: Unexpected token Function("var") error; errorRecovery drops the declaration (also for custom properties)
root_cause: var() requires a <custom-property-name> as first argument, so the declaration is invalid at parse time in browsers too; lightningcss errors by design and errorRecovery removes it (equivalent).

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Strict errors are intentional; when changing strictness, check that errorRecovery drops exactly what browsers drop and nothing more.

title: Incorrect conversion from color-mix to oklab
trigger: color-mix(in oklab, ...) producing tiny negative components printed in scientific notation
root_cause: CSSNumber::to_css (src/values/number.rs) handled |n|<1 by writing '-' and trimming a leading "-0", assuming fixed notation; for -7.45058e-9 nothing was trimmed. #901 (v1.29.2) fixed numbers; the identical logic in serialize_dimension (src/values/length.rs) was fixed only by #1192 (v1.33.0) and src/values/percentage.rs:69 is still unfixed on master (`-1e-7%` -> `--10e-8%`, verified 1.28.2-1.33.0).

regression.introduced_by: v1.20.0 (bisect; exact commit not identified). The double-minus printer logic dates from 2021 (7529be2/16aa687)
regression.evidence: bisect: <=1.19 valid, 1.20.0..1.29.1 print '--', fixed in 1.29.2 (#901); the same trick in serialize_dimension fixed by #1192

reviewer_lesson: A serialization fix must grep for the same trick in sibling serializers (number, length, percentage, angle, time, resolution) and add negative + scientific-notation cases for each.

title: CSS modules scoped and global class name selectors aren't combined when minified
trigger: :global(.c) rules with identical declarations next to local rules
repro_css: .a { color: red; } .b { color: red; } :global(.c) { color: red; } :global(.d) { color: red; }
actual: .x_a,.x_b{color:red}.c{color:red}.d{color:red}
root_cause: PseudoClass::Global/Local fall into `PseudoClass::Custom { .. } | _ => return false` in is_compatible (src/selector.rs:1994), so merge_style_rules (src/rules/mod.rs) refuses; with targets, a list like `.a, :global(.b)` is also wrapped in :is() or split (verified: chrome 100 -> `:is(.x_a,.b)`). Equal-selector :global rules are not merged either.
reviewer_lesson: is_compatible must explicitly classify compile-away pseudo-classes (:global/:local) and every new PseudoClass variant; the catch-all `_ => false` silently disables merging and triggers selector splitting.

title: add support for compress css to native css nesting
trigger: request to re-nest flat CSS as a minification
actual: flat output
root_cause: Feature request; closed as duplicate (by sapphi-red, no link). Canonical is most likely open #623 'Possible to use nesting as minification feature' (UNVERIFIED).
reviewer_lesson: Re-nesting is not a pure syntax change: & uses :is() specificity and cannot represent pseudo-elements, so any such PR needs specificity-preservation proofs.

title: Requesting support for Android Termux
trigger: installing on Android Termux
actual: no prebuilt binary
root_cause: No android target was published; #932 (v1.30.0) added android-arm64 only (no armv7).
reviewer_lesson: New platform targets need install+load smoke tests and matching optionalDependencies/detect logic in node/index.js.

title: Minify - omit contents of invalid @media queries
trigger: media queries that can never match
actual: kept
root_cause: No dead-query elimination exists.
reviewer_lesson: Any query-pruning PR must handle mixed units (em vs px, font-relative), not/or/only, media types and unknown features conservatively.

title: :where(::before) and :where(::after) is compiled to :where()
trigger: :where(::before)
actual: :where()
root_cause: Pseudo-elements are not valid inside :is()/:where(); the forgiving selector list drops them, matching browsers (CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync gives ':where()').
reviewer_lesson: Before calling a selector rewrite a bug, compare with the browser's own serialization (CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync + selectorText).

title: Malformed @supports block when using combined :root, :host selectors
trigger: selector list where every selector is incompatible with targets (:root in IE 8, :host; or nested & with iOS<14/IE11) plus a declaration needing @supports color fallback
options: targets ie 8, safari 15 (Tailwind v4 output with 'last 4 versions' / '>= 0.2%')
actual: leading `@supports (color: lab(0% 0 0)) { { --c: lab(100% 0 0) } }` with an empty selector; re-minifying fails with 'Invalid empty selector'
root_cause: CssRuleList::minify (src/rules/mod.rs ~758-822 and 898) partitions incompatible selectors; when none are compatible, style.selectors becomes empty and the rule itself is skipped (is_empty), but get_supports_rules(&style) and get_additional_rules(&style) are still computed for the emptied rule and pushed. Verified on 1.28.2-1.33.0; master unchanged in that path.

regression.evidence: present in 1.28.2; the nested variant #1010 appears from 1.30.0 because nested rules started getting color fallbacks (Component::Nesting maps to Feature::IsSelector)

reviewer_lesson: Any code that rewrites a rule's selector list must handle the empty-list case for every derived rule (@supports fallbacks, logical/dir rules, prefixed copies), and the output must re-parse.

title: Unable to compose class named `default`
trigger: composes: <name> where the class name is a reserved word (default, initial, inherit, unset, revert...)
repro_css: .default { color: blue; } .foo { composes: default; color: red; }
expected: foo composes EgL3uq_default (export) and the composes declaration is removed
actual: no composes in exports; `composes: default;` printed as an unknown declaration, no error or warning
root_cause: Composes::parse -> parse_one_ident -> CustomIdent::parse (src/properties/css_modules.rs:78-87, src/values/ident.rs:34) rejects `default` and CSS-wide keywords; the failure silently falls back to an unparsed declaration. Class names are not <custom-ident>s. Open PR #909 switches to input.expect_ident().
reviewer_lesson: When a typed parse of a known property fails, check whether the fallback (unparsed) path silently changes semantics (here: lost composition) instead of erroring.

title: Segmentation fault 11
trigger: sum of two parenthesized sums whose terms cannot be combined (unlike units)
actual: stack overflow -> SIGSEGV (playground: too much recursion)
root_cause: Mutual recursion: Calc::add arm `(Sum, Sum) => V::try_from(a)?.add(V::try_from(b)?)` (src/values/calc.rs:955) calls Length::add, whose `(Length::Calc(a), Length::Calc(b)) => a.add(*b)` (src/values/length.rs:710) calls Calc::add with the same operands. Verified crashing on 1.28.2-1.33.0; e3c8e12 (v1.28.0) fixed other overflow cases (#827/#791/#611) but not this one. Open PR #1245 flattens and reduces sum terms.

regression.evidence: reported on 1.24.1; still crashes on 1.33.0 and master source is unchanged at calc.rs:955/length.rs:710; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: calc simplification changes need adversarial inputs (sum of sums, unlike units, nested min/max/clamp, negative terms) run in a subprocess so a stack overflow is caught, and the recursion must provably shrink.

title: Add a feature to resolve dependencies for Bundle API
trigger: bundle() with @import of a bare package specifier
actual: must pass a JS resolver
root_cause: Bundler only resolves relative paths unless a resolver is provided; request for built-in resolution. Related #747.
reviewer_lesson: Resolver features must preserve @import layer/supports/media conditions and source_index ordering of the bundled output.

title: ERROR  Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
trigger: Alpine (musl) container loads lightningcss
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
root_cause: node/index.js libc detection via detect-libc 1.0.3 misdetected musl; fixed by upgrading detect-libc (#923, v1.29.2; familySync()/MUSL in node/index.js).
reviewer_lesson: Changes to native-binary selection need a musl (Alpine) and glibc smoke test; the loader's catch-and-retry hides the first error.

title: `@container style(--variable)` without value results in an error
trigger: @container style(--var) boolean style query (no value)
actual: Unexpected end of input (errorRecovery removed the rule)
root_cause: StyleQuery parser required `: value`; 2284653 (v1.29.2) allows a bare custom property feature (src/rules/container.rs).
reviewer_lesson: For query grammars, test every production in the spec grammar (boolean form, not/and/or nesting) rather than just the common `name: value` form.

title: height rounded
trigger: decimal values with more than 6 significant digits
actual: rounded to 6 significant digits
root_cause: Numbers are f32 and serialized through cssparser/dtoa-short with 6 significant digits; maintainer says this matches browser serialization. Note CSSOM says <=6 decimals (not significant digits), see #949.
reviewer_lesson: Precision changes affect every numeric output; check large values (>=1e6) and integers in custom properties, not just fractions.

title: linear-gradient `to` keyword conversion error
trigger: linear-gradient(to <side>|to <corner>|<angle>) lowered to -webkit-linear-gradient for old targets
actual: -webkit-linear-gradient(right, red, green) (reversed)
root_cause: Prefixed fallback copied the standard direction; legacy keywords name the start side and legacy angles are math angles (0deg = right, counter-clockwise). #936 (v1.30.0) adds convert_to_legacy_direction/convert_to_legacy_degree (src/values/gradient.rs:551-610). Still open (#1107): LinearGradient::to_css (gradient.rs:268-330) treats Vertical(Bottom) as the default and Vertical(Top) as reversible for prefixed gradients too, and LineDirection::to_css prints Horizontal(Left) as 270deg under minify; verified 1.28.2-1.33.0: -webkit-linear-gradient(bottom, a, b) -> (a, b) even without minify; (top, a, b) -> (b, a) and (left, ...) -> (270deg, ...) when minified.

regression.evidence: bisect of minified output: <=1.29.3 90deg, >=1.30.1 270deg; both wrong for legacy semantics

reviewer_lesson: Prefixed legacy syntaxes have different semantics from the standard ones (start side vs to-side, math angles); every optimization (default omission, stop reversal, angle conversion) must branch on the vendor prefix.

title: ailed to load config from C:\Users\visha\Desktop\Ehome\vite.config.js error when starting dev server: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node'
trigger: Windows without the VC++ runtime
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node'
root_cause: Same as #920 (missing VCRUNTIME140.dll; masked by node/index.js fallback require); closed by maintainer; fixed by e5c4139 (v1.30.0).
reviewer_lesson: Load-failure reports need the original dlopen error; the loader should surface it instead of the fallback path's 'Cannot find module'.

title: error when starting dev server: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node'
trigger: loading lightningcss-win32-x64-msvc on Windows without the Visual C++ redistributable
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node' (underlying: error 126, missing DLL)
root_cause: MSVC builds linked the CRT dynamically; e5c4139 (v1.30.0) adds +crt-static for x86_64/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc (.cargo/config.toml). node/index.js tries require('lightningcss-<platform>') and on failure requires '../lightningcss.<platform>.node', so the second 'Cannot find module' error replaces the real one (still the case on master node/index.js:16-21).

regression.evidence: surge came with Tailwind v4 adoption (Jan 2025); dynamic CRT linkage was the Rust MSVC default before (UNVERIFIED whether older builds differed); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Release-pipeline changes need a clean-VM load test per platform; error handling in the loader must not swallow the first failure.

title: @property initial-value parsing error
trigger: @property initial-value whose value cannot be resolved at build time (color-mix with currentColor)
repro_css: @property --my-color { syntax: "<color>"; inherits: true; initial-value: color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 15%, transparent); }
actual: Unexpected token Function("color-mix") (whole stylesheet fails; location always line 1 col 12)
root_cause: PropertyRule::parse (src/rules/property.rs:89-100) re-parses the initial-value substring with a fresh ParserInput via syntax.parse_value; CssColor::parse only accepts color-mix() it can resolve, and there is no token-list fallback; the fresh parser also loses the stylesheet location. Normal declarations keep such color-mix() as unparsed tokens. Labeled bug by maintainer.
reviewer_lesson: Values that are parsed in secondary contexts (@property initial-value, @font-face descriptors, style attributes) must have the same unresolvable-value fallback and error locations as ordinary declarations.

title: chained selectors split into repeated blocks (browserslist ignored?)
trigger: selector list containing ::selection with iOS Safari in targets
actual: split into two rules
root_cause: By design: compat data marks ::selection unsupported in iOS Safari, and an unsupported selector invalidates the whole list in that browser, so lightningcss splits it (src/rules/mod.rs incompatible partition).
reviewer_lesson: Selector splitting is driven by per-browser compat data; changes to it must be checked with ios_saf, not just safari.

title: Suggestion: Nesting should be renamed to Unnesting
trigger: naming of Features.Nesting
root_cause: Naming suggestion; maintainer: feature names are nouns for the syntax that gets compiled. Closed not planned.
reviewer_lesson: Renaming public Features flags is a breaking API change across node/flags.js, index.d.ts and Rust.

title: Strange behavoiur for prefixing property `user-select`
trigger: user-select with Safari/iOS targets newer than the prefix data snapshot (18.2/18.3)
actual: user-select: all only (<=1.29.1)
root_cause: Generated src/prefixes.rs had `version >= 196864 && version <= 1179904` (Safari 3.1-18.1); scripts/build-prefixes.js keeps an upper bound unless the last prefixed version equals caniuse's latest agent version, so autoprefixer data lagging caniuse-lite leaves a closed range. Data bump eccb673 (v1.29.2) and later bumps made it open-ended. Verified: 1.28.2-1.29.1 unprefixed, 1.29.2+ prefixed for safari 18.2. Issue still open/pending triage.

regression.introduced_by: 4159bc5 'Bump browser compat data' (v1.28.2) capped Safari/iOS user-select prefixing at 18.1
regression.evidence: git: 4159bc5 added `version <= 1179904` (18.1); eccb673 (v1.29.2) raised it to 18.3; c03a7e7 (v1.29.3) removed the cap. Bisect: 1.17.1..1.27.0 prefixed, 1.28.2..1.29.1 unprefixed, 1.29.3+ prefixed

reviewer_lesson: For compat-data bumps, diff prefixes.rs for closed upper bounds at the snapshot's newest version and test targets newer than the snapshot.

title: LogicalProperties Conversion Skipped with CSS Variable in calc()
trigger: logical shorthand (inset, inset-inline, margin-block, padding-inline...) whose value contains var(), with targets lacking the shorthand
actual: shorthand passed through unchanged (ignored by the target browser); longhands like margin-inline-start with var() ARE converted
root_cause: side_handler! in src/properties/margin_padding.rs (and inset) pushes Property::Unparsed shorthands as-is because a bare var() could expand to several components. Open PR #1227 splits when the token list is not a lone var(), but would also split multi-component lists such as `calc(var(--s)) 5px`, producing invalid longhands.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Splitting an unparsed shorthand into longhands is only safe when the token list is provably one component (a single math function or var-free value); test multi-component lists with var() and whitespace.

title: `calc(<LENGTH> - 0)` should be simplified to `<LENGTH>`
trigger: calc() adding a <number> (unitless 0) to a <length>
expected: (request) simplify to 100px; spec: declaration invalid, so margin-left stays 3px
actual: kept as calc(100px - 0); with an earlier valid declaration lightningcss deletes the fallback: `.t{margin-left:calc(100px - 0)}`
root_cause: Request closed not planned: calc(100px - 0) is invalid (unitless 0 is a <number> in math functions). But lightningcss's Calc parser accepts Sum(Value, Number) (pinned by test src/lib.rs:8538 `calc(1px + 1)`), so the property is typed and the declaration handler dedupes the earlier valid `margin-left: 3px` away. Verified 1.28.2-1.33.0 also for `width: 3px; width: calc(0 + 5px)`. Unfiled.
reviewer_lesson: If lightningcss accepts a value that browsers reject, dedupe/merging will delete the author's valid fallback; parsing strictness for typed properties must match the spec's type checking.

title: Windows compatibility seems down
trigger: Windows (Next.js + Tailwind) loading the msvc binary; esbuild bundling node/index.js
actual: error 126 loading lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node; esbuild: Could not resolve "../pkg"
root_cause: Same CRT linkage as #920, fixed by e5c4139 (v1.30.0). The esbuild error came from the CSS_TRANSFORMER_WASM branch `require('../pkg')` in node/index.js, removed by #1170 (v1.32.0).
reviewer_lesson: Dynamic requires in node/index.js affect bundlers that inline it; keep the loader statically analyzable.

title: `text-size-adjust` is not prefixed for WebKit
trigger: text-size-adjust with targets that contain desktop Safari but not ios_saf (e.g. Vite defaults)
actual: no -webkit- added, and an authored -webkit-text-size-adjust is removed (output: -moz-text-size-adjust + text-size-adjust)
root_cause: prefixes.rs adds WebKit for text-size-adjust only for ios_saf >= 5 (desktop Safari has neither form), so it is correct for ios_saf targets (verified 1.28.2-1.33.0) but prefix removal drops authored prefixes when ios_saf is absent. Open PR #1178 hand-edits generated src/prefixes.rs to always add -webkit- (would be overwritten by build-prefixes.js and adds the prefix for chrome-only targets).
reviewer_lesson: Desktop and iOS Safari are separate targets; check that prefix removal never deletes an authored prefixed declaration needed by a browser family the caller may not have listed, and reject hand edits to generated prefixes.rs/compat.rs.

title: `animation: move2 var(--animation-time) alternate infinite;` is not parsed correctly
trigger: animation shorthand with var() in a CSS module, Rust API without StyleSheet::minify()
repro_css: .animate2 { animation: move2 var(--animation-time) alternate infinite; } @keyframes move2 { to { margin-left: 40px } }
actual: Unparsed animation; name not scoped
root_cause: A var() makes the shorthand ambiguous so it stays Property::Unparsed; AnimationHandler rewrites non-keyword idents to AnimationName tokens during StyleSheet::minify (src/properties/animation.rs ~844-870). Turbopack skipped minify() in dev; fixed downstream (next.js #77313). Same API trap breaks light-dark() (cargo-leptos#622); open #1118.
reviewer_lesson: Behavior that lives in minify() handlers (scoping, toggles, prefixes) is skipped by Rust callers that only print; new transforms should not depend on both phases running.

title: Empty :is() when minifying LightningCSS output
trigger: & used under a parent list containing a pseudo-element (input::file-selector-button)
actual: selectors that match nothing / empty :is() after re-minify
root_cause: The nesting selector cannot represent pseudo-elements, so the input matches nothing natively either; output is equivalent.
reviewer_lesson: Compile-then-minify (two passes) is a good idempotency test; but check the native meaning first before treating differences as bugs.

title: Unable to parse specific css urls
trigger: url('data:...<svg xmlns="...">...') with double quotes inside a single-quoted url string
actual: reporter: parse error (node)
root_cause: Not reproducible on 1.28.2-1.33.0 linux-x64-gnu binaries: the string is re-serialized as url("...\"...\"...") and re-parses. The repro also uses the non-property `backgroundColor`, which is kept as an unknown declaration and moved before `background`. UNVERIFIED: likely environment-specific.
reviewer_lesson: Quote-flipping serialization must escape the chosen quote character; keep a round-trip test with both quote kinds inside url() and strings.

title: Odd handling of specific character "E" in certain cases, being mapped to unicode U+0065
trigger: dimension token whose unit starts with e/E (e.g. 0e)
actual: 0\65 (trailing space kept even when minified)
root_cause: serialize_dimension (src/values/length.rs:513) delegates to cssparser Token::Dimension serialization, which escapes a leading e/E in the unit so the output cannot be re-tokenized as scientific notation (1e-3). Valid and equivalent; `0e` is an invalid height anyway.
reviewer_lesson: Unit/ident escaping changes must keep units like e, e-3, E3 from re-tokenizing as exponents.

title: Transform @property at-rule into CSS variables
trigger: @property for browsers without it (Safari 15)
actual: kept
root_cause: Not emulatable: registration changes parsing, inheritance and animation of the property (maintainer).
reviewer_lesson: Reject 'lowerings' that only approximate a feature (e.g. @property -> initial values) unless every observable behavior is preserved.

title: Nesting breaks at-rules
trigger: declarations directly inside a nested group rule (@media/@starting-style) under a pseudo-element or :open parent
expected: @media (...) { display: none; } kept as nested declarations
actual: @media (...) { & { display: none; } } (<=1.29.3); & cannot represent pseudo-elements so the declaration is ignored
root_cause: Printer wrapped declarations of nested group rules in an explicit `& {}` per the pre-2024 spec; 6c465c1 (v1.30.0) implemented the nested declarations rule and prints bare declarations.

regression.evidence: followed the old spec; became wrong when CSSNestedDeclarations shipped

reviewer_lesson: Never insert explicit `& {}` wrappers or move declarations relative to nested rules; check pseudo-element parents and specificity under CSSNestedDeclarations.

title: Add support for picker pseudo-element
trigger: ::picker(select), ::picker-icon, ::checkmark
actual: warnings (unknown pseudo-element)
root_cause: Added by #957 (v1.30.0) with compat data.
reviewer_lesson: Functional pseudo-elements need argument parsing/printing tests plus compat entries so targets do not split lists.

title: color-mix is not transpiled after replace var with their color value
trigger: visitor replacing var() inside color-mix() with a literal color
repro_css: :root { --c: hsl(120deg 10% 20%); } .x { background-color: color-mix(in hsl, var(--c) 25%, hsl(30deg 30% 40%)); }
actual: color-mix left unevaluated
root_cause: Duplicate of #459 (visitor ordering / multi-pass). The declaration was parsed as Property::Unparsed because of var(); the visitor's token replacement does not re-parse it, so minify() never sees a typed color-mix. Returning {property, raw} from a Declaration visitor forces re-parsing.
reviewer_lesson: Visitor API changes should state which phase sees typed values; test a token-level replacement followed by a transform that needs typed values.

title: :is() selector is used to de-nesting selector even target is set to Chrome 87
trigger: nesting lowered for targets without :is() (chrome 87)
actual: :is(.test-0, .test-1) .a (unsupported in Chrome 87, rule dropped)
root_cause: Duplicate of #202: lowering nesting below :is() support is not implemented (expansion can be exponential and impossible for some combinators); output uses :is() regardless of targets.
reviewer_lesson: For lowering features, check the output only uses syntax supported by the lowest target (here :is()); flag silent reliance on newer syntax.

title: lightningcss ate my precision
trigger: numbers with more than 6 significant digits, including integers in custom properties
expected: integers kept in full; CSSOM allows up to 6 decimals
root_cause: Values are f32 and printed with 6 significant digits via cssparser (dtoa-short). Token::Number in custom properties is printed through CSSNumber::to_css (src/properties/custom.rs:544-546), ignoring int_value, so integers above 6 digits are rounded (verified 1.28.2-1.33.0, print mode). Integer dimensions in custom properties keep digits since the cssparser 0.37 upgrade in 1.33.0 (`--w: 1234567px`). Maintainer considers fractional rounding browser-compatible; upstream servo/rust-cssparser#430 closed without change.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Numeric serialization changes must be tested on integers > 999999 and on custom-property token values, where authored text is observable via getPropertyValue and var() consumers.

title: Support for OpenBSD/adJ
trigger: installing lightningcss-cli on OpenBSD/adJ 7.6 (amd64); there is no prebuilt binary for openbsd
expected: install succeeds (or a wasm fallback is used)
actual: postinstall fails: 'Failed to move lightningcss-cli binary into place.'
root_cause: No openbsd target in the scripts/build-npm.js triples, and the CLI postinstall has no wasm fallback. The reporter closed it after switching to lightningcss-wasm via pnpm overrides (tailwindcss#17452).
reviewer_lesson: Packaging changes (scripts/build-npm.js, node/index.js, cli/postinstall.js) must be checked against the full platform matrix and must fail with a clear message on unsupported platforms.

title: custom media are not replaced when a visitor returns the style sheet on StyleSheetExit
trigger: JS visitor whose StyleSheet/StyleSheetExit callback returns the stylesheet (s => s), with drafts.customMedia and targets
options: drafts: {customMedia: true}, targets chrome 100, visitor {StyleSheetExit: s => s}
expected: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.animation{color:red}}, the same as when the visitor returns undefined
actual: the @custom-media rule is kept and @media (--motionOK) stays unresolved (verified on 1.29.3 and 1.33.0). With cssModules:true, the same visitor also turns off class hashing and exports (verified on 1.33.0).
root_cause: StyleSheet.options is #[serde(skip)] (src/stylesheet.rs:89-91). napi call_visitor (napi/src/transformer.rs:623-637) replaces *value with the deserialized StyleSheet, so ParserOptions resets to Default. minify() then no longer sees ParserFlags::CUSTOM_MEDIA (src/stylesheet.rs:232), and css_modules is None (src/stylesheet.rs:253, 291).
reviewer_lesson: A #[serde(skip)] field on any type a JS visitor can return is silently reset to Default on the round-trip. Check whether state lives in skipped fields (StyleSheet.options, content_hashes), and test visitor identity (return the node unchanged) for every visitable type.

title: @property with <ratio> returns bad value
trigger: @property with syntax "<ratio>" (or "<line-style>"), generated by Sass in charts.css
expected: per the maintainer, rejected: <ratio> is not a supported syntax component name
actual: ERROR: Invalid value (1.29.3 and 1.33.0). With errorRecovery, the whole @property rule is dropped with a warning.
root_cause: css-properties-values-api section 5.1 allows only these syntax component names: angle, color, custom-ident, image, integer, length, length-percentage, number, percentage, resolution, string, time, transform-function, transform-list, url. <ratio> and <line-style> are not among them. Chrome 156 also ignores the rule (verified: the registered initial value is not applied).
reviewer_lesson: The current ED makes an invalid syntax descriptor 'invalid and ignored': the rule stays valid with syntax '*' and inherits true. Chrome 156 still drops the whole rule. Verify any @property validation change in shipping browsers, not only against the ED.

title: i can,t run dev
trigger: Vite dev server (esbuild dep optimizer) bundling lightningcss/node/index.js
actual: [ERROR] Could not resolve "../pkg" at node/index.js:17
root_cause: Through v1.31, node/index.js had `if (process.env.CSS_TRANSFORMER_WASM) module.exports = require('../pkg')`, which static bundlers try to resolve. Closed as a duplicate of #701, which is still open. That branch was removed in 96c5c6d (#1170, v1.32.0). UNVERIFIED whether this fixes the Vite case.
reviewer_lesson: node/index.js must stay statically resolvable by bundlers, so it must not require() paths that are missing from the published package.

title: GitHub Actions Linux fails to find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node' even though it works locally on mac
trigger: lockfile created on macOS, then a clean install on Linux CI leaves out the optional lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu package
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
root_cause: A package-manager bug with optional dependencies in lockfiles (npm/cli PR #8184), not LightningCSS. Workaround: list the linux gnu/musl packages in optionalDependencies.
reviewer_lesson: 'Cannot find module ../lightningcss.<triple>.node' reports usually come from the package manager's optional-dependency handling. Check the lockfile before suspecting the loader.

title: error when starting dev server: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node'
trigger: Windows with Vite and Tailwind 4: the optional lightningcss-win32-x64-msvc package is missing
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-x64-msvc.node'
root_cause: Missing optional platform package (package-manager issue). The workaround from #920 fixed it for the reporter; duplicate of the #920 family.
reviewer_lesson: Same as #956: failures to resolve the platform binary are a packaging problem, not a transform-correctness one.

title: Is there a standalone executable that I can use without installing node?
trigger: asks for a standalone CLI executable that does not need Node
root_cause: Answered: download the lightningcss-cli-<triple> tarball from the npm registry; it contains a ~10 MB static binary.
reviewer_lesson: Nothing for correctness: the CLI wraps the same Rust core as napi, so both behave the same.

title: support an option to keep invalid css in the output
trigger: errorRecovery with framework syntax such as `:deep(.foo)-bar {}` or Tailwind `--color-*: initial`
expected: requested: invalid rules and declarations passed through verbatim for later tools
actual: on 1.33.0 the invalid rule and declaration are dropped with warnings; `::v-deep()` and `:global()` are kept, with warnings
root_cause: The AST cannot represent invalid rules or declarations, and error recovery follows css-syntax by dropping the construct. The maintainer prefers that pre-processors run before LightningCSS, and that narrow type-checking cases (#209) get fixed instead.
reviewer_lesson: errorRecovery means browser semantics: drop the invalid construct and continue. A PR that preserves invalid CSS must not change how the valid CSS around it parses, and must keep the warnings.

title: bug: `@property` rules remain nested in selector when targeting Chrome ≥120
trigger: @property nested directly inside a style rule
repro_css: .example { @property --angle { syntax: '<angle>'; inherits: true; initial-value: 0turn; } animation: spin 3s linear infinite; }
options: any; with targets that lower nesting (chrome <=119) the rule is hoisted
expected: a parse error, as for nested @keyframes (a warning under errorRecovery), per the maintainer
actual: Up to 1.30.2: warning 'Unknown at rule: @property', and the rule stays nested. Since 1.31.0: accepted silently, still nested, no warning. When nesting is lowered, the rule is hoisted to the top level, so a rule browsers ignore becomes a working registration.
root_cause: NestedRuleParser::parse_prelude returns early for "property" and "position-try" (src/parser.rs:731-739), which skips the `is_in_style_rule && !allowed_in_style_rule()` check at src/parser.rs:744. #1090 added that arm (to allow @property inside group rules) and removed the old warning path.

regression.introduced_by: #1090 (28d7794, v1.31.0) made it silent; the nested output itself is older
regression.evidence: Local bisect: 1.30.2 warns 'Unknown at rule: @property'; 1.31.0 and 1.33.0 give no warning for the same input.; bisect

reviewer_lesson: An early `return Ok(..)` in parse_prelude skips the shared context validation. Test every new at-rule arm in four places: nested in a style rule, in @media inside a style rule, inside a top-level group rule, and at the top level.

title: `:where` not being transpiled for older browsers
trigger: :where() left in the output while the targets include browsers without :where() support
expected: a warning that the output uses syntax the targets don't support (the maintainer agreed to this)
actual: on 1.33.0, :where() is kept with no warning
root_cause: :where() has zero specificity, so it cannot be lowered without changing specificity. LightningCSS has no 'unsupported by targets' diagnostic.
reviewer_lesson: Selector rewrites must keep specificity exactly the same. Reject proposals that strip :where(). Note that the existing :is() -> :-webkit-any() fallbacks already change specificity in Chromium (see #997).

title: `@mixin` example from documentation breaks property ordering
trigger: the documented @mixin/@apply custom at-rule visitor returns a style-block body (which becomes a nested `&{}` rule), followed by declarations
repro_css: article blockquote { @apply card; border-top-left-radius: 0; }  /* mixin card = border-radius: var(--r) */
options: customAtRules mixin(style-block)/apply, visitor Rule.custom, targets that lower nesting
expected: the mixin declarations stay at the @apply position, so the later border-top-left-radius wins
actual: Up to 1.29.3, the nested rule is emitted after the parent's declarations, so border-radius overrides border-top-left-radius.
root_cause: The pre-2024 nesting spec moved all declarations before nested rules; 6c465c1 (v1.30.0) implemented nested declarations rules (CSSNestedDeclarations). Follow-up regression: since v1.30.2 the same documented example fails with 'failed to deserialize; expected an object-like struct named Specifier, found ()' when the mixin body contains var() (DashedIdentReference.from: null). It comes from the serde-content migration in #1062 (9879b91) and is still open as #1065/#1071/#1081 (verified 1.30.2-1.33.0).
reviewer_lesson: Rules returned by visitors go back through the nesting and declaration pipeline. Check the order of interleaved declarations and nested rules, and round-trip every AST shape a visitor can return through JS (#1062 broke var() nodes).

title: Suggestion on Expanding Node.js tests
trigger: proposal to move the Node tests to Vitest with table-driven test.each fixtures, plus a `just` wrapper
root_cause: Test-infrastructure suggestion; the Vitest PR #967 was closed without being merged.
reviewer_lesson: Backs the probe-corpus approach: many tiny input -> output cases across napi and wasm cover more per unit of maintenance than large end-to-end fixtures.

title: "Unknown at rule: @view-transition" in 1.29.3
trigger: @view-transition nested inside a style rule (:root { @view-transition { navigation: auto } })
expected: an error saying the at-rule is not allowed in this context
actual: ERROR 'Unknown at rule: @view-transition', although the rule is known and only disallowed inside a style rule
root_cause: User error. The wrong-context path returns BasicParseErrorKind::AtRuleInvalid, which prints as 'Unknown at rule' (src/parser.rs:744), so the message is misleading.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Context errors reuse the 'Unknown at rule' message, so expect reports like this whenever an at-rule appears in the wrong context; a dedicated error kind would be clearer.

title: Unknown at rule: @property
trigger: @property inside @layer (also @media and @supports), e.g. the daisyUI base properties
expected: a parsed @property kept inside the layer, with no warning
actual: Up to 1.30.2: warning 'Unknown at rule: @property', and the body is kept as raw, unminified tokens.
root_cause: The "property" prelude was handled only in TopLevelRuleParser (src/parser.rs ~L323 at 400f705), so NestedRuleParser fell through to an unknown rule. The maintainer first replied that it is only valid at the top level, but WPT (css-cascade/layer-property-override.html) and css-conditional-3 #contents-of show it is valid. Fixed by #1090.
reviewer_lesson: Check 'this is invalid' claims against WPT and css-conditional-3 #contents-of: group rules accept any top-level rule. PR #1314 tightens the same code path, so keep a guard for @property inside @layer, @media and @supports.

title: Vendor prefixes may be duplicated if the value is a CSS variable
trigger: an authored -webkit-mask-image/mask-image pair with an unparsed value (var()), with targets that need the -webkit- mask prefix
actual: .bar{-webkit-mask-image:var(--foo);-webkit-mask-image:var(--foo);mask-image:var(--foo)}. Not idempotent: each run adds another copy (verified 1.18.0-1.33.0). `mask` behaves the same way.
root_cause: The MaskHandler branch for unparsed values (src/properties/masking.rs:700-707) calls get_prefixed() and pushes the result without merging it into the identical authored prefixed declaration just before it. Parsed values and the other handlers do merge prefixes.
reviewer_lesson: Run the transform twice. Code that adds prefixes to Property::Unparsed values must be idempotent and must merge with an identical authored prefixed declaration.

title: oklch in @property doesn't accept `<number>`
trigger: oklch()/lab() with a <number> lightness, e.g. oklch(0.5 0 0): a hard error in @property initial-value, silently left unparsed elsewhere
repro_css:
@property --c { syntax: "<color>"; inherits: false; initial-value: oklch(0.5 0 0); }
.t { color: oklch(0.5 0.1 200); }
expected: parsed as a color: accepted in @property, and lowered with a hex fallback for old targets
actual: Up to 1.29.3: ERROR 'Unexpected token Function("oklch")' in @property, and `color: oklch(.5 .1 200)` passes through unlowered (verified)
root_cause: Before #465, the lab/lch/oklab/oklch parsers required <percentage> lightness (older CSS Color 4). Outside typed contexts the declaration silently fell back to an unparsed token list (src/properties/custom.rs TokenList), which hid the parse failure and skipped lowering. Closed as a duplicate of #809, fixed by #465 (4ebcb45, v1.30.0).
reviewer_lesson: A value parser that fails falls back to Property::Unparsed without any error, losing lowering and minification. Check that lowering still emits fallbacks for old targets (typed parse vs unparsed), not just that no error is thrown.

title: Bug in ordering of nested `@layer`s
trigger: `@layer one, one.a, one.b;` then `@layer one { @layer b {..} }` then `@layer one.a {..}` (one sub-layer reached through a nested block, another through a dotted name)
options: any (transform() always runs minify; print mode is affected too)
expected: layer order one, one.a, one.b, so red wins
actual: `@layer one{@layer b{..}}@layer one.a{..}@layer one.b;`, so one.b comes before one.a and green wins (verified in Chrome 156 through the probe). Also `@layer components; @layer components.legacy{..} @layer components{@layer legacy{..}}` comes out with the two blocks swapped.
root_cause: CssRuleList::minify (src/rules/mod.rs) turned each name in an @layer statement into a placeholder LayerBlock keyed by the full dotted name, merged later blocks into those placeholders, and turned leftover empty ones into statements. That ignored that `one { @layer b }` and `one.a` address the same hierarchy. The fix 32aecd9 keys by root layer name, merges only identical names, and stops merging across non-layer rules, conditional groups and @import.

regression.evidence: Local bisect: 1.22.1 keeps `@layer one,one.a,one.b;` first (correct); 1.23.0 through 1.33.0 print `@layer one.b;` last. Fixed on master by 32aecd9 (2026-09-26), not yet in a release as of v1.33.0.; bisect: 1.33.0 wrong, master right

reviewer_lesson: Layer order is set by first appearance, across dotted names and nested blocks. Test any @layer merge or hoist with sub-layers declared by another route, inside conditional groups, and via @import layer().

title: Automatic `:is()` wrapping of pseudo-elements + nested media query produces invalid CSS
trigger: a selector list with pseudo-elements and a nested @media, with nesting lowered
actual: Up to 1.29.3: `@media screen{:is(.foo:after,.bar:after){color:red}}`, which matches nothing because :is() cannot contain pseudo-elements (verified in Chrome 156 through the probe)
root_cause: Lowering nested group rules wrapped multi-selector parents in :is() without the has_pseudo_element() guard that top-level selector partitioning uses (src/rules/mod.rs ~763-770). The nesting rewrite 6c465c1 (v1.30.0) fixed it.
reviewer_lesson: Neither :is() nor & can represent pseudo-elements. Every code path that wraps selectors in :is() (nesting serialization, selector-list splitting) needs the pseudo-element guard; see #982 and PR #1156 for the remaining cases.

title: Whitespace removal before visitors run causing issues when replacing variables using Variable visitor.
trigger: minify plus a Variable visitor that returns {raw} for var() tokens separated by whitespace
actual: Up to 1.30.2: `.foo{margin:2rem3rem;padding:2rem0}` (verified); 1.31.0 and later are correct
root_cause: TokenList::parse_into dropped whitespace after delimiters, functions and var() at parse time (the last_is_delim logic), and the printer re-added it only after var/env/function tokens (write_whitespace_if_needed). Replacing a var() with a raw token therefore glued it to its neighbour. 32f1f52 keeps whitespace tokens and collapses them to a single space when printing.
reviewer_lesson: Compaction of token lists must assume visitors can replace any token. Never drop whitespace whose necessity depends on what the neighbouring tokens are; since 32f1f52, custom transformers are responsible for adding whitespace around values they replace.

title: Unable to set a different value for a single vendor
trigger: an author-written prefixed declaration next to the unprefixed one with a different value, or an unprefixed feature inside @supports not()
options: targets chrome 87, firefox 78, safari 14, edge 88 (appearance); any targets or none (backdrop-filter); safari 15 targets (@supports)
expected: each per-vendor value preserved in source order, the unprefixed declaration kept, and the meaning of @supports not() unchanged
actual: appearance: `-webkit-appearance:none;-webkit-appearance:textfield;-moz-appearance:textfield;appearance:textfield` (WebKit and FF78 now get textfield). backdrop-filter: `.c{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(8px)}`, unprefixed declaration dropped (Chrome 156 computes none; verified). @supports: `not ((-webkit-backdrop-filter: none) or (backdrop-filter: none))`, so `(-webkit-backdrop-filter:none) and (not (backdrop-filter:none))` becomes always false.
root_cause: PrefixHandler (src/properties/prefix_handler.rs:22-45) merges any declaration with an equal value or an overlapping prefix, as if -webkit-X and X were aliases. FallbackHandler (prefix_handler.rs:118-125) overwrites the stored declaration (dest[index] = ...) when a differently prefixed declaration of the same property arrives and there are no targets (or the value is compatible). @supports prefixing rewrites (prop: v) to ((-webkit-prop: v) or (prop: v)) even under not().

regression.introduced_by: 2694a18 'Handle properties with auto fallback implementation' (v1.21.0), for the backdrop-filter/filter drop
regression.evidence: local bisect: 1.20.0 keeps `backdrop-filter:blur(4px);-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(8px)`, 1.21.0..1.33.0 keep only the -webkit- one; 2694a18 added the FallbackHandler slot overwrite (prefix_handler.rs). The appearance/PrefixHandler part is older and not a regression

reviewer_lesson: Prefixed and unprefixed spellings are separate properties in engines that implement only one of them. If the author wrote both with different values, keep both in source order, and never prefix-expand a feature query inside @supports not().

title: Error while trying to run tailwind project in termux
trigger: Tailwind or Nuxt in Termux on Android arm64
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.android-arm64.node' (1.30.0 and 1.30.1)
root_cause: Android builds were added in v1.30.0 (#932), but scripts/build-npm.js did not publish the android package. #1030 (2fae1a2, v1.30.2) added it.
reviewer_lesson: A PR that adds a build target must also add it to scripts/build-npm.js and the platform loader; check the published package list, not only CI artifacts.

title: Incorrect output when using "advanced attr" with `type(<length>)` function
trigger: unminified printing of attr() with type(<length> | ...)
actual: Up to 1.30.2: `type(< length> | fit-content)`, which is invalid, so the declaration is dropped (Chrome 156: max-width 40px becomes none; verified through the probe). Minified output was fine.
root_cause: Pre-1.31 TokenList::to_css printed every Delim token (other than +/-) through Printer::delim (src/printer.rs:194-200), which adds a space after the delimiter when not minifying, giving `< length`. 32f1f52 removed that normalization (it also closed PR #1068).
reviewer_lesson: Test pretty (unminified) output as well as minified output: the printer's pretty-whitespace helpers (delim, whitespace) can insert spaces that change tokenization inside unknown syntax.

title: Issue with text-shadow property in lightningcss when using visitor
trigger: a Length visitor that converts px to rem (0px becomes 0rem), applied to text-shadow
options: minify, visitor {Length(l) { if (l.unit === 'px') return {unit: 'rem', value: l.value / 100} }}
actual: `.foo{text-shadow:0 .02rem 0 0 #0000000d}` (verified 1.18.0-1.33.0). Chrome 156 rejects a 4-length text-shadow (CSS.supports is false), so the declaration is dropped.
root_cause: TextShadow::to_css (src/properties/text.rs:1438-1445) decides whether to print blur and spread with `!= NonNegative::zero()`, which compares structurally against Px(0). A 0rem spread from the visitor is printed. It should use is_zero(). The same pattern exists in box_shadow.rs:115-119 (harmless there) and effects.rs:127/290.
reviewer_lesson: When serialization omits default components, compare semantically (is_zero()), never with == against a px zero. Visitors and unit conversions produce 0rem and 0em.

title: Nested selectors should not be transpiled when the parent selector contains pseudo elements.
trigger: a nested rule whose parent selector contains a pseudo-element (`#b::after { & {..} }` or `&:hover`), with nesting lowered
expected: the nested rule matches nothing, as in native nesting, so lowering must not produce a matching selector
actual: `#b:after{content:"x";color:red}#b:after{color:green}`. Chrome 156 shows ::after green for the output and red for the native input (verified through the probe). `.x::before { .y & {} }` gives `.y :is(.x:before)`, which also matches nothing.
root_cause: serialize_nesting (src/selector.rs:1742-1764) writes the parent selector directly when it is a single selector and & comes first, or when it is simple with no type selector, without checking has_pseudo_element(). In native nesting & means :is(parent), which cannot represent pseudo-elements.

regression.evidence: 6c465c1 (v1.30.0) enabled nesting under pseudo-elements; flattening behaviour pre-dates it

reviewer_lesson: Lowered nesting must match exactly what native nesting matches in the same modern browser. Probe with targets that force lowering and compare against the unlowered input (WPT css-nesting/nesting-basic.html), including parents with pseudo-elements and multi-selector parents (PR #1156 review).

title: "Maximum call stack size exceeded" on Docker builds
trigger: Astro/Vite build run from the container root (/) in Docker
actual: [commonjs--resolver] Maximum call stack size exceeded in Vite findNearestPackageData
root_cause: Not LightningCSS: Vite's package lookup walked the whole filesystem from /. Building from WORKDIR /app fixed it (reporter).
reviewer_lesson: None for correctness; a triage example where the stack trace never enters LightningCSS.

title: Failed to build wasm32-unknown-unknown
trigger: cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown fails in the ahash dependency (tkaitchuck/aHash #274/#276)
actual: compile error in ahash
root_cause: An upstream ahash/getrandom wasm issue. Closed in 2026-05 because lightningcss-wasm is published for current versions; no specific fix commit is cited (UNVERIFIED).
reviewer_lesson: Dependency bumps (Cargo.lock) need a wasm32 build in CI; a broken wasm build does not show up in napi tests.

title: No AST produced when media query has an invalid `calc` even with `error_recovery = true`
trigger: a media feature whose value fails to parse, e.g. (min-width: calc(baseUnit * 1)), with errorRecovery
expected: the rule is kept (per MQ4, `( <any-value> )` is <general-enclosed>, which evaluates to unknown); Chrome 156 keeps mediaText as-is (verified)
actual: 1.30.x drops the whole @media rule (no AST); 1.31.0+ keeps it with a warning. Without errorRecovery it is still a hard error 'Invalid media query', also for `(foo: bar baz)`.
root_cause: MediaCondition parsing has no <general-enclosed> branch. Before 220b390 the error propagated and error recovery dropped the rule. 220b390 (v1.31.0) wraps parse_query_condition in try_parse and falls back to MediaCondition::Unknown(TokenList), but only when error_recovery is on (src/media_query.rs, MediaCondition::parse_with_flags). The issue is still open on GitHub.
reviewer_lesson: Media, container and supports conditions have 'unknown' branches defined by the spec (<general-enclosed>, unknown @supports features). Rejecting them breaks valid stylesheets, so read the MQ4 grammar before adding a hard error and check mediaText in a browser.

title: LightningCSS fails to build on nextjs docker images using linux/arm/v6 and linux/arm/v7 architectures
trigger: next build in linux/arm/v6 and v7 Alpine (musl) Docker images
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-arm-musl.node'
root_cause: armv7 musl is not a published target (scripts/build-npm.js has armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf only). The maintainer declined the extra low-usage platform.
reviewer_lesson: Platform requests are product decisions. Check that the loader's triple naming (node/index.js) matches published package names.

title: Minification error when using nesting
trigger: minify without lowering nesting: a style rule with a nested @media that holds declarations followed by a nested rule
options: minify, no targets (or targets that support nesting)
actual: `.bar{@media (width>10em){margin:autodiv &{color:red}}}` in 1.30.0-1.30.2 (verified). Browsers read it as one invalid declaration.
root_cause: Since 6c465c1 (v1.30.0), interleaved declarations are a CssRule::NestedDeclarations, printed without `&{}` when nesting is not compiled. A minified declaration block omits its last semicolon, so the next nested rule's selector was glued onto the value. 9e04c01 writes `;` after a NestedDeclarations rule that is not last (src/rules/mod.rs, CssRuleList::to_css). Closed by a maintainer as a duplicate; fixed in 1.31.0.

regression.evidence: local bisect: 1.29.3 `&{margin:auto}div &{..}`, 1.30.0-1.30.2 `margin:autodiv &{..}`, 1.31.0 `margin:auto;div &{..}` (fix 9e04c01, closes #1089)

reviewer_lesson: Every rule type printed without braces needs a minified test in which it is followed by another rule; re-parse the output (idempotence) to catch tokens glued together.

title: Support `::before::marker` and `::after::marker` pseudo-elements.
trigger: the sub-pseudo-elements ::before::marker or ::after::marker
expected: accepted (css-pseudo-4: ::marker::before is not allowed, but ::before::marker is); Chrome 156 supports it (CSS.supports('selector(::before::marker)') is true)
actual: ERROR 'Invalid state' (1.33.0); with errorRecovery the rule is dropped
root_cause: SelectorParsingState::allows_pseudos() (selectors/parser.rs:145-148) returns false once any pseudo-element has been seen (AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT), so parse_one_simple_selector raises InvalidState (selectors/parser.rs:3030-3031). Sub-pseudo-elements are not modeled.
reviewer_lesson: Changes to pseudo-element parsing should be checked against the css-pseudo-4 list of allowed chains, and the error message ('Invalid state') should say what is wrong.

title: Pseudo-elements  Content Bug
trigger: string escape for a private-use code point in content, e.g. content: "\e6a0" (icon fonts)
options: Rust crate 1.0.0-alpha.66 with the visitor feature
expected: the escape is kept, or an equivalent string is output
actual: the raw UTF-8 character U+E6A0 is written (it looks empty in many editors); both content declarations are kept
root_cause: cssparser decodes escapes during tokenization (visit_token shows String("\u{e6a0}")), and the printer serializes strings like CSSOM serialize-a-string, which escapes only control characters, quotes and backslashes. The result is equivalent as long as the output is decoded as UTF-8. LightningCSS emits no @charset, so a page that decodes the CSS in a legacy encoding would mangle the glyph. Closed by the reporter.
reviewer_lesson: Changes to string or escape serialization need a round-trip test plus a browser check of the computed `content`. Note the UTF-8 assumption: no @charset is emitted for non-ASCII or private-use output.

title: Avoid injecting `:is` in `:not` if all the arguments are known to be supported
trigger: :not() or :is() with a selector list, and targets without selector-list support (chrome 87, firefox 78, safari 14, edge 88)
expected: specificity preserved: :not(a, block) has specificity (0,0,1), so the earlier .x rule (0,1,0) keeps winning
actual: `:not(:-webkit-any(a,block)){..}:not(:-moz-any(a,block)){..}:not(:is(a,block)){..}`. Chrome 156 still supports :-webkit-any() and gives it pseudo-class specificity, so .x turns blue (verified through the probe; also `:is(span,b)` against `.y`). The issue itself asks to skip the :is() injection when it is not needed.
root_cause: Selector lowering emits vendor :-webkit-any()/:-moz-any() alternatives for :is() (src/selector.rs, Component::Is with vendor prefixes; rules split in src/rules/mod.rs ~757-790). It assumes those alternatives do nothing in engines that support :is(). They are live in Chromium and carry pseudo-class weight instead of the weight of their most specific argument.
reviewer_lesson: Vendor alternatives of selectors are live in modern engines (Chromium parses :-webkit-any()), so their specificity must match the standard form. Test lowered selectors in a current browser against a competing rule whose specificity sits in between.

title: minifier: merge adjacent rules by using `:where`
trigger: adjacent rules with identical declarations where one selector may be unsupported (:unknown)
expected: requested: merge as :is(a, :unknown) or :where(a, :unknown), relying on forgiving selector lists
actual: not merged (correct today; verified 1.33.0, which warns about ':unknown')
root_cause: Feature request. An invalid selector invalidates the whole list, so plain merging is unsafe. Wrapping in :is() raises a's specificity to (0,1,0), and :where() lowers it to 0, so the suggestion is safe only when every merged selector has equal specificity and :is() is used.
reviewer_lesson: Rule merging must keep the is_compatible check (merge_style_rules). Any :is()/:where() wrapping must prove equal specificity, and unknown pseudo-classes must never be merged with known selectors.

title: Using lightning with bun results in incorrect architecture selection
trigger: `bun run dev` on Apple Silicon loads lightningcss-darwin-x64
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.darwin-x64.node'
root_cause: node/index.js selects the binary from process.arch. `bun run` runs the script under an x64 node (Rosetta), while `bun --bun run` uses bun's own arm64 runtime. This is an environment issue, not LightningCSS (UNVERIFIED which x64 runtime was involved).
reviewer_lesson: None for correctness. The loader trusts process.arch; arch mismatches in reports point at the runtime.

title: The conversion of calc() does not take into account the valid range of the property value
trigger: a calc() that simplifies to a negative value in a property that only accepts non-negative values
expected: width:0 (clamped) or calc() kept; css-values-4 says calc(5px - 10px), calc(-5px) and 0px are equivalent for width
actual: `width:-5px` (1.18.0-1.33.0), which is invalid outside calc(), so the declaration is dropped. Chrome 156 shows inline-size 0px becoming the container width (verified through the probe). Same for line-height and border widths.
root_cause: calc() simplification produced a plain literal with no range check. #1329 (b0939ab, master, not yet released as of v1.33.0) wraps range-restricted values in NonNegative<T> (src/values/number.rs:55), clamps calc() results in parse_with_range (src/values/length.rs:586-603, src/values/number.rs) and rejects negative literals (falling back to raw tokens). The PR says it also fixes over 600 WPT cases found with #1328. The same bug class was reported against esbuild (#4197), oxc (#17703) and csskit.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Simplifying calc() must respect the property's allowed range: clamp the top-level result or keep calc(). Probe every range-restricted property (lengths, line-height, flex-grow, border widths), and choose cases where the initial value differs from the clamped result (padding's initial 0 hides the dropped declaration).

title: Custom transformer removes whitespace
trigger: a Function visitor that replaces a custom function token followed by whitespace, e.g. margin: test("2px") 0
actual: `margin:2px0` up to 1.30.2 (verified); correct from 1.31.0. The same happened with Variable visitors.
root_cause: Same as #976: whitespace after functions was dropped when the token list was parsed (the last_is_delim logic) and re-added only after function/var tokens when printing. 32f1f52 fixed it.
reviewer_lesson: Same as #976. Visitor docs examples (design tokens) are a regression corpus worth running on every token-list change.

title: Bug: property sandwiched between nested selectors produces invalid CSS
trigger: minified nested rule, then a declaration, then another nested rule, with nesting not lowered
repro_css: .foo { &.bar { color: red; } border-color: blue; &:hover { background: green; } }
actual: `.foo{&.bar{color:red}border-color:#00f&:hover{background:green}}` in 1.30.0-1.30.2. Chrome 156 then loses border-color on .foo.bar (verified through the probe on 1.30.2).
root_cause: Same as #989: a NestedDeclarations rule printed without braces and without a trailing semicolon. Fixed by 9e04c01 (v1.31.0).

regression.evidence: Local bisect: 1.29.3 OK (declarations hoisted), 1.30.0-1.30.2 broken, 1.31.0 OK.; bisect: 1.22.1..1.29.3 hoisted decls, 1.30.1..1.30.2 missing ;, 1.31.0 fixed

reviewer_lesson: Same as #989: run a minified-output re-parse and browser check whenever rule printing changes.

title: Missing semicolon after variable defined between selectors
trigger: a custom property (or any declaration) between two nested rules, minified, nesting not lowered; also a declaration followed by a nested rule inside @media nested in a rule
repro_css: .Foo { color: red; .Bar { color: blue; } --some-var: 100%; .Baz { color: green; } }
actual: `--some-var:100%& .Baz{color:green}` in 1.30.0-1.30.2: the custom property swallows the next rule. Also `grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)&>:first-child{..}` inside a nested @media.
root_cause: Same as #989; fixed by 9e04c01 (v1.31.0). The comment from 2026-01-21 was most likely made against a playground build that predates 1.31.0 (UNVERIFIED); 1.31.0 output is correct.

regression.evidence: Local bisect: 1.29.3 OK, 1.30.0-1.30.2 broken, 1.31.0+ OK for all four repros in the thread.; bisect

title: Bug: EnvironmentVariable visitor runs _after_ throwing away whitespaces, resulting in incorrect code
trigger: an EnvironmentVariable visitor that replaces env() tokens separated by whitespace (documentation example)
options: visitor {EnvironmentVariable: {'--branding-padding': () => ({type: 'length', value: {unit: 'px', value: 20}})}}, minified or not
actual: `padding: 20px20px` even unminified, up to 1.30.2 (verified); correct from 1.31.0
root_cause: Same as #976 (whitespace after env() dropped while parsing). Fixed by 32f1f52.
reviewer_lesson: Same as #976. The docs' entry/exit visitor examples belong in the regression corpus.

title: Add support for parsing colors encoded as hex values without `#` prefix
trigger: hashless hex colors such as background-color: 333333 (the reporter's page has no doctype, so it is in quirks mode)
expected: Per css-color-4 Appendix B, <quirky-color> is valid only in quirks mode, only in background-color, border*-color and color, never in shorthands or functions. Standards-mode behavior must not change.
actual: `background-color: 333333` is kept as-is (fine). But `background: 333333` becomes `background:333333px`, a valid background-position, which resets background-color to transparent (Chrome 156 standards mode, verified through the probe).
root_cause: Request: parse hashless hex as #333. Side finding while triaging: LengthValue::parse_with_range accepts any <number-token> as px (src/values/length.rs:145-148, `// TODO: quirks mode only?`), so `width: 10`, `translate(10, 20)` and `background: 333333` turn invalid declarations into valid ones in every context (open issue #682).
reviewer_lesson: Quirks-mode syntax (hashless hex, unitless lengths) is valid only in quirks mode, only in the listed longhands, and never in shorthands or functions. Accepting it turns invalid declarations into valid ones in standards-mode pages, so reject such PRs unless they are scoped to quirks mode.

title: Add `Clone`, `Copy` & `Debug` to `PrinterOptions`
trigger: the Rust API: PrinterOptions (and DependencyOptions, PseudoClasses) lack Clone/Copy/Debug
root_cause: PrinterOptions holds `source_map: Option<&mut SourceMap>`, which blocks Clone/Copy. The proposal is cfg_attr derives when the sourcemap feature is off.
reviewer_lesson: Public-API derive changes that depend on cargo features (cfg_attr) change the API surface per feature set; build the crate with and without `sourcemap`.

title: Add support for `-webkit-text-fill-color`
trigger: -webkit-text-fill-color is an unknown property, so visitors see raw tokens and no color handling applies
expected: requested: parse it as a CssColor so visitors and color lowering apply
actual: kept as unparsed tokens. oklch() inside it is not lowered, while rgb(255 0 0 / 50%) is (verified 1.33.0)
root_cause: There is no Property::WebKitTextFillColor; unknown properties go through UnparsedProperty with partial token-level color handling.
reviewer_lesson: Turning a pass-through property into a typed one moves it under a property handler, which changes ordering, merging and fallbacks (see #1084). Test it next to color and -webkit-text-stroke, and in no-target mode.

title: Vue SFC: LightningCSS will shuffle properties order when CSS is scoped
trigger: any rule mixing handler-managed and unhandled properties (seen in Vue SFC scoped CSS via Vite)
repro_css: .logo { height: 6em; padding: 1.5em; will-change: filter; transition: filter 300ms; }
expected: the reporter expected source order to be kept
actual: `.logo{will-change:filter;height:6em;padding:1.5em;transition:filter .3s}`. A contributor called this harmless; true here, but the same mechanism breaks the cascade for #1084 (verified).
root_cause: DeclarationBlock::minify (src/declaration.rs:245-262) pushes unhandled declarations immediately, while handler-managed ones (size, padding, transition, font...) are buffered and flushed at finalize, so unknown properties move ahead. Harmful when the unknown property is a longhand of a known shorthand: transition-behavior after transition, font-variant-emoji after font (both reset; verified in Chrome 156). See #1084 and #572, both open.
reviewer_lesson: Declaration reordering is safe only between properties with no shorthand/longhand relationship. Whenever a spec adds a longhand to a shorthand (transition-behavior, font-variant-emoji, animation-range...), check that LightningCSS knows the relationship, or flush handlers before pushing an unknown property.

title: Using CSS nesting with `&.selector, .selector {}` and oklch colors causes empty selector output in iOS < v14
trigger: a nested selector list (`&.a, .a`) with a custom property that needs a color @supports fallback, with targets lacking :is() (iOS 13, IE 11)
expected: per-selector rules with @supports fallbacks, no empty selectors
actual: `@supports (color: lab(0% 0 0)) { { --color-500: lab(0% 0 0); } } ...`. Re-parsing (Vite transformer + minifier) fails with 'Invalid empty selector'. Present in 1.22.1-1.33.0 (verified).
root_cause: CssRuleList::minify (src/rules/mod.rs ~757-823) splits selectors that are incompatible with the targets into separate rules. When all of them are incompatible (nested & selectors while nesting is lowered), style.selectors becomes empty. get_supports_rules (src/context.rs:202-226) still emits an @supports rule cloning that empty list. The #1010 input surfaced in v1.30.0 because #465 made oklch(0 ...) parse as a color. Closed as a duplicate of #907 (open), although #907's own top-level `:root, :host` repro passes on 1.33.0.
reviewer_lesson: Code that builds extra rules from a rule's selectors (@supports fallbacks, :dir/:lang logical rules, dark-mode rules) must handle an empty selector list after splitting. Re-parse the output (idempotence) to catch this.

title: Animation property shorthand is expanded incorrectly
trigger: animation shorthand with N animations followed by animation-timeline with fewer values (scroll-driven animations)
repro_css: .o { animation: --a step-end, --b step-end reverse; animation-timeline: scroll(self); }
expected: the shorthand kept (or longhands with animation-duration: auto, the initial value)
actual: expanded to longhands with `animation-duration:0s,0s` (1.25.0-1.33.0). Chrome 156 computes `auto, auto` for the input and `0s, 0s` for the output (verified), which breaks the scroll-driven animation. Before 1.25.0 the output was `animation-timeline:scroll(self);animation:..`, reordered so the shorthand reset the timeline.
root_cause: AnimationHandler::finalize (src/properties/animation.rs ~900-1060) rebuilds the shorthand only when every list has the same length; otherwise it emits each longhand from the parsed values, and Animation.duration defaults to NonNegative(Time::Seconds(0.0)) (animation.rs:650), with no `auto` variant. Related open bugs on the same handler: folding animation-timeline into the shorthand (`animation:1s foo view()`, which Chrome 156 rejects; compat key AnimationTimelineShorthand from MDN, src/compat.rs:3513; #1283/#1342/#1369), and a nameless shorthand `animation:.5s ease-out both` collapsing to `animation:none`.
reviewer_lesson: Shorthand/longhand rewrites must use spec initial values (animation-duration: auto) and must not fold reset-only sub-properties (animation-timeline) into the shorthand. Check with CSS.supports() in shipping engines, because BCD keys can mislead.

title: @property with type <hue> is thrown as a error
trigger: @property with syntax "<hue>"
expected: per the maintainer, rejected: <hue> is not a supported syntax name (use <angle> | <number>)
actual: ERROR: Invalid value (1.33.0). Chrome 156 also ignores the rule (verified: --rotation has no initial value)
root_cause: Not a bug. <hue> is a value type in css-color, not a syntax component name in css-properties-values-api section 5.1. Closed as not planned.
reviewer_lesson: Same as #952: check syntax-name additions against the supported-names list and Chrome; LightningCSS added <string> in #1134, which Chrome 156 supports.

title: css modules: second nested element inside of :global is referencing global not local name of parent
trigger: CSS modules: block-form `:global { ... }` (non-function) nested in a local rule
expected: reporter wanted the block to switch to global scope
actual: 1.28.2-1.33.0: error 'Ambiguous CSS module class not supported'; 1.22.1 passed `:global` through as an unknown pseudo-class
root_cause: Only the functional `:global(...)`/`:local(...)` forms are implemented (PseudoClass::Global/Local, src/selector.rs:244-245); block form is documented as unsupported.

regression.evidence: unsupported by design (docs: css-modules.html#unsupported-features)

reviewer_lesson: CSS-modules scoping PRs must state which :global/:local forms are supported and test the unsupported ones error rather than silently pass through.

title: False positive warning when using `::highlight` pseudo element
trigger: `::highlight(name)` pseudo-element
actual: 1.28.2-1.32.0: warning "'highlight' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-element"; CSS preserved
root_cause: PseudoElement::HighlightFunction did not exist until #970 (df63db2, v1.33.0); unknown pseudo-elements become PseudoElement::Custom with a warning.

regression.evidence: never supported before v1.33.0

reviewer_lesson: New pseudo-element PRs must add an is_compatible() Feature mapping (src/selector.rs) because recognized pseudos become mergeable into selector lists when targets allow it.

title: Downleveling `margin-inline-start` changes specificity and breaks Tailwind
trigger: logical margin/padding lowered for targets without logical properties (e.g. chrome 64) followed by an equal-specificity physical override
actual: .ms-0:not(:lang(...)){margin-left:0} has specificity (0,2,0) and beats .ml-2: margin-left 0
root_cause: PropertyHandlerContext::get_additional_rules (src/context.rs:93) appends :dir()/:lang() fallbacks to the selector, raising specificity; the TODO at src/context.rs:94 acknowledges it. :where() would fix it but is only available after logical properties ship natively.

regression.evidence: same output 1.28.2-1.33.0; maintainer: no specificity-neutral lowering exists for those targets; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Any lowering that adds selector components (:lang, :dir, :not, :is) changes specificity; reviewers must test it against a later physical override of equal specificity.

title: "No such file or directory" when specifying sourcemaps for nonexistent output directory
trigger: CLI `--sourcemap` with --output-file/--output-dir in a directory that does not exist
actual: Error: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }
root_cause: src/main.rs:258 writes the .map file before fs::create_dir_all at src/main.rs:263 (#432 added create_dir_all only for the CSS file).

regression.evidence: incomplete fix of #421 via #432 (82bca74, 2023); never worked with --sourcemap

reviewer_lesson: CLI fixes that create output paths must cover every file written (CSS, .map, CSS-modules JSON) and be tested with a non-existent directory.

title: Support `::grammar-error` and `::spelling-error`
trigger: `::grammar-error` / `::spelling-error`
actual: 1.28.2-1.30.1: unknown pseudo-element warnings (CSS preserved); Next.js surfaced them as errors
root_cause: Pseudo-elements were missing from the parser list in src/selector.rs; added with Feature::GrammarError/SpellingError compat data.

regression.evidence: new feature

reviewer_lesson: Check new pseudo-elements get both parse support and a compat Feature, otherwise merging/:is() decisions treat them wrongly.

title: `margin-inline-start` disappears when using CSS nesting
trigger: logical property declared directly inside a nested @media within a style rule, with targets that lower nesting and logical properties
options: targets chrome 68 (or browserslist '> 0.2% and not dead')
expected: @media block contains the :lang() fallbacks for margin-inline-start: 2px
actual: 1.30.0-1.33.0: @media keeps only h1{color:red}; the 2px margin vanishes (1.29.3 was correct)
root_cause: Since 6c465c1 declarations inside nested group rules become CssRule::NestedDeclarations; NestedDeclarationsRule::minify (src/rules/nesting.rs:73) runs the property handlers, which move logical props into handler_context ltr/rtl, but nothing ever calls get_additional_rules/get_supports_rules for it (only the CssRule::Style branch at src/rules/mod.rs:822-841 does).

regression.introduced_by: 6c465c1 (direct push, 'Update nesting implementation for new spec', v1.30.0)
regression.evidence: 1.29.3 output contains margin-left:2px inside @media, 1.30.0+ does not (local bisect over published binaries)

reviewer_lesson: Every code path that runs DeclarationBlock::minify with the handler context must also emit (and reset) the side rules it queues; diff lowered output for declarations inside nested @media and after nested rules.

title: Cannot find module Android Arm64
trigger: npm install on android-arm64 (Termux) with lightningcss 1.30.0/1.30.1 (pinned by tailwind 4.1.x)
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.android-arm64.node'
root_cause: #932 (496f4f6, v1.30.0) added the Android build, but the triple was missing from scripts/build-npm.js so no optionalDependency was published until #1030 (2fae1a2, v1.30.2); Tailwind pinned exactly 1.30.1.
