regression.evidence: never worked before v1.30.2; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A PR adding a build target must also add it to scripts/build-npm.js triples/optionalDependencies and be verified with `npm info lightningcss optionalDependencies` after release.

title: `transform-origin` with two values sometimes gets reduced to one, even if the values differ
trigger: `transform-origin: 90% center`
actual: `90%` and `50% 60%`; equivalent per spec (one value implies center)
root_cause: Not a bug: a single <length-percentage> sets the x offset and the y offset defaults to center.

regression.evidence: output is correct

reviewer_lesson: Before accepting a 'value shortened' report, check the omitted-component defaults in the property grammar; keep a test that pins the shortening as intended.

title: Broken pseudo element selectors when output uses `:is`
trigger: CSS modules selector list of `:global(...)` items containing pseudo-elements (or with different inner specificity) and targets >= chrome 88
actual: :is(.a:before,.a:after){color:red} (invalid, browsers drop the rule); with nesting preserved: .x{:is(& .line:before,& .hl:before){...}}; also :is(.a,#b .c) raises .a to id specificity
root_cause: In CssRuleList::minify (src/rules/mod.rs, 'incompatible' block), is_compatible() returns false for PseudoClass::Global (falls into `_ => return false`), and has_pseudo_element()/specificity() do not look inside :global(), so the :is() fold guard (no pseudo-element, equal specificity) passes wrongly.

regression.evidence: same output 1.28.2-1.33.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Selector rewrites must compute pseudo-element presence and specificity through wrapper pseudo-classes (:global/:local) and through visitor round-trips, not from cached parse flags.

title: cssModules exports of css with @import's
trigger: bundle() with cssModules: exports of @import-ed files
expected: reporter wanted shared.css classes in exports
actual: exports only contain the entry file's classes; imported file classes get their own hash prefix
root_cause: By design: each file is its own CSS module, @import does not re-export.

regression.evidence: by design

reviewer_lesson: Bundler+CSS-modules changes must keep per-file hashing and export scoping stable; test exports for multi-file bundles.

title: Support `:state(<custom-ident>)` and other pseudo-classes
trigger: `:state(<custom-ident>)` pseudo-class
actual: 1.28.2-1.30.2: warning; Turbopack treated it as an error
root_cause: PseudoClass::State added in #1133 (a177fd6, v1.31.0) with Feature::StatePseudoClass.

regression.evidence: new feature

reviewer_lesson: With no targets a newly recognized pseudo becomes mergeable (`.a:state(x),.b`), so new pseudo PRs need compat data and a merge test with old targets.

title: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
trigger: CI install with npm versions affected by npm/cli#8516 (optional dependency resolution)
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
root_cause: npm optionalDependencies resolution bug (npm/cli#8516), not LightningCSS code.

regression.evidence: external npm behavior

reviewer_lesson: Packaging changes should be checked against npm's optionalDependencies + lockfile behavior across npm versions.

title: Unexpected units for CSS properties
trigger: unitless non-zero number in a <length> slot
expected: width: 100 left invalid (dropped by browsers in standards mode) or preserved verbatim
actual: width: 100px (also margin: 1 2 -> 1px 2px, flex-basis: 4 -> 4px)
root_cause: LengthValue::parse_with_range accepts Token::Number as px for every value (src/values/length.rs:145-147, `// TODO: quirks mode only?`), since ff88d98 (2021).

regression.evidence: since ff88d98, 'Parse lengths' (2021)

reviewer_lesson: Parsers must not make invalid values valid; check unitless numbers (non-zero) in every <length> slot stay invalid.

title: "Unreachable executed" error when encountering min/max with unitless numbers
trigger: min()/max()/clamp() of plain numbers in a slot parsed as Calc<Percentage> (rgb channels, opacity, filter amounts)
repro_css: b { color: rgb(max(1, 255), 0, 0); } .foo { opacity: max(1, 0.2); filter: brightness(min(1, 0.2)); }
actual: 1.28.2-1.30.2: 'internal error: entered unreachable code' at src/values/percentage.rs:30 (process abort in Node)
root_cause: Percentage::parse did `Ok(_) => unreachable!()` assuming Calc<Percentage> always reduces to a value (since 8e99bc2, 2021); number-only min/max produced Calc::Function. #1131 reduces number min/max/clamp; b0939ab (#1329, unreleased) replaced the unreachable with InvalidValue.

regression.evidence: unreachable!() present since v1.0.1

reviewer_lesson: Search new parsing code for unreachable!/unwrap/expect on user-controlled paths and fuzz math functions in every numeric slot type (number, percentage, number-or-percentage).

title: Option to ignore stripping of unknown at rules
trigger: unknown/custom at-rule (`@apply`, UnoCSS) nested in a style rule
expected: option to keep unknown at-rules verbatim
actual: no targets: kept with a warning; nesting lowered: 1.28.2-1.32.0 hoisted `@apply` to top level, 1.33.0 keeps it in place (#1233); customAtRules without `body` prints NO terminating semicolon (`@apply x semiboldwidth:5em` when minified)
root_cause: Feature request. Related bugs found: nested unknown at-rules were hoisted out of their rule when nesting was lowered (fixed by #1233, 729e03e, v1.33.0); napi custom AtRule::to_css (napi/src/at_rule_parser.rs:163-195) never writes ';' when body is None (unreported, present since db5a8ed 2024-02).

regression.evidence: feature request; semicolon bug long-standing

reviewer_lesson: Printers for statement at-rules must terminate with ';' (compare UnknownAtRule::to_css in src/rules/unknown.rs); minify+re-parse round-trip tests catch token gluing.

title: Missing declarations for 'object-fit'
trigger: visitor sees `object-fit` as an untyped custom declaration
actual: {property:'custom', value:{name:'object-fit', value:[tokens]}}
root_cause: object-fit is not in define_properties! (src/properties/mod.rs), so it parses as Property::Custom with CustomPropertyName::Unknown.

regression.evidence: never typed

reviewer_lesson: Adding a typed property changes visitor AST shape (custom -> typed), normalizes serialization and enrolls it in handler reordering; review for minimal serialization and visitor compatibility.

title: Missing declarations for 'object-position'
trigger: visitor sees `object-position` as an untyped custom declaration
actual: custom declaration with token list
root_cause: object-position missing from define_properties! (src/properties/mod.rs).

regression.evidence: never typed

reviewer_lesson: When typing a <position>-valued property, verify keyword serialization (top vs 50% 0%) is equivalent and not longer.

title: Missing declarations for 'outline-offset'
trigger: visitor sees `outline-offset` as an untyped custom declaration
actual: custom declaration with a length token
root_cause: outline-offset missing from define_properties! (src/properties/mod.rs); the outline handler only knows outline/outline-width/style/color.

regression.evidence: never typed

reviewer_lesson: Typed-property additions must be checked against the owning shorthand handler so the new longhand keeps its position relative to the shorthand.

title: logical border-radius removed when :where is present
trigger: logical property declared AFTER a nested rule in the same style rule, targets that lower nesting+logical (chrome 80)
actual: 1.30.0-1.33.0: radius declarations removed entirely (any nested rule triggers it, :where is irrelevant); @supports enhancement and light-dark() dark-mode @media rule are lost the same way; queued ltr/rtl rules can attach to the NEXT sibling nested rule (.p .d)
root_cause: Same as #1023: NestedDeclarationsRule::minify (src/rules/nesting.rs:73) fills handler_context ltr/rtl/supports/dark but never emits them; they are discarded with the child context or drained by the next CssRule::Style. Open PR #1123 merges the child context into the parent, which Devon flagged for ordering and which would hoist rules out of nested @media.

regression.introduced_by: 6c465c1 (Update nesting implementation for new spec), v1.30.0
regression.evidence: 1.29.3 emits the :lang() radius rules, 1.30.0+ emit nothing (local bisect); bisect: 1.22.1..1.29.3 emit :lang() rules, 1.30.1..master drop them

reviewer_lesson: For nesting changes, diff lowered output with declarations before/after/between nested rules and inside nested @media for every property kind that emits side rules (logical, @supports fallbacks, light-dark/color-scheme).

title: Dimension values are sometimes duplicated in the visitor
trigger: visitor reads border-radius corner values
actual: each corner is [h, v] (two identical dimensions)
root_cause: By design: corners are Size2D<T>(T, T) (src/values/size.rs:18) = horizontal + vertical radius, typed as a 2-tuple in node/ast.d.ts.

regression.evidence: by design; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: AST/serde shape changes are breaking for visitor users; check node/ast.d.ts diffs in PRs.

title: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-ia32-msvc.node'
trigger: 32-bit Node on Windows (win32-ia32)
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-ia32-msvc.node'
root_cause: No win32-ia32 build target is published; user fix: 64-bit Node.

regression.evidence: unsupported platform

reviewer_lesson: Platform matrix changes should be reflected in node/index.js error messages (unsupported vs missing install).

title: Some invalid CSS values are removed silently, while others are not
trigger: `border-image: none` (all components initial)
repro_css: .foo { border-image: none; animation-play-state: none; position: none; }
actual: border-image: (empty, invalid) in 1.28.2-1.33.0; position:none/animation-play-state:none pass through as unparsed (by design)
root_cause: BorderImage::to_css_internal (src/properties/border_image.rs:295-335) omits every component equal to its initial value with no fallback to `none` (since d7b2e50, v1.0.1). Canonical issue #1146 (open).

regression.evidence: since d7b2e50 'Handle border-image' (2021)

reviewer_lesson: Shorthand serializers that skip default components must emit a keyword when everything is default; test the all-initial value of every shorthand.

title: `transform: none` breaks when also specifying a `translate`/`scale`/`rotate`
trigger: `transform` combined with individual `translate`/`rotate`/`scale` in one rule
repro_css: .foo { transform: none; translate: none; } p { scale: 0.8; transform: rotate(10deg); }
actual: 1.28.2-1.33.0: .foo{transform:translate(0,0)} (new containing block/stacking context), p{transform:rotate(10deg)} (scale lost)
root_cause: TransformHandler individual_property! pushed translate/rotate/scale into a buffered transform list and `transform` cleared buffered individual properties (src/properties/transform.rs, since cc54e46 v1.0.1). Canonical #426; fixed on master by #1340 (40fb4ea, unreleased as of v1.33.0).

regression.evidence: since cc54e46 'Combine transform property with individual properties' (2021)

reviewer_lesson: Never merge independent properties that cascade separately (translate/rotate/scale vs transform); `none` and an identity function are not equivalent (containing block, stacking context).

title: Stripping quotes breaks font-family with double spaces
trigger: quoted font-family name containing two consecutive spaces
actual: 1.28.2-1.30.2: font-family:HW Impey  Bold (re-parses as 'HW Impey Bold', font not matched)
root_cause: FamilyName::to_css (src/properties/font.rs:414) serialized as identifiers whenever shorter; whitespace runs collapse on re-parse. #1064 quotes names containing '  '. Residual on master: a single leading/trailing space (" lead", "trail ") is still unquoted and lost (check is val.contains("  ")).

regression.evidence: since the original FamilyName serializer

reviewer_lesson: Unquoting strings into identifier sequences must round-trip exactly: test whitespace runs, leading/trailing spaces, keywords and generic names.

title: can't use css `filter:url(#svgFilterId)` inside my css
trigger: fragment-only url(#svgFilterId) with analyzeDependencies in a bundler
actual: reported as a url dependency with a placeholder; bundler warned UNRESOLVED_IMPORT '#goo'
root_cause: Url::to_css (src/values/url.rs:41-63) reports every url() as a dependency; is_absolute() (treats '#...' as document-relative) is only consulted for custom properties (src/properties/custom.rs:501). Closed by reporter.
reviewer_lesson: Dependency-reporting changes must skip document-local fragment URLs and data: URLs, matching is_absolute().

title: lightningcss no longer compiles with serde 1.0.220 or above
trigger: build with serde >= 1.0.220
actual: error[E0433]: could not find `__private` in `serde` (src/properties/mod.rs:992)
root_cause: Property/CssRule deserializers buffered through serde::__private::de::Content, which serde made private; #1062 switched to the serde-content crate.

regression.evidence: external API removal; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Dependency swaps in (de)serialization paths need JS visitor round-trip tests; #1062 shipped with none and caused #1065/#1081.

title: SyntaxError: Invalid state
trigger: structural pseudo-class after a pseudo-element (`::slotted(x):first-of-type`)
actual: Syntax Error: Invalid state (error object carries line/column)
root_cause: Correct rejection: structural pseudo-classes cannot follow a pseudo-element; message 'Invalid state' is unhelpful.

regression.evidence: correct behavior

reviewer_lesson: Selector-parser changes must keep rejecting pseudo-classes after pseudo-elements except the allowed user-action ones, and should give actionable errors.

title: Unexpected token Ident("vars") tailwindcss@4.1.13
trigger: any non-CSS-wide-keyword value for `all` (Tailwind `[all:vars]`), including the valid `all: var(--x)`
expected: invalid `all: vars` dropped/preserved like other invalid declarations; `all: var(--x)` accepted
actual: 1.25.0-1.33.0: hard error 'Unexpected token Ident("vars")' / 'Function("var")' for the whole stylesheet; 1.22.1 passed both through
root_cause: Property::parse returns `Property::All(CSSWideKeyword::parse(input)?)` with no Unparsed fallback (src/properties/mod.rs:714), added by d7aeff3 'optimize "all" property' (v1.25.0); every other known property falls back to Property::Unparsed.

regression.evidence: 1.22.1 outputs .a{all:var(--x)}, 1.25.1+ error; #752 (same bug) filed three weeks after v1.25.0

reviewer_lesson: Special-cased property parsers must keep the Unparsed fallback so var()/env() values and unknown values never become stylesheet-level errors.

title: Stylesheet visitor fails when using custom properties in 1.30.2
trigger: any JS visitor that returns a node containing var() (from: null), incl. identity StyleSheet/StyleSheetExit/Declaration/Rule visitors
actual: 1.30.2-1.33.0: 'failed to deserialize; expected an object-like struct named Specifier, found ()' (1.30.1 ok)
root_cause: #1062 replaced serde's private ContentDeserializer with serde_content; its deserialize_option only maps Value::Option(None) to None, so JS null (Value::Unit) for Option<Specifier>/Option<TokenList> goes to visit_some (napi/src/transformer.rs:759-831, src/properties/mod.rs:995/1068, src/rules/mod.rs:216-252).

regression.evidence: identity visitors succeed on 1.30.1 and fail on 1.30.2-1.33.0 (local bisect); #1062 changed no tests; bisect: 1.14.0..1.30.1 ok, 1.30.2..1.33.0 error

reviewer_lesson: Any change to serde/napi conversion must run an identity visitor (return every node unchanged) over a real-world corpus and assert byte-identical output.

title: adjacent `:has()` selectors aren't grouped
trigger: adjacent rules with identical declarations and :has() selectors under targets without :has()
actual: not merged; merged when targets support :has()
root_cause: By design: merging only happens when every selector is compatible with all targets, so an unsupported selector cannot invalidate the whole list.

regression.evidence: by design

reviewer_lesson: Merging selector lists is only safe when all members are supported by every target; changes to is_compatible() mappings directly change merge safety.

title: matching adjacent vendor specific pseudo-elements aren't flattened
trigger: two adjacent rules with the identical vendor-prefixed pseudo-element selector
expected: single rule (safe: identical selectors fail or succeed together)
actual: two rules (missed optimization)
root_cause: merge_style_rules (src/rules/mod.rs) requires is_compatible() for both rules even when selectors are equal; vendor-prefixed pseudo-elements map to `_ => return false`.
reviewer_lesson: Distinguish identical-selector merges (always safe) from selector-list merges (need compat) when reviewing merge changes.

title: Fails to parse "range syntax" in container style queries
trigger: range syntax inside a container style() query
actual: hard error 'Unexpected token Dimension'; with errorRecovery 1.28.2-1.30.2 drop the rule, 1.31.0+ keep it verbatim
root_cause: StyleQuery (src/rules/container.rs:121) only has Declaration/Property/Not/Operation; no range form and no <general-enclosed> fallback in container conditions.

regression.evidence: never supported

reviewer_lesson: Condition parsers (@media/@supports/@container) must preserve unknown queries as <general-enclosed> instead of failing the stylesheet.

title: logical properties with css variables
trigger: two-value logical shorthand with var() (padding-inline/margin-inline/inset-inline/border-inline-width) for targets without logical properties
actual: passed through unlowered (single-value longhands like padding-inline-start: var() are lowered)
root_cause: src/properties/margin_padding.rs:271-283 flushes and pushes unparsed *-inline/*-block shorthands verbatim because a var() may hold 1 or 2 values; splitting it statically is unsafe.

regression.evidence: same 1.28.2-1.33.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Lowering var()-valued shorthands into longhands is unsafe unless the substituted value's arity is known; reject PRs that duplicate var() into each longhand.

title: mixin and apply in the official document is not working
trigger: docs @mixin/@apply visitor where the mixin's style-block contains a nested rule without `&`, nesting lowered
repro_css: @mixin username { display: flex; .uid { display: flex; } } #live-users { .user { @apply username; padding: 4px 10px; } }
options: customAtRules mixin(style-block)+apply, visitor from docs, targets chrome 100
actual: 1.28.2-1.33.0: .uid{...} at top level; 1.30.2+: error from #1065 when the CSS contains var(); 1.30.0-1.30.2 (no targets): display:flex.uid{ missing ';' (fixed 9e04c01)
root_cause: A top-level @mixin body is parsed by parse_style_block with is_in_style_rule=false (napi/src/at_rule_parser.rs:116 -> src/parser.rs:1176), so `.uid` gets no implicit `&`; once spliced into .user and lowered it becomes a root selector. Preserved nesting works because browsers treat nested `.uid` as relative.

regression.evidence: lowering bug present 1.28.2-1.33.0; the 1.30.2 error is #1065

reviewer_lesson: Nested selectors must mean the same thing whether nesting is printed or lowered; test visitor-inserted rule lists under lowering targets.

title: CSS Parsing error for `:scroll-button`
trigger: `::scroll-button()` / `::scroll-marker` pseudo-elements
actual: warning 'not recognized as a valid pseudo-element' (CSS preserved); Turbopack escalated warnings to errors
root_cause: Pseudo-elements not in src/selector.rs list; unknown ones become PseudoElement::Custom (never merged, compat false).

regression.evidence: never supported

reviewer_lesson: Keep unknown pseudos as warnings with verbatim output and excluded from merging; adding them requires compat data.

title: Nested `:has(+ &)` is rewritten incorrectly (even without minification)
trigger: `&` right after a relative combinator inside :has() (`:has(+ &)`, `:has(~ &)`) with a complex parent selector, nesting lowered
actual: :has(+.container .style-previous) (matches the wrong elements), same 1.28.2-1.33.0
root_cause: serialize_selector (src/selector.rs:1464-1479) skips the implicit :scope of a relative selector but leaves first=true, so the `&` after `+`/`~` is treated as leading and serialize_nesting (src/selector.rs:1742) inlines the parent's complex selector without :is().

regression.evidence: same output 1.28.2-1.33.0

reviewer_lesson: Inlining a complex parent for `&` is only valid at the leftmost position of an absolute selector; test & inside :has() relative selectors, :not(), :is() and after combinators.

title: `@import` layer information missing in dependencies when `analyzeDependencies` is enabled
trigger: analyzeDependencies with `@import ... layer(...)`
actual: ImportDependency has url/supports/media only; the @import is removed from output, so the layer is lost entirely
root_cause: ImportDependency (src/dependencies.rs:46-57) and ImportDependency::new omit ImportRule.layer; node/index.d.ts mirrors it.

regression.evidence: field never existed

reviewer_lesson: Any rule removed from output in favor of dependency metadata must carry all of its cascade-relevant conditions (media, supports, layer).

title: Add support for the s390x architecture
trigger: install on linux-s390x (OpenShift)
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-s390x-gnu.node'
root_cause: No s390x target in scripts/build-npm.js (see also #1163 ppc64/AIX).

regression.evidence: unsupported platform

reviewer_lesson: New platform targets need CI build + publish list + node/index.js resolution changes together.

title: Report a wasm error for the deno envirnoment
trigger: lightningcss-wasm via https://esm.run in Deno 2.5
actual: LinkError: Import #21 'env' '__getrandom_v03_custom': function import requires a callable
root_cause: UNVERIFIED: since #1022 (8fa6592, v1.30.2) the wasm imports env.__getrandom_v03_custom (1.30.1 imported __getrandom_custom); the package's own index.mjs/wasm-node.mjs supply it, so the error implies a JS/wasm version skew (e.g. CDN serving <=1.30.1 JS with >=1.30.2 wasm) or a custom loader.

regression.evidence: wasm import name changed between 1.30.1 and 1.30.2 (checked published tarballs)

reviewer_lesson: Dependency bumps that change wasm imports are breaking for custom loaders; check `WebAssembly.Module.imports` diffs of the built wasm.

title: Nested rules in media query problem
trigger: minified nested @media inside a style rule with declarations followed by a nested rule
repro_css: p { color: red; @media (min-width: 560px) { color: green; &:hover { color: blue; } } }
actual: 1.30.0-1.30.2: color:green&:hover{...} (missing ';', next rule swallowed)
root_cause: NestedDeclarationsRule printing (6c465c1) omitted the trailing semicolon before a following nested rule in minified output; fixed by 9e04c01 (closes #1089). Canonical #989.

regression.evidence: 1.29.3 printed &{color:green}, 1.30.0-1.30.2 missing ';', 1.31.0 fixed (local bisect)

reviewer_lesson: Printer changes need minify+re-parse round-trip checks for declarations followed by nested rules.

title: Bug: wrapping selectors with a useless `:is()` when there is a `:global()` and a visitor
trigger: selector list with `:global(...)::before, :global(...)::after` + any JS visitor that returns style rules (even unchanged), targets that compile selectors (or include IsSelector)
options: cssModules, visitor Rule.style returning the rule, include: Features.IsSelector or targets chrome 120
actual: :is(.foo:before,.foo:after){margin:3px} (invalid)
root_cause: The Selector serde Deserialize (selectors/serialization.rs, builder.build(false,false,false)) and From<Vec<Component>> (selectors/parser.rs:996) never set HAS_PSEUDO/HAS_SLOTTED/HAS_PART, so has_pseudo_element() is false after a visitor round-trip and the :is() fold in CssRuleList::minify applies (is_compatible is false because of :global).

regression.evidence: same 1.30.1-1.33.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Never trust cached selector flags/specificity after deserialization; recompute from components or test with an identity visitor.

title: 3D Transform Values Get Minified Incorrectly
trigger: 3D transform functions that are numerically 2D (scale3d(1,1,1), rotate3d(0,0,1,a), translate3d(x,0,0))
actual: scale(1), rotate(0), translate(0,0); translateZ(0) and matrix3d kept
root_cause: Transform minification converts 3D functions with neutral z components to 2D equivalents; visually identical but drops the 3D-layer hint browsers use. Canonical #239 (open), PR #1157 closed.
reviewer_lesson: Equal matrices are not always equal rendering: treat 3D-to-2D transform rewrites as behavior changes needing maintainer sign-off.

title: Regression in `v1.30.2`? "Error: failed to deserialize; expected an object-like struct named Specifier, found ()"
trigger: customAtRules mixin/apply or @theme visitors returning declarations that contain var()
options: customAtRules theme(declaration-list) + visitor returning a style rule
actual: 1.30.2-1.33.0: failed to deserialize; expected an object-like struct named Specifier, found ()
root_cause: Same as #1065: serde_content deserialize_option treats JS null as Some(()) after #1062; anonymous @layer (Option<Vec>) fails similarly ('expected a sequence, found ()'). PR #1357 (open) normalizes Unit to Option(None).

regression.evidence: pinning 1.30.1 fixes it for every reporter; local bisect agrees; reporters pin 1.30.1

reviewer_lesson: Treat JS null and missing keys identically for every Option field; add serde round-trip tests over tests/testdata.

title: [Bug]: CSS properties sorting breaks cascade
trigger: untyped longhand (transition-behavior, animation-composition, font-kerning, font-variant-*, font-feature-settings, font-optical-sizing) written after its buffered shorthand
actual: transition-behavior:allow-discrete;transition:transition .3s (the shorthand resets it); same for font: 16px serif; font-kerning: none
root_cause: Shorthand handlers (TransitionHandler, AnimationHandler, FontHandler) buffer until flush/finalize while untyped longhands (Property::Custom unknown) are pushed to dest immediately, so they land before the shorthand that resets them. PR #1365 (open) fixes transition/animation only; the font case is #1207 (open, PR #1209 open); umbrella #572.

regression.evidence: same 1.28.2-1.33.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: For each buffered shorthand handler, list its reset-only/untyped longhands from the spec and test 'shorthand; longhand' order survives minification.

title: [BUG]Unexpected CSS minify
trigger: `backdrop-filter: X; -webkit-backdrop-filter: X` (unprefixed first; !important irrelevant); same for filter/-webkit-filter
expected: both declarations kept (Chrome/Firefox only support unprefixed)
actual: only -webkit-backdrop-filter kept: effect lost in Chrome and Firefox
root_cause: BackdropFilter/Filter use define_fallbacks! FallbackHandler (src/properties/prefix_handler.rs), which replaces the stored declaration (value and prefix) with the later one instead of OR-ing prefixes like define_prefixes! does; since 2694a18 (v1.21.0); b9624aa (v1.7.0) added the handler without the overwrite. Canonical #695 (open, PR #1259 unmerged), also #785/#1229/#1327.

regression.evidence: git show 2694a18: before it every Filter/BackdropFilter declaration was pushed; after it a later declaration overwrites the stored slot including its prefix. Same bisect as #977/#1327: 1.20.0 keeps both, 1.21.0+ keep only the prefixed one

reviewer_lesson: Prefixed and unprefixed declarations are different properties to browsers that know only one; a merge may only union prefixes, never let the later one replace the earlier.

title: Inconsistency between return type and actual value for `browserslistToTargets`
trigger: browserslistToTargets with mobile browser names (and_chr, and_ff, op_mob, ie_mob)
expected: mapped to firefox/opera/... (as Rust Browsers::from_browserslist does, src/targets.rs:112-117)
actual: returned under the original names, which the native side silently ignores (no lowering for those targets) and TS rejects
root_cause: node/browserslistToTargets.js uses BROWSER_MAPPING only to skip null entries and never renames mapped ones (since 34b67a4, 2022).
reviewer_lesson: Keep JS and Rust browserslist conversion in sync and test that unknown target keys are rejected or mapped rather than silently ignored.

title: [BUG] Stack overflow on DeclarationBlock::parse_string
trigger: calc() sum of two parenthesized sums whose terms cannot be combined, in any length/length-percentage slot
actual: infinite recursion -> stack overflow, SIGSEGV of the Node process on every release tested (1.18.0-1.33.0), even with a 1 GB stack; fuzz input reached it via font:calc(50vw - 5060px - (50vh - 50%))
root_cause: Calc::add on (Sum, Sum) (src/values/calc.rs:925) calls V::try_from(a)?.add(V::try_from(b)?); DimensionPercentage AddInternal::add -> add_recursive fails -> inherent add on (Calc, Calc) (src/values/percentage.rs:404) -> Calc::add again, never reducing. Canonical #910 (open since 2025-02); PR #1245 open, unreviewed.

regression.evidence: crashes on 1.18.0 too

reviewer_lesson: Math-simplification changes must be fuzzed with nested sums/differences of unlike units and checked for termination, in a separate process (a stack overflow kills Node).

title: [BUG] assertion failed in DeclarationBlock::parse_string (cssparser-color)
trigger: hsl()/hwb() hue that overflows f32 or is infinite
expected: hue censored/clamped per css-values-4 then converted
actual: debug: panic 'assertion failed: (0.0..=1.0).contains(&hue)' in cssparser-color hsl_to_rgb; release: NaN hue gives gray #404040
root_cause: From<HSL> for SRGB (src/values/color.rs:2799-2805) normalizes with h - 360*floor(h/360), which is NaN for infinite h, then calls cssparser_color::hsl_to_rgb whose debug_assert rejects NaN.

regression.evidence: not version-specific

reviewer_lesson: Color conversions must handle NaN/infinite channels (censor/clamp first); run tests in debug builds so debug_asserts fire.

title: serde is included when `default-features = false`
trigger: Rust crate with default-features = false
expected: no serde in the dependency tree
actual: serde pulled in via indexmap
root_cause: Cargo.toml:78 enables indexmap's serde feature unconditionally (`indexmap = { version = "2.2.6", features = ["serde"] }`, added by 4cffb66, #840) instead of through the crate's serde feature.

regression.evidence: indexmap was added in d7aeff3 without features; 4cffb66 (#840) added features = ["serde"] unconditionally

reviewer_lesson: Dependency feature flags must be gated behind the crate's own features; check `cargo tree -e features --no-default-features`.

title: All properties in animation shorthand are ignored if name is none
trigger: `animation` shorthand whose name is `none` (or omitted) but other components are set
repro_css: .foo { animation: none 1s linear infinite; } .foo--a { animation-name: a; }
expected: animation:1s linear infinite none (duration etc. kept for later animation-name overrides)
actual: animation:none (duration, easing, iteration count dropped), 1.28.2-1.33.0
root_cause: Animation::to_css (src/properties/animation.rs:662-668) has `AnimationName::None => {}` skipping every other component (originally `return Ok(())`, 7843eff, v1.0.1). Canonical #337 (open since 2022).

regression.evidence: since 7843eff 'Optimize animations' (2021); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A keyword value for one shorthand component never makes the other components irrelevant; serializers must print every non-initial component.

title: Grid template shorthand causes unreachable code with `grid-template-areas`
trigger: `grid: auto-flow / <cols>` followed by `grid-template-areas` in the same rule
repro_css: .grid-broken { display: grid; grid: auto-flow / 1fr 2fr 1fr; grid-template-areas: ". content ."; }
actual: <=1.30.2: panic `internal error: entered unreachable code` at src/properties/grid.rs:830
root_cause: GridHandler::finalize built a Grid shorthand with areas set but rows=None (auto-flow row syntax); Grid::to_css delegated to GridTemplate::to_css_with_indent, which assumes rows is a TrackList (`_ => unreachable!()`). #1132 added an auto-flow path in Grid::is_valid/to_css and emits grid-template-areas separately. Side effect still on master: the new early return in Grid::is_valid (src/properties/grid.rs:1305-1311) ignores auto_columns, so `grid-auto-columns` is silently dropped (unreported).

regression.evidence: panics in 1.19.0 and 1.25.1 as well (npm repro)

reviewer_lesson: When a fix relaxes a shorthand is_valid() check, enumerate every longhand combination it now admits and assert the serializer prints all of them; #1132 turned this panic into a silent grid-auto-columns drop.

title: Negative linear gradient radius becomes invalid
trigger: negative number with |x| < 1 whose shortest form is scientific notation (e.g. -1.42109e-14deg)
actual: <=1.32.0: linear-gradient(--1.42109e-14deg,...) (invalid, whole background dropped)
root_cause: serialize_dimension (src/values/length.rs:515-540) wrote '-' and then s.trim_start_matches("-0"), which strips nothing when s starts with "-1" (scientific notation), producing a double minus; #1192 only strips when the prefix is "-0". The same pattern is still in Percentage::to_css (src/values/percentage.rs:66-70): `-1e-7%` prints `--10e-8%` on master (#1219 open).

regression.evidence: 1.19.0 through 1.32.0 all print --1.42109e-14deg

reviewer_lesson: Hand-rolled number serializers must be tested with negative scientific-notation values and the output re-parsed; grep for sibling copies of the same trimming trick (percentage.rs still has it).

title: [BUG] `DeclarationBlock::parse_string()` takes way too much time
trigger: deeply nested math functions, especially nested atan2(): every level re-parses its arguments for up to 5 numeric types
expected: near-linear parse time or a nesting-limit error
actual: master release build: 6.1 s for the 692-byte fuzz input, 23 s for the 6-deep valid repro above, >120 s at depth 8 (`atan2(` x8 unclosed: 9.7 s)
root_cause: Calc::parse_atan2 (src/values/calc.rs:816-845) tries Calc<Length>, Calc<Percentage>, Calc<Angle>, Calc<Time> and Calc<CSSNumber> in turn via try_parse, each recursively parsing the nested arguments, so nesting is O(5^depth) and multiplies with the outer property's own alternatives. MaximumNestingDepth only guards TokenList, not Calc.

regression.evidence: maintainer dismissed as unrealistic; still reproduces on master cbeaf83

reviewer_lesson: Parser changes that add try_parse alternatives inside recursive grammars (math functions, images) need a nested-input timing test; backtracking cost multiplies per level.

title: Minification merges individual transform properties (`scale`, `rotate`, `translate`) into `transform`, breaking downstream overrides
trigger: individual transform properties (translate/rotate/scale) in the same rule as transform
expected: keep scale as its own property so .menu.open can override it
actual: <=1.33.0: .menu{transform:translate(-50%)scale(.8)}; also `scale:2;transform:translate(10px)` drops scale, `transform:scale(2);translate:10px` doubles the translation, `transform:none;translate:none` becomes `transform:translate(0,0)`
root_cause: TransformHandler (src/properties/transform.rs ~1740) appended individual properties declared after `transform` into its function list and cleared them when `transform` came later, ignoring that they cascade independently and compose in a fixed order (translate, rotate, scale, then transform). Closed as duplicate of #426; fixed on master by #1340 (unreleased), which also stops the accidental lowering of individual transforms for engines without them (Safari < 14.1, Chrome < 104).

regression.evidence: same output in 1.19.0 (`.c{transform:matrix(...)}`); tracked since #426 (2023); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Never fold a property that cascades independently into another one; test with a second rule that overrides only the folded property, and check declaration-order permutations.

title: UnexpectedToken(Function("--spacing")) with .\[--anchor-gap\:--spacing\(3\)\] { css
trigger: Tailwind v4 `--spacing()` used inside var(): `--anchor-gap: var(--spacing(3))`
actual: Err UnexpectedToken(Function("--spacing")); with error_recovery the declaration is dropped with a warning
root_cause: Input is invalid: var() needs a <custom-property-name> first argument, so Variable::parse fails and, without error_recovery, the whole stylesheet parse fails. Chrome 156 also drops the declaration at parse time (CSS.supports('--a','var(--spacing(3))') is false). The value came from a Tailwind v3 build passing a v4-only arbitrary value through.
reviewer_lesson: Before treating a 'parse error' report as a bug, check whether browsers accept the input; integrations without error_recovery turn one invalid declaration into a build failure.

title: Prefix and unprefix print-color-adjust
trigger: print-color-adjust for targets that need -webkit- (Chrome < 136, Safari < 15.4)
actual: <=1.30.2: property untyped, no prefix added or removed
root_cause: No typed property. #1102 (v1.31.0) added PrintColorAdjust with prefixes generated from autoprefixer data, but it emits `-moz-print-color-adjust` for Firefox 48-96; no Firefox shipped that name (BCD: alternative_name `color-adjust`; autoprefixer lib/hacks/print-color-adjust.js maps -moz- to color-adjust). Unreported on master.
reviewer_lesson: For prefix data taken from autoprefixer, also port its lib/hacks renames and check MDN BCD alternative_name; a prefix that never shipped is dead output that hides a missing fallback.

title: Keyframe including invalid code is removed while browsers ignore the invalid code part
trigger: any parse error inside a keyframe block: a nested @supports/@media or an invalid declaration
options: any; happens without error_recovery and without any warning
expected: @keyframes k{0%{opacity:.25}to{opacity:1}} (Chrome 156 keeps the declarations and ignores the at-rule), ideally with a warning
actual: @keyframes k{to{opacity:1}} (whole 0% keyframe silently removed); Tailwind output became `@keyframes name {}`
root_cause: KeyframeListParser::parse_block (src/rules/keyframes.rs:403-415) parses the block with ParserOptions::default() (error_recovery off, no warnings sink), so one bad item fails the keyframe, and src/parser.rs:880-884 collects keyframes with filter_map(Result::ok), discarding the error silently.

regression.evidence: same output in 1.19.0

reviewer_lesson: Grep for nested parsers built with ParserOptions::default() and for filter_map(Result::ok) over rule results: they silently delete content and ignore the caller's error_recovery and warnings.

title: Stylesheet visitor with ignored rule causes `missing field 'value'` error
trigger: JS StyleSheet/StyleSheetExit visitor returning the stylesheet when the bundler has replaced rules with {type:'ignored'}
options: bundle()/bundleAsync() of a file with @import, visitor: { StyleSheetExit(sheet) { return sheet } }
actual: Error: missing field `value` (1.25.1-1.33.0 and master)
root_cause: CssRule::Ignored is serialized as {type:'ignored'} with no value (serde tag/content on a unit variant), but the hand-written CssRule Deserialize (src/rules/mod.rs:~226-246, since #363) requires `value` before dispatching on the type, so 'ignored' can never be deserialized. Exposed once the StyleSheet visitor (bda77f3, v1.23.0) let users return whole sheets.

regression.evidence: latent since the StyleSheet visitor landed (bda77f3, v1.23.0); 1.19-1.22 never call StyleSheetExit in bundle(); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Every AST variant must survive a serialize -> deserialize round trip through the JS visitor; test returning each visited node unchanged, including bundler-produced placeholder rules.

title: Bug: Incorrect Transformation of Range Context Media Queries (Negation Error)
trigger: range syntax lowered with include: MediaRangeSyntax but not MediaIntervalSyntax (Next 16 defaults), combined with and/or
options: include: Features.MediaRangeSyntax (128), targets that support interval syntax
actual: <=1.30.2: @media not (min-width:768px) and (min-width:600px) (invalid grammar -> `not all`, never matches)
root_cause: QueryFeature::needs_parens (src/media_query.rs) returned false early when MediaIntervalSyntax was not being compiled, skipping the parentheses that the `<` -> `not (min-...)` range rewrite needs; #1114 moved the compat checks into the Interval and Range arms.

regression.evidence: latent; exposed when Next 16 changed default targets so MediaIntervalSyntax was no longer included (vercel/next.js#84401)

reviewer_lesson: Test lowering under include/exclude flag combinations, not only browser targets: integrators toggle features independently that targets always toggle together.

title: Add SVG 1.1 variants of presentation attribute values
trigger: camel-cased SVG keywords: geometricPrecision, crispEdges, linearRGB
repro_css: .a { text-rendering: geometricPrecision; shape-rendering: crispEdges; color-interpolation: linearRGB; }
actual: <=1.30.2: typed parse failed (case-sensitive), value kept as unparsed tokens
root_cause: The derived keyword parsers for these SVG enums matched case-sensitively; #1108 added #[css(case = lower)] (src/properties/svg.rs) so they parse ASCII case-insensitively (and now print lowercase, e.g. geometricprecision). color-rendering optimizeQuality and image-rendering optimizeSpeed are still untyped.
reviewer_lesson: Keyword enums must parse ASCII case-insensitively; when a value moves from unparsed to typed, check the new printed form and the AST shape visitors see.

title: Bug: Incorrect conversion of legacy -webkit-linear-gradient direction keywords
trigger: an existing -webkit-/-moz-/-o-linear-gradient with a side keyword or a 0/180deg angle
options: minify (Rspack LightningCssMinimizerRspackPlugin); some cases also without minify
actual: -webkit-linear-gradient(270deg,red,#00f) (paints top to bottom; Chrome 156 pixel check). (top,red,blue) minifies to (#00f,red) (reversed); (bottom,...) and (180deg,...) lose their direction even without minify
root_cause: LinearGradient::to_css and LineDirection::to_css (src/values/gradient.rs:268-300, 501-542) apply standard-syntax rules to prefixed gradients: omitting 180deg/bottom as the default, flipping stops for 0deg/top, and mapping left->270deg when minifying. In the 2011 prefixed syntax the keyword names the start side, 0deg points right and the default is top. #936 fixed only standard->prefixed conversion (convert_to_legacy_direction). The test at src/lib.rs:14210-14212 codifies the wrong `bottom` output.

regression.evidence: identical output in 1.19.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Vendor-prefixed values have their own grammar and semantics; any optimization on them needs a rendering (pixel) check, and existing expectations may codify wrong output.

title: Bug: `!important` rules are ignored unless directly next to each other
trigger: the same selector with the same property set twice, non-adjacent, where one copy is !important
repro_css: h1 { color: green !important; } body { margin: 0; } h1 { color: red; }
actual: 1.20.0-1.33.0: body{margin:0}h1{color:red} (the !important rule is removed)
root_cause: Duplicate-rule removal keyed on StyleRule::hash_key/is_duplicate (src/rules/style.rs:149-171), which compared selectors and property ids but not importance, so the earlier !important rule looked fully overridden; 93b9e66 adds importance to both.

regression.evidence: reporter bisected 1.19.0 ok / 1.20.0 broken; reproduced with npm 1.19.0 vs 1.20.0; reporter + bisect: 1.19.0 ok, 1.20.0..1.33.0 dropped

reviewer_lesson: A dedupe or merge key must include everything that affects cascade precedence (importance, layer, scope, conditional context) and be tested with an unrelated rule between the duplicates.

title: color-mix on custom properties transpiled when it shouldn't be
trigger: Tailwind @utility containing color-mix(in oklab, var(--a), var(--b) N%)
actual: every color-mix replaced by the first color (inside Tailwind)
root_cause: Tailwind's own color-mix() polyfill (tailwindcss#17555) replaced it before LightningCSS ran; the reporter could not reproduce in the LightningCSS playground and closed the issue (tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#19445).
reviewer_lesson: Reproduce with LightningCSS alone before attributing Tailwind output to it; Tailwind runs its own transforms first.

title: Tests rely on deprecated `assert_cmd::cargo_bin` which will break on future Cargo versions
trigger: cargo test with a non-default build dir (CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR)
expected: CLI integration tests locate the binary
actual: assert_cmd::Command::cargo_bin relies on cargo's target-dir layout and will break
root_cause: tests/cli_integration_tests.rs:160-321 call the deprecated Command::cargo_bin("lightningcss"); replacement is the assert_cmd::cargo_bin! macro. Still present on master.
reviewer_lesson: CI should exercise non-default cargo build directories so layout assumptions surface before cargo changes ship.

title: Minification of animation-timeline in animation shorthand
trigger: animation shorthand plus animation-timeline, with no targets or Chrome >= 115 targets
repro_css: .foo { animation: alternate fade-in ease-in-out both; animation-range: 10svh 50svh; animation-timeline: scroll(block root); }
expected: animation:...;animation-timeline:scroll(root);animation-range:... (timeline stays a longhand after the shorthand)
actual: animation:ease-in-out alternate both fade-in scroll(root) — Chrome 156 rejects the whole declaration (CSS.supports false), so the animation is lost
root_cause: Feature::AnimationTimelineShorthand (src/compat.rs:3513) is generated from BCD css.properties.animation.animation-timeline_included, whose Chrome 115 entry is partial_implementation with the note 'reset-only'; scripts/build-prefixes.js:337 does not filter partial_implementation for this key (it does for statePseudoClass), so AnimationHandler folds the timeline into the shorthand. Issue was closed after the maintainer's 'set targets' reply; the Chrome follow-up (xPaw) is unaddressed.

regression.introduced_by: f4408c7 'Implement animation-timeline property and add to animation shorthand' (v1.25.0)
regression.evidence: 1.22.0 kept animation-timeline as a longhand (but moved the shorthand after it, resetting it); 1.25.1+ fold scroll(root) into the shorthand

reviewer_lesson: When compat data comes from MDN BCD, honour partial_implementation/notes (reset-only, prefixed, alternative_name) and check folded shorthands with CSS.supports in the target engine.

title: Minify
trigger: empty issue titled 'Minify'
root_cause: Opened by accident and closed within seconds as not planned; the author filed #1117 (light-dark(x, x)) a minute later.
reviewer_lesson: None (empty report).

title: Minify light-dark(x, x) to x
trigger: light-dark() with two equal colors
actual: <=1.32.0: light-dark(#fff,#fff)
root_cause: No simplification existed; #1183 (v1.33.0) returns the light color from parse_color_function (src/values/color.rs) when both arguments compare equal. It runs at parse time, so visitors and non-minified output also see the collapsed color. A reviewer asked for more equivalence tests (rgb/hsl spellings) after merge.
reviewer_lesson: Parse-time simplifications change the AST visitors see; ensure equality is on resolved values and that var()-containing arguments are never collapsed.

title: Clarify and improve semantics of `StyleSheet::minify` and `StyleSheet::to_css`
trigger: Rust users calling StyleSheet::to_css without StyleSheet::minify first
options: Rust API (cargo-leptos dev mode, Turbopack before vercel/next.js#77313)
expected: to_css alone produces correct output, or the API makes the required step explicit
actual: transforms that minify() performs (e.g. light-dark() / color-scheme variable fallbacks) are missing, breaking output (cargo-leptos#622)
root_cause: minify() is also the transform/lowering pass ('bad name, it should really be called transform' - maintainer in #935); nothing enforces calling it before to_css. Open API/docs proposal.
reviewer_lesson: For Rust API changes, check implicit call-order requirements between minify() and to_css() and document or enforce them.

title: Incorrect output with `attr(foo %)`
trigger: attr() with a % unit: attr(data-width %)
actual: <=1.30.2: attr(data-width%)
root_cause: The token-list printer dropped whitespace before delimiters. For % this is token-equivalent (ident + delim; Chrome 156 accepts both), and ident units kept their space, so behavior did not change. 32f1f52 (v1.31.0) stopped removing whitespace; #1127 added tests.
reviewer_lesson: Separate cosmetic serialization changes from semantic ones by re-tokenizing the output: whitespace before a delimiter is insignificant, between two identifiers it is significant.

title: Unexpected token Function("scroll-state")
trigger: @container <name> scroll-state(...) query
repro_css: .parent { container-type: scroll-state; container-name: my-container; & .child { @container my-container scroll-state(stuck: top) { opacity: 0; } } }
actual: <=1.30.2: Unexpected token Function("scroll-state")
root_cause: The container query parser only knew size features and style(); 220b390 (v1.31.0) added scroll-state() (QueryConditionFlags::ALLOW_SCROLL_STATE) and also made unknown media/container conditions recoverable under error_recovery (MediaCondition::Unknown).
reviewer_lesson: New query functions should come with error-recovery and empty-input tests; this commit also introduced the #1137 regression.

title: [BUG] unreachable code in percentage.rs  [ input background:(lineal-gradient(rgba(max(1,2)))); ]
trigger: number-only math function where a percentage is parsed (rgba() channel inside an unknown function token list)
expected: no panic (unparsed value or parse error)
actual: <=1.30.2: panic `entered unreachable code` at src/values/percentage.rs:30
root_cause: Percentage::parse matched the Calc::<Percentage>::parse result with `Ok(_) => unreachable!()` ('percentages always compute to a value'), but number-only min()/max()/clamp() return Calc::Number. #1131 (v1.31.0) fixed these shapes; percentage-typed sign()/abs()/mod() still panicked in 1.33.0 (#1312) until b0939ab (#1329, master) replaced the unreachable with an InvalidValue error.
reviewer_lesson: Treat every unreachable!()/unwrap() on a parse path as a crash; fuzz mixed-type math in every numeric slot (colors, opacity, gradients).

title: `grid-template` shorthand parsing error
trigger: grid-template-rows lists more tracks than grid-template-areas has rows, and the longhands are folded into grid-template
repro_css: .grid { grid-template-areas: "a a a" "b c c"; grid-template-rows: 30px 60px 100px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; }
actual: <=1.30.2: grid-template:"a a a"30px"b c c"60px/1fr 1fr 1fr (100px row lost)
root_cause: GridTemplate::to_css_with_indent walks the area strings and pairs each with a row size, so surplus row tracks were never printed. #1132 pads the areas with '. . .' rows; layout is identical but the computed grid-template-areas string changes (Chrome 156: "a a a" "b c c" ". . .").

regression.evidence: same output in 1.19.0

reviewer_lesson: Serializers that zip two lists must handle unequal lengths; when a shorthand cannot express the input exactly, prefer keeping longhands over padding that changes computed values.

title: [BUG] Scroll State Container Queries Completely Fail
trigger: @container scroll-state(scrollable: x)
actual: <=1.30.2: Unexpected token Function("scroll-state")
root_cause: Same as #1128: no scroll-state() support until 220b390 (v1.31.0); maintainer closed as already fixed, release pending.
reviewer_lesson: Unknown functions in conditional preludes are hard errors without error_recovery even though <general-enclosed> makes them valid; new CSS features become build failures for every integrator.

title: [minify] Do not convert `rotate: 0deg` to `rotate: none`
trigger: rotate: 0deg (also -0deg, z 0deg)
actual: <=1.31.1: rotate:none (no stacking context or containing block; rule merging then also combined it with real `none` rules)
root_cause: Rotate serialization treated a zero angle as the identity keyword none; the spec says rotate serializes as none only if none was specified. #1147 (v1.32.0) rewrote Rotate::to_css (src/properties/transform.rs) to keep 0deg and to normalize z-axis vectors (0 0 1, 0 0 2, 0 0 -1) to a bare angle, matching WPT rotate-parsing-valid.html.
reviewer_lesson: Identity values are not equivalent to none when they create stacking contexts or containing blocks (transform, translate, rotate, scale, filter, perspective, will-change).

title: `error_recovery: true` incorrectly reports `EndOfInput` parse error on 1.31.0
trigger: @import without a media list while error_recovery is true
actual: 1.31.0: warning `EndOfInput` at 1:30 and output `@import "./actual-styles.css" ;`
root_cause: 220b390 wrapped MediaCondition::parse_with_options in error recovery (warn and keep MediaCondition::Unknown(TokenList)); MediaList::parse on an exhausted prelude therefore recorded EndOfInput as a warning and kept an empty Unknown condition. f3666d6 returns an empty MediaList when the input is exhausted (src/media_query.rs:59-61).

regression.evidence: 1.30.2 clean; 1.31.0 warns and prints the extra space; 1.31.1 (6993d9f, untagged) fixed

reviewer_lesson: Error-recovery branches need tests on empty/exhausted input and must not change output or warnings for valid CSS; diff warnings as well as output between base and head.

title: Supported desugaring of multi-level nested at-rules
trigger: @media nested in @media inside a style rule, lowered for targets without nesting
repro_css: .test { display: grid; @media (orientation: landscape) { grid-auto-flow: column; @media (width >= 1px) { max-inline-size: 1024px; } } }
actual: nested @media kept inside @media
root_cause: By design: only style-rule nesting is lowered; nested conditional group rules have been supported by engines since about 2013, and the maintainer declined the complexity of merging queries.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Distinguish nesting style rules (needs lowering) from nesting conditional rules (old, widely supported) before judging lowering output.

title: FamilyName appears to be an opaque value.
trigger: Rust users inspecting or constructing FontFamily::FamilyName
expected: public access to the family name string
actual: FamilyName is opaque; only Parse/serde can create or read it
root_cause: #840 (4cffb66, v1.29.0) changed FontFamily::FamilyName(CowArcStr) to FontFamily::FamilyName(FamilyName) with `pub struct FamilyName<'i>(CowArcStr<'i>)` whose field is private and has no constructor or accessor (src/properties/font.rs:383).

regression.evidence: before #840 the variant carried a public CowArcStr

reviewer_lesson: For public Rust types, newtypes need pub fields or From/AsRef/as_str APIs; changing an enum payload type is a semver-visible break.

title: Font-stretch percentages are not supported in Chrome 143.0.7499.193 in the font shorthand rule
trigger: font shorthand containing a font-stretch keyword when minifying (or a percentage font-stretch longhand folded into font)
actual: font:400 75% 36px/38px TeX Gyre Heros (invalid per css-fonts-4; Chrome 156 drops the declaration, font-size falls back to 16px)
root_cause: FontStretch::to_css (src/properties/font.rs:264-272) prints a percentage whenever dest.minify, without knowing it is inside the font shorthand (which only accepts <font-width-css3> keywords) and without checking FontStretchPercentage for the targets (chrome 60 also gets 75%). FontHandler additionally folds a percentage longhand (font-stretch:100%) into font even without minify.

regression.evidence: same output in 1.19.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A value's valid serialization depends on context: when a longhand value is printed inside a shorthand, check the shorthand's (often narrower) sub-grammar and the targets' support for the shorter form.

title: Additional whitespace being inserted in `var(--foo,)` and `env(--foo,)`
trigger: var() or env() with an empty fallback: var(--foo, )
actual: 1.31.0-1.31.1: var(--bar,  ), one more space on every pass (broke Tailwind tests)
root_cause: 32f1f52 began preserving whitespace tokens in token lists, but Variable/EnvironmentVariable::to_css still wrote the comma with dest.delim(',', false), which adds its own space when not minifying; #1142 writes ',' and adds a space only if the fallback does not already start with whitespace (src/properties/custom.rs).

regression.introduced_by: 32f1f52 'Do not remove whitespace in token lists' (v1.31.0)
regression.evidence: 1.30.2 ok; 1.31.0 and 1.31.1 double the space; 1.32.0 fixed; reporter (Tailwind)

reviewer_lesson: Run every serializer change twice (idempotency) and on Tailwind output; whitespace-handling changes interact with every place that adds its own separators.

title: :dir(ltr) / :dir(rtl) isn't supported?
trigger: :dir() written after a pseudo-element (.x:before:dir(rtl))
actual: selector error, rule dropped
root_cause: Invalid per Selectors 4: only specific pseudo-classes may follow a pseudo-element. Chrome 156 also rejects it (CSS.supports('selector(.x:before:dir(rtl))') false); the fix is .x:dir(rtl)::before.
reviewer_lesson: Check browser acceptance (CSS.supports('selector(...)')) before treating a selector rejection as a bug.

title: The border-image shorthand was incorrectly parsed as an empty value
trigger: border-image (or mask-border, -webkit-mask-box-image) whose components are all initial, e.g. `border-image: none`
actual: border-image: (empty; browsers drop it, so an earlier border-image survives); `none 30` prints ` 30`
root_cause: BorderImage::to_css_internal (src/properties/border_image.rs:295-334) omits every component equal to its initial value and prints nothing when all are initial. The same serializer uses border-image initials for mask-border/-webkit-mask-box-image (initial slice 0, width auto) and drops the explicit slice of -webkit-border-image (which implies fill), all unreported. Open fix PR #1336; #1052 was closed as its duplicate.

regression.evidence: same output in 1.19.0

reviewer_lesson: For every shorthand, test the all-initial value and each single non-initial component; 'omit defaults' logic must use the defaults of the property actually being printed.

title: Inconsistent `url()` locations
trigger: url() in list-style-image or border-image-source with analyzeDependencies
repro_css: body { cursor          : url(missing1.png); list-style-image: url(missing2.png); background-image: url(missing3.png); }
expected: dependency loc column 25 for every url (start of the URL text)
actual: list-style-image (and border-image-source) report one column less; image-set string URLs are off by 4
root_cause: Url::parse (src/values/url.rs:33-38) captures current_source_location() before expect_url() skips leading whitespace; properties whose parser has not consumed the whitespace yet record the whitespace position (+4 for 'url('). Same in 1.19.0. Open PR #1150.

regression.evidence: same columns in 1.19.0

reviewer_lesson: Code that records source positions must skip whitespace first; test locations for each property path that can contain the token.

title: Minification regression in 1.31: whitespace after comma not removed
trigger: invalid value kept as a token list: translate3d(0px, 0px) (needs 3 arguments)
actual: 1.31.0+: translate3d(0px, 0px)
root_cause: 32f1f52 preserves whitespace in unparsed token lists; the value is invalid so it stays unparsed. Size-only; the general case (calc() with var(), Tailwind's calc(var(--spacing) * N)) is tracked in #1378 (open, ~1% raw size).

regression.introduced_by: 32f1f52 'Do not remove whitespace in token lists' (v1.31.0)
regression.evidence: size-only change; closed as not planned because the input is invalid; bisect

reviewer_lesson: Measure minified size on real corpora (Tailwind) when changing token-list printing; correctness fixes can be large size regressions.

title: Improve support for the text-decoration shorthand
trigger: text-decoration shorthand with style/color/thickness for engines that only support the CSS 2 shorthand
expected: a `text-decoration: underline` fallback before the full shorthand (postcss-text-decoration-shorthand)
actual: text-decoration:underline dotted red;text-decoration-thickness:2px (shorthand invalid in those engines)
root_cause: No compat feature or fallback for the CSS Text Decoration 3 shorthand form.
reviewer_lesson: When a shorthand gains new components, check older engines that only parse the old grammar; the whole declaration is dropped there.

title: Can not use relative URLs in custom properties
trigger: relative url() inside a custom property with analyzeDependencies on (Vite hard-codes it)
actual: error: Ambiguous url() in custom property. Use an absolute URL instead
root_cause: By design: TokenList::to_css (src/properties/custom.rs) rejects relative URLs in custom properties when collecting dependencies because var() resolves URLs where it is used; the option is forced by Vite (fixed by the reporter outside LightningCSS).
reviewer_lesson: Check which options the integrator forces (Vite: analyzeDependencies) before treating an error as a LightningCSS default.

title: Crash: stack overflow / integer overflow on deeply nested CSS (found via fuzzing)
trigger: pathologically deep nesting of style rules
options: StyleSheet::parse + to_css(PrinterOptions::default()); debug or overflow-checks builds
expected: an error instead of a panic or abort
actual: debug: `attempt to add with overflow` at src/printer.rs:219 after 128 levels (u8 indent); release: indentation wraps silently; ~10,000 levels: stack overflow abort on master
root_cause: Printer.indent is a u8 (src/printer.rs:76) incremented without checks (indent/indent_by), StyleRule::to_css_base and CssRuleList::to_css recurse without a depth limit, and the rule parser has no nesting limit (only TokenList has MaximumNestingDepth).
reviewer_lesson: Fuzz printers as well as parsers; bound recursion depth and avoid narrow integer types for depth or indentation.

title: :is() incorrectly added to the output when targeting older browsers
trigger: nesting lowering where the parent is complex or a list and & is not first, for targets without :is()
expected: a selector the target can parse, or a warning
actual: .baz :is(.foo .bar){margin-top:0} — rule dropped by engines without :is()
root_cause: serialize_nesting (src/selector.rs:1742-1764) writes :is() whenever the parent is not a single simple selector, without checking Feature::IsSelector for the targets. :-webkit-any() cannot hold complex selectors (Chrome 156: CSS.supports('selector(:-webkit-any(.a .b))') false), so no exact lowering exists; expansion changes specificity and matching (#202, #312, #1324, #1345).

regression.evidence: long-standing (#202 from 2022); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A lowering must re-check compat of every construct it introduces (here :is()) against the same targets, and warn when no exact lowering exists.

title: Support display-p3-linear color space
trigger: color(display-p3-linear ...) and the display-p3-linear interpolation space
actual: kept as an unparsed value, no fallback
root_cause: The predefined color-space list (src/values/color.rs) lacks display-p3-linear, added to CSS Color 4.
reviewer_lesson: When adding a color space, add it to parsing, conversion, interpolation spaces (color-mix, gradients) and fallback generation together.

title: Don't map oklab/oklch lightness of 0/100% to black/white
trigger: fallback generation for lab/lch/oklab/oklch colors whose OKLCH lightness is >= 100% (or <= 0%)
options: targets chrome 100 (any target that needs an sRGB fallback)
actual: background-color:#fff fallback
root_cause: map_gamut (src/values/color.rs:~3325-3350) follows the CSS Color 4 gamut-mapping pseudo-code, which returns white when OKLCH L >= 100%; lch(100% 110 60) has OKLCH L = 1.0106. Chrome clips instead. Spec-conformant; the request is to match engine rendering (w3c/csswg-drafts#8794).
reviewer_lesson: Gamut-mapping changes move many fallback colors at once (see #1323 on master); compare against both the spec pseudo-code and actual engine rendering.

title: Add support to ppc64/s390 and IBM AIX architectures
trigger: installing the npm package on linux ppc64le, s390x or AIX
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-ppc64-gnu.node' (Node.js CI)
root_cause: The release workflow and scripts/build-npm.js publish no ppc64le/s390x packages; node/index.js resolves lightningcss-<platform>-<arch>-<abi>. PR #1217 (open) cross-compiles both; s390x is big-endian and untested.
reviewer_lesson: New release targets need the binding's tests run on the target (big-endian s390x especially).

title: bundleAsync() randomly silently crashes
trigger: bundleAsync() on Windows (about 1 in 10 runs), no reproduction
options: bundleAsync({minify: true, sourceMap: true, analyzeDependencies: false}), Windows 11, Dev Drive
actual: node exits silently (code 1, Vite code 5); bundle() works
reviewer_lesson: Changes to napi async paths need repeated-run stress tests; release builds use panic='abort' (Cargo.toml:129), so any panic on the rayon worker kills the process.

title: Support Scoped Declarations
trigger: declarations directly inside @scope (scoped declarations)
expected: declarations kept (they apply as :where(:scope); Chrome 156 parses them as CSSNestedDeclarations)
actual: parse error; with error_recovery `@scope(.foo){}` and any following nested rule is lost
root_cause: NestedRuleParser::parse_nested (src/parser.rs:473-520) only accepts declarations when allow_declarations || is_in_style_rule; a top-level @scope is parsed with allow_declarations=false (src/parser.rs:191), so `border: ...; .a {...}` is consumed as one qualified-rule prelude.
reviewer_lesson: For rules whose body is a style block, check top-level declarations are accepted where the spec allows them; error recovery must not swallow sibling rules.

title: `clamp()` causes a panic
trigger: number-only clamp() inside rgb()
actual: <=1.30.2: panic at src/values/percentage.rs:30
root_cause: Same unreachable!() as #1129; fixed by #1131 (v1.31.0). The input comes from WPT css-values/clamp-color-computed.html.
reviewer_lesson: WPT computed-value tests are a ready-made corpus for math in every slot; run them through the parser before releasing math changes.

title: Generated sourcemap gives invalid references
trigger: bundle()/bundleAsync() with sourceMap: true over several @imported files loaded in parallel
options: bundle or bundleAsync, sourceMap: true (minify on or off)
expected: each mapping points to the file that contains the rule
actual: reproduced: in 8-20% of runs (1.25.1, 1.30.2, 1.33.0) rules from items.css map to more.css and vice versa; the order of map.sources changes between runs
root_cause: Bundler::load_file assigns a stylesheet's source_index at registration (src/bundler.rs:413-414, stylesheets.len()) but adds the file to the shared SourceMap in parse-completion order (src/bundler.rs:463-465, add_source, its returned index ignored); with rayon loading imports in parallel the orders diverge, and the printer writes mappings with loc.source_index (src/printer.rs:252) against the map's sources list.

regression.introduced_by: bfa8b8c 'Use inline source maps during bundling' (v1.15.0) introduced the add_source call (UNVERIFIED that earlier versions were correct)
regression.evidence: nondeterministic; reproduced on every tested version; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Run bundler outputs (code and maps) N times and diff them; any index shared by two registries must be assigned in one place under one lock.

title: Support `<radial-extent>`
trigger: circle()/ellipse() radii closest-corner or farthest-corner
actual: kept as unparsed tokens
root_cause: ShapeRadius (src/values/shape.rs:71-78) only has closest-side and farthest-side; css-shapes now uses <radial-size>/<radial-extent>.
reviewer_lesson: Share grammar types across specs (gradients and shapes both use <radial-extent>) so one fix covers both.

title: Improving CSS Shapes Module Level 1
trigger: basic shapes beyond the current shape.rs (newer css-shapes-1 grammar)
root_cause: src/values/shape.rs predates the current css-shapes-1 draft (e.g. <radial-size>, shape(), rect()/xywh() details); unknown forms fall back to unparsed tokens.
reviewer_lesson: When upgrading a value type from unparsed to typed, run the WPT parsing corpus for it to catch newly rejected valid values.

title: [Question] How to allow functions to be the prelude of custom at-rule?
trigger: @-moz-document domain("...") (userstyles) with customAtRules
expected: handled as a custom or unknown at-rule
actual: Unexpected token Function("domain") (error recovery drops the rule)
root_cause: The built-in -moz-document prelude parser (src/parser.rs:641-660) only accepts url-prefix() and runs before parse_custom_at_rule_prelude, so the name cannot be overridden; custom at-rule SyntaxString preludes cannot describe functions (an unknown name like @foo-document keeps its token prelude).
reviewer_lesson: Built-in support for an at-rule name shadows unknown and custom at-rule handling; keep a fallback to a token prelude when the built-in grammar does not match.

title: Calculation error when using transparent in relative colors
trigger: relative color with omitted alpha from a transparent or translucent origin
repro_css: .foo { color: rgb(from transparent r g b); }
actual: 1.33.0: #000; also rgb(from rgb(255 0 0 / .5) r g b) -> red
root_cause: Relative color parsing defaulted the omitted alpha to 1 instead of the origin color's alpha; a862e39 (#1343, master, unreleased) keeps the origin alpha. The issue is still open.
reviewer_lesson: Relative-color tests need translucent origins; check every channel default against the current css-color-5 text, which has changed over time.

title: Without targets nesting produces invalid CSS
trigger: nested relative selectors with no targets
actual: .foo,.faa{& .bar{&>h3{color:green}}}
root_cause: Without targets LightningCSS assumes every feature is supported, keeps nesting and prints explicit & (#777). The output is valid: Chrome 156 computes the same color for input and output, so the reported breakage did not reproduce; older engines need targets.

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: 'No targets' means latest engines; kept modern syntax is not a bug unless the targets say it is unsupported.

title: Support container-type: anchored and @container anchored()
trigger: container-type: anchored and @container anchored(fallback: ...)
actual: Unexpected token Function("anchored"), the whole build fails; with error_recovery it is preserved with a warning (since 220b390)
root_cause: The container query parser has no anchored() feature, and without error_recovery any unknown query function is a hard error even though <general-enclosed> makes it syntactically valid. PR #1218 (open) adds typed support; #1228 closed as duplicate.
reviewer_lesson: Preserve <general-enclosed> in media and container queries even without error_recovery; otherwise every new query function is a build break for integrators.

title: CSS Parsing error for ::scroll-marker
trigger: css-overflow-5 ::scroll-marker / ::scroll-marker-group pseudo-elements and scroll-marker-group property
actual: warning "'scroll-marker' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-element"; rule preserved as .carousel>::scroll-marker (equivalent); Turbopack turns the warning into a build error
root_cause: No ::scroll-marker variants in PseudoElement (src/selector.rs); unknown pseudo-elements become a warning and set AFTER_UNKNOWN_PSEUDO_ELEMENT (selectors/parser.rs:2778-2784). Devon declined full support while other engines object; PR #1321 open.
reviewer_lesson: When a pseudo-element becomes known, check which pseudo-classes may follow it (e.g. ::scroll-marker:target-current): known pseudo-elements set AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT and reject what unknown ones allowed.

title: Logical Properties order is not preserved when syntax lowering with `:dir()`
trigger: logical margin followed by a physical longhand of the same side, lowered to :dir()/:lang() fallback rules
expected: in RTL the later margin-right:10px wins
actual: .foo{margin-right:10px}.foo:dir(ltr){margin-left:20px}.foo:dir(rtl){margin-right:20px}; Chrome 156 RTL margin-right 10px -> 20px
root_cause: PropertyHandlerContext::get_additional_rules (src/context.rs:93-127) emits ltr/rtl declarations as separate rules appended after the base rule and adds :dir()/:lang() specificity (TODO at src/context.rs:94), so source order between the logical and a later physical declaration is lost.

regression.evidence: fallback rules have always been appended after the base rule; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: For lowering that moves declarations into extra rules, test a later physical/longhand declaration in the same block and compare computed styles in dir=ltr and dir=rtl (and lang=ar for the :lang() variant).

title: Minification doesn't work for Android
trigger: explicit targets {android: 95<<16} (not via browserslist)
actual: .main{color:transparent} (v1.32.0)
root_cause: caniuse squashes Android WebView into 2.x-4.4.4 plus latest, so generated ranges in src/compat.rs/src/prefixes.rs treat android 5..latest-1 like 4.4.4. #1198 switched only #rrggbbaa to MDN data. Residual on master: MaskImage android range is 2.1..=4.4.3 (src/prefixes.rs:1454-1458), so android 95 gets no -webkit-mask-image while chrome 95 does (v1.33.0).
reviewer_lesson: When touching compat or prefix data, test android (and other caniuse-squashed browsers) at a mid version such as 95 and prefer MDN BCD; browserslist maps 'android >= 95' to the latest version, so only explicit targets expose it.

title: 'target-current' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class
trigger: a:target-current (css-overflow-5)
actual: warning "'target-current' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class"; rule preserved. Still warns in v1.33.0 unless drafts.scrollNavigationControls is set
root_cause: #1185 added :target-current/:target-before/:target-after (src/selector.rs:154-156) only behind ParserFlags::SCROLL_NAVIGATION_CONTROLS (drafts.scrollNavigationControls / --scroll-navigation-controls), so default behavior is unchanged.
reviewer_lesson: A fix behind a draft flag does not change default behavior; check the default ParserOptions path and say so when closing the issue.

title: Minification incorrectly collapses align-self + justify-self: auto into place-self shorthand
trigger: align-self + justify-self:auto (or align normal + justify stretch) merged into place-self / place-items
actual: .a{place-self:self-start}; justify-self becomes self-start (Chrome 156 item width 200px -> 8px). Also align-self:normal;justify-self:stretch -> place-self:normal and align-items:normal;justify-items:stretch -> place-items:normal
root_cause: PlaceSelf::to_css (src/properties/align.rs:509-520) returns is_equal=true for JustifySelf::Auto regardless of align and compares the Stretch arm against AlignSelf::Normal; PlaceItems::to_css (:779-780) has the same Stretch/Normal mistake.

regression.evidence: git blame of the match arms; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: When a shorthand omits a component because it equals another, check every arm compares like with like (an omitted second value copies the first) and test each keyword pair in a grid.

title: Support CSS Overflow Module Level 5
trigger: css-overflow-5 syntax: ::scroll-marker, ::scroll-marker-group, scroll-marker-group, ::scroll-button(), :target-*
actual: only :target-current/before/after implemented, behind a drafts flag (#1185); ::scroll-* PR #1321 open
reviewer_lesson: New pseudo-elements need parsing tests for the pseudo-classes allowed after them and compat data so is_compatible/selector splitting treat them correctly.

title: riscv64 support
trigger: npm install on linux riscv64
actual: no prebuilt binary; building from source works
root_cause: riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu is not in the release matrix / scripts/build-npm.js.
reviewer_lesson: Platform additions need a way to test the binary in CI; Devon declined riscv64 in #1268 for low usage and no test hardware.

title: LightningCSS strips :host pseudo-class from CSS embedded in JS string literals during Vite dependency pre-bundling
trigger: :root, :host rule inside CSS imported with ?inline and pre-bundled by Vite (Angular 20)
options: Vite 6 dependency pre-bundling; CSS inside a JS string
actual: reporter sees :host removed; LightningCSS v1.33.0 keeps :host with no targets and with chrome 50/80, safari 9, ie 11 (old targets only split it into its own rule)
root_cause: Not reproducible in LightningCSS: it does not process CSS embedded in JS string literals and transform() never strips :host; the stripping comes from another tool in the Vite/Angular pipeline (UNVERIFIED which).
reviewer_lesson: Reproduce reports with a direct transform() call before attributing them to LightningCSS; framework pipelines run several CSS tools.

title: Failed to deserialize infinity or big number when using visitors
trigger: JS visitor returning an AST node that contains a number outside -32768..65535 or infinity (e.g. Tailwind's calc(infinity * 1px))
actual: throws 'failed to deserialize; expected a 32-bit floating point, found inff64' (99999px: 'found 99999i64'; 65535px works, 65536px fails)
root_cause: napi/src/transformer.rs:759-777 deserializes visitor results with serde_content::Deserializer::coerce_numbers(); serde-content 0.1.2 coerces integers to f32 only within i16::MIN..=u16::MAX and f64 only within f32::MIN..=f32::MAX (serde-content src/de/number.rs:150-155, 244-246), so large integers and infinity fail.

regression.evidence: v1.29.3 round-trips 99999px and calc(infinity*1px); v1.30.2, v1.32.0 and v1.33.0 throw (tested locally); bisect: <=1.30.1 ok, >=1.30.2 error

reviewer_lesson: Any change to the JS<->Rust (de)serialization layer needs a pass-through-visitor round trip over extreme numbers (infinity, -infinity, NaN, >65535, < -32768, -0, 1e10).

title: `@scope`: `&` has the wrong specificity
trigger: & directly inside @scope when targets lack nesting (e.g. chrome 118)
expected: & keeps zero specificity (:where(:scope)); div wins -> green
actual: @scope(.s){:scope{color:red}}div{color:green}; Chrome 156 green -> red
root_cause: ScopeRule::to_css prints child rules with a cleared nesting context (src/rules/scope.rs:102); serialize_nesting then writes ':scope' when Nesting is compiled (src/selector.rs:1767-1771), which has (0,1,0) instead of :where(:scope)'s 0.
