regression.introduced_by: @scope support 6f71ef5 (#586, v1.22.0); spec later defined & as :where(:scope) (CSSWG issue 9740)
regression.evidence: v1.24.1-v1.33.0 all emit :scope

reviewer_lesson: Any selector rewrite (& lowering, :is() wrapping) must keep specificity; check the spec rule for that context and test against a competing selector with slightly lower specificity.

title: Suggestion: bundle option to set http[s] imports as external (without a custom resolver)
trigger: bundle() with @import url("https://...") and no custom resolver
expected: option to treat http(s) specifiers as external
actual: bundle() fails with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'; works with a resolver returning {external} (#880)
root_cause: The default resolver/FileProvider treats every specifier as a file path (src/bundler.rs); external specifiers are only possible through a custom resolve().
reviewer_lesson: Bundler changes should be tested with remote and data: URLs, and errors should name the failing specifier.

title: [pnpm linux] Cli: wrong/no binary ("lightningcss: 1: This: not found")
trigger: pnpm add lightningcss-cli (dependency scripts not approved) or npm --ignore-scripts
actual: 'lightningcss: 1: This: not found' - the placeholder text file is executed
root_cause: lightningcss-cli's bin is a placeholder (cli/lightningcss) that cli/postinstall.js replaces by hard-linking/copying the platform binary; pnpm 10 blocks dependency lifecycle scripts by default and --ignore-scripts skips it.
reviewer_lesson: Packaging changes must be tested with pnpm (scripts blocked) and npm --ignore-scripts; prefer a JS launcher or runtime optionalDependencies resolution over postinstall.

title: color-mix: division by zero in polar color space unpremultiply when alpha is 0
trigger: color-mix() in a polar space (oklch/lch, also hsl/hwb internally) where both colors have alpha 0
actual: oklch(none none 180/0); Chrome 156 computes the input as oklch(0 0 180 / 0)
root_cause: polar_premultiply!::unpremultiply (src/values/color.rs:3659-3666) divides by alpha without the `alpha != 0.0` guard that rectangular_premultiply has (:3640); 0/0 = NaN and NaN is LightningCSS's encoding of `none`.

regression.introduced_by: #465 (4ebcb45), v1.30.0 started resolving color-mix() with oklch/lch arguments; latent bug from 5079e35 (2022)
regression.evidence: v1.29.3 leaves the color-mix() unresolved; v1.30.0-v1.33.0 print oklch(none none 180/0) (tested)

reviewer_lesson: For color math, test alpha 0, alpha none and missing/powerless hues; NaN doubles as `none`, so any arithmetic that can yield NaN silently changes meaning.

title: light-dark() does not return any value when no color-scheme is defined
trigger: light-dark() lowered for targets without support when no color-scheme is declared anywhere
expected: light value, as in native implementations without color-scheme
actual: background:var(--lightningcss-light, red) var(--lightningcss-dark, #00f); both fallbacks substitute and the value is invalid at computed time, so no background
root_cause: The polyfill relies on --lightningcss-light/--lightningcss-dark space toggles that are only emitted where color-scheme is declared (ColorSchemeHandler); documented requirement in website/pages/transpilation.md:336. Closed by Devon as working as intended.
reviewer_lesson: Polyfills that depend on state set elsewhere (custom properties) must document and test the state-absent case; browser comparisons of light-dark() lowering need a color-scheme declaration or an explicit whitelist.

title: Numbers inside invalid syntax are converted to <length> units (px)
trigger: unitless non-zero number where a <length> is expected
expected: invalid declarations stay invalid (kept verbatim, or dropped/warned)
actual: p{grid:1px/1px;width:3px;transform:translateZ(9px)} - invalid CSS becomes valid (Chrome 156 width auto -> 3px)
root_cause: LengthValue::parse_with_range accepts Token::Number as LengthValue::Px with a 'TODO: quirks mode only?' (src/values/length.rs:145-148).

regression.evidence: same output in v1.20.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A minifier must keep invalid input invalid: test that values browsers reject (unitless lengths, wrong types) are not repaired into valid ones.

title: Whitespace stripped incorrectly between adjacent var() calls in translate property, breaking Firefox
trigger: adjacent var() references in a typed property (translate) when minified
actual: translate:var(--x)var(--y); after substitution Firefox sees 12px0-style tokens and drops the declaration
root_cause: Token-list parsing/printing removed whitespace it considered insignificant (src/properties/custom.rs); 32f1f52 stopped removing whitespace in token lists (released v1.31.0). Follow-up size regression #1378.
reviewer_lesson: Whitespace in token lists is significant after var() substitution; test minified var()/env() adjacency in Firefox and weigh the size trade-off (#1378).

title: :has-slotted is flagged as invalid, but it's not
trigger: slot:has-slotted
actual: warning "'has-slotted' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class"; rule preserved
root_cause: Pseudo-class missing from parse_non_ts_pseudo_class in src/selector.rs.
reviewer_lesson: New pseudo-classes need a compat Feature so selector splitting and :is() wrapping treat them correctly for targets.

title: Add support for :interest-source and :interest-target
trigger: :interest-source / :interest-target
actual: warning; rule preserved
root_cause: Not implemented by policy: Devon declined until the spec advances (Chrome-only, other vendors opposed); PR #1204 closed. Devon suggested a way to suppress such warnings.
reviewer_lesson: Maintainer policy: no Chrome-only experimental selectors; unknown selectors must stay warnings and be preserved verbatim.

title: url visitor doesn't visit the url of @import
trigger: Url visitor on a stylesheet with @import
actual: only bar.png is visited
root_cause: ImportRule.url is a CowArcStr marked #[skip_visit] (src/rules/import.rs:25-26), not a Url value, so neither the Rust nor the JS Url visitor sees it.
reviewer_lesson: When an AST field holds a URL or name, decide and document whether visitors see it; enumerate visitor coverage in tests.

title: Visiting both Rules and Urls only visits Rules
trigger: Rust Visitor overriding visit_rule without calling rule.visit_children(self)
actual: URLs inside rules are not visited
root_cause: Default Visitor::visit_rule calls rule.visit_children(self) (src/visitor.rs:169-171); an override replaces it, so children are skipped unless the override recurses. The JS visitor always recurses. Documentation gap.
reviewer_lesson: Visitor API changes should document recursion semantics and keep Rust and JS visitors consistent.

title: Property reordering during minification causes certain settings to be ignored
trigger: font shorthand followed by a reset-only font longhand the FontHandler does not track
actual: p{font-variant-numeric:oldstyle-nums;font:12px serif}; the shorthand resets it (Chrome 156: oldstyle-nums -> normal). Same for font-kerning, font-feature-settings, font-variation-settings, font-optical-sizing, font-size-adjust, font-variant-*, font-language-override, font-width
root_cause: FontHandler (src/properties/font.rs:830-892) buffers the font shorthand and 7 longhands until finalize ('TODO: reset other properties' at :879); other font-* longhands return false and are pushed immediately, ahead of the flushed shorthand.

regression.evidence: TODO present since the handler was written; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: For shorthand handlers, list every property the shorthand resets (the spec's 'reset implicitly' list) and test each one written after the shorthand.

title: Update const-str dependency to 0.3.2+
trigger: cargo deny reports duplicate syn versions through const-str 0.3
actual: const-str-proc-macro pulled syn 1
root_cause: Outdated const-str dependency.
reviewer_lesson: Dependency bumps such as #1200 (which also bumped cssparser) can change tokenizer behavior; diff output on a corpus before release.

title: Support multiple comma-separated queries in @container rules
trigger: @container with a comma-separated list of conditions
actual: ERROR 'Unexpected token Comma' (hard error); with errorRecovery the rule is dropped
root_cause: ContainerRule holds a single name: Option<ContainerName> and condition: Option<ContainerCondition> (src/rules/container.rs:30-41), parsed once at src/parser.rs:670-671; supporting a list changes the public AST (serde, ast.d.ts, visitors).
reviewer_lesson: Check at-rule prelude grammars against the current editor's draft; newly valid syntax must never become a hard error that fails builds.

title: `:-webkit-any(:lang(...))` and `:-moz-any(:lang(...))` rules dropped when targets are set
trigger: :-webkit-any()/:-moz-any() rules next to an equivalent :is() rule, with targets set; or :-webkit-any() nested inside :not() with no targets
expected: reporter expected the prefixed rules to be kept
actual: prefixed rules are merged into the :is() rule and dropped because chrome 100 needs no prefix (they are kept when safari 13 / firefox 70 are targeted). Separately, with no targets .a:not(:-webkit-any(.b,.c)) prints as .a:not(:is(.b,.c)) and :-webkit-any(#x) :not(.c) gains an extra :is(#x) :not(.c) copy
root_cause: merge_style_rules (src/rules/mod.rs:1082-1093) treats prefix-equivalent rules (is_equivalent) as one rule whose prefixes are recomputed from targets (intended since f782754). The no-target bug: get_prefix (src/selector.rs:2075-2100) returns VendorPrefix::None at :not()/:is()/:lang() without descending, and Component::Any serializes with dest.vendor_prefix.or(prefix) (src/selector.rs:1671-1679), so a nested :-webkit-any() prints as :is() and None|WebKit rules print twice.

regression.introduced_by: f782754 'Fix bugs with merging rules containing :is and :-webkit-any' (v1.22.0); duplicate copy since v1.21.0
regression.evidence: v1.20.0/v1.21.0 keep .a:not(:-webkit-any(.b,.c)); v1.22.1-v1.33.0 print :not(:is(.b,.c)) (tested). The targets-set drop is intended behavior

reviewer_lesson: Prefix logic must look into nested selector lists (:not/:is/:has/:where) and be tested with no targets, where nothing may be rewritten or duplicated.

title: Support `::search-text` (and `:current::search-text`) highlight pseudos from CSS Pseudo-4
trigger: .x::search-text (css-pseudo-4 highlight pseudo)
actual: warning in v1.32.0
root_cause: Pseudo-element unknown. #1213 (v1.33.0) added it but made ::search-text:current and ::search-text:not(:current) hard errors (#1303): a known pseudo-element sets AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT and accepts_state_pseudo_classes() is false (selectors/parser.rs:2778-2786), and #1213 implemented :current::search-text instead of the spec form.
reviewer_lesson: When a pseudo-element moves from unknown to known, forms that used to pass with a warning can become hard errors; test the spec's allowed trailing pseudo-classes and the WPT parsing file before merging.

title: `transition` shorthand incorrectly combines `inherit` with other longhand sub-properties
trigger: transition: <CSS-wide keyword> followed by a transition longhand (also a CSS-wide transition-property merged into the shorthand)
expected: two declarations kept; the other longhands still inherit
actual: foo{transition:bar}: duration/delay/easing reset (Chrome 156 2s -> 0s). transition-property:initial plus longhands -> invalid transition:initial 1s. Same class: font:12px serif;font-family:inherit -> invalid font:12px inherit
root_cause: The transition parser takes the property via PropertyId::parse (src/properties/transition.rs:69; src/properties/mod.rs:240-244), which accepts any ident including CSS-wide keywords, so the value is typed instead of falling back to Property::Unparsed and TransitionHandler merges it. FamilyName::parse (src/properties/font.rs:385-410) has the same gap.

regression.evidence: same output in v1.20.0; bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Any parser that accepts <custom-ident> or family names must reject CSS-wide keywords and `default`; test each shorthand handler with a CSS-wide keyword in the shorthand and in each longhand.

title: `composes:` silently accepts references to non-existent local classes
trigger: composes: <name> where no local class <name> exists
expected: error or warning (postcss-modules-scope errors: referenced class name not found)
actual: builds silently; exports composes [{type: local, name: <hash>_historychevron}] for a class that is never emitted
root_cause: CssModule::handle_composes (src/css_modules.rs:464-524): the local (from: None) branch hashes the name without checking exports; the from-file (SourceIndex) branch silently `continue`s on a miss.
reviewer_lesson: CSS-modules validation must be order-independent (the composed class may be defined later) and should start as a warning so existing builds do not break.

title: Negative scientific notation numbers are emitted incorrectly
trigger: negative number small enough to serialize in scientific notation, as a dimension or percentage
actual: rotate(--1e-7deg) in v1.32.0; fixed for dimensions in v1.33.0 (#1192). v1.33.0 still prints margin-left:--10e-8% for -0.0000001%
root_cause: Three copies of the strip-leading-zero logic: CSSNumber (src/values/number.rs, fixed by #901 in v1.29.2), serialize_dimension (src/values/length.rs, fixed by #1192 in v1.33.0) and Percentage::to_css (src/values/percentage.rs:66-70, still writes '-' then trim_start_matches("-0")).
reviewer_lesson: When fixing a serialization bug, grep for every copy of the logic (number, dimension, percentage) and test tiny negative values in each type.

title: minify: linear-gradient(0deg... with percentages is incorrectly rotated
trigger: linear-gradient(0deg | to top, ...) with non-monotonic percentage stop positions, minified
expected: same rendering (keep 0deg, or flip after color-stop fixup)
actual: linear-gradient(#242430 100%,#1f1f29 0%) renders #242430 where the input renders #1f1f29
root_cause: LinearGradient::to_css (src/values/gradient.rs:282-318) reverses items and maps p -> 1-p whenever all positions are percentages, without first applying color-stop fixup (each position clamped to the largest earlier one).

regression.evidence: same output in v1.20.0

reviewer_lesson: Geometric rewrites of gradients must be checked with non-monotonic stops, hints and double-position stops, comparing rendered pixels rather than serialized strings.

title: `font-family: monospace, monospace` should not deduplicate (the duplication is load-bearing)
trigger: font-family list repeating a family (monospace, monospace)
actual: font-family:monospace; a lone generic monospace triggers the UA monospace font-size quirk (Chrome 156: 16px -> 13px)
root_cause: FontHandler::flush dedupes every family list (src/properties/font.rs:926-931), added in 41dfaa4 to clean up system-ui fallback expansion (#246).

regression.evidence: git: no dedupe before 41dfaa4 (first tag v1.13.0); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master all dedupe

reviewer_lesson: Deduplicating list values needs both spec and browser justification; check known quirks (monospace sizing) in a real browser and dedupe only what LightningCSS itself inserted.

title: `@layer` ordering declaration is silently dropped when followed by `@layer` blocks
trigger: @layer statement followed by blocks for the same layers in the same order
expected: reporter expected the statement to be kept
actual: statement removed; blocks keep the declared order, so the cascade is unchanged (verified in Chrome 156). Closed as not planned
root_cause: CssRuleList::minify turns statement names into placeholder LayerBlock rules and merges later blocks into them (src/rules/mod.rs:712-752). Real ordering bugs in this code (#974 sublayers; merging a block across an @media that adds to the same layer) were fixed on master by 32aecd9 on the day #1222 was closed; v1.33.0 still has them.

regression.introduced_by: aedf6b6 'Optimize @layer rules' (v1.23.0) folds the statement into the blocks
regression.evidence: bisect: <=1.22.1 kept the statement, >=1.23.0 removes it; cascade unchanged within one stylesheet (Chrome 156); maintainer: not a bug; users with several CSS chunks rely on the statement

reviewer_lesson: Layer optimizations are only safe when no rule between the moved blocks can declare or add to the same layer hierarchy (conditional groups, imports, nested sublayers); test with @media/@supports in between.

title: New color-mix() features: optional interpolation method, variadic color arguments
trigger: color-mix() without an interpolation method, or with one / three+ colors
expected: resolve with the oklab default (or keep for supporting targets); lower for others
actual: passed through unchanged (safe); Chrome 156 supports the optional method but not variadic colors
root_cause: The color-mix() parser requires `in <space>` and exactly two colors (src/values/color.rs).
reviewer_lesson: When extending color-mix(), verify the oklab default, percentage normalization for more than two colors, and that unsupported forms still pass through untouched.

title: Minification reorders duplicate declarations for `position`, `direction`, and `unicode-bidi` when one uses `var()`
trigger: typed position/direction/unicode-bidi followed by a var() value of the same property
actual: .x{position:var(--x,static);position:static}; the static fallback wins (Chrome 156 absolute -> static)
root_cause: PositionHandler::handle_property has no Unparsed arm (src/properties/position.rs:104-114), so the var() declaration is pushed immediately while the typed value waits for finalize; direction/unicode-bidi are buffered in DeclarationHandler::handle_all (src/declaration.rs:646-657, flushed at :696-700) with the same gap.

regression.introduced_by: d7aeff3 'optimize all property' (v1.25.0) for direction/unicode-bidi; position since 9f937df (2021)
regression.evidence: v1.24.1 keeps direction order, v1.25.0-v1.33.0 reverse it (tested); position reversed in every tested version; bisect: direction ok <=1.24.1, reordered >=1.25.0; position reordered in all versions

reviewer_lesson: Every handler that buffers a property must flush before an Unparsed (var()) declaration of the same property; add a var()-after-static test per buffered property.

title: animation-range keywords (entry/exit) transformed incorrectly during build
trigger: animation-range shorthand whose end is a bare <timeline-range-name>
actual: entry exit 0%; and entry 0% exit 100% -> entry exit -> (second pass) entry exit 0%
root_cause: AnimationRange::parse parses the end with AnimationRangeStart::parse (default offset 0%) and rewraps it as AnimationRangeEnd (src/properties/animation.rs:537-540); AnimationRangeEnd::to_css omits only 100%, so 0% is printed.

regression.evidence: bisect: <=1.25.1 pass animation-range through untouched, >=1.27.0 print 'exit 0%' (1.26.0 not installed); wrong since the typed parser landed

reviewer_lesson: Run serializer tests through parse(print(x)) again (idempotency): Tailwind + Vite run LightningCSS twice, so a lossy round trip breaks real builds.

title: Anchored container queries are not supported
trigger: @container anchored(fallback: ...)
actual: ERROR 'Unexpected token Function("anchored")' (hard error); with errorRecovery the rule is kept verbatim with a warning
root_cause: The container (and media) query parser has no anchored() feature and does not fall back to <general-enclosed> for unknown functions: `@media foo(bar){}` and `@container foo(bar){}` also hard-error in v1.33.0, while `@supports foo(bar)` is accepted. Tracked in #1176 (PR #1218 open).
reviewer_lesson: Query grammars include <general-enclosed>; unknown functions must parse and evaluate to unknown instead of failing the whole stylesheet.

title: `backdrop-filter` dropped when `-webkit-backdrop-filter` present, breaking styles
trigger: backdrop-filter followed by an equal -webkit-backdrop-filter (same for filter)
expected: both kept (or only the unprefixed one)
actual: .glass{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(16px)saturate(1.2)}; Chrome and Firefox ignore it (Chrome 156 computed none)
root_cause: FallbackHandler for Filter(prefix)/BackdropFilter(prefix) (src/properties/prefix_handler.rs:93-121) keeps one index per property and overwrites the earlier declaration with the later one, prefix included (:119-120), instead of OR-ing prefixes as PrefixHandler does (:28-34). Canonical issue #695 (open), PR #1259 (open).

regression.evidence: same mechanism and bisect as #977/#1086/#1327 (1.20.0 keeps both declarations, 1.21.0+ keep only the prefixed one); the b4 note 'since b9624aa' is wrong: b9624aa added FallbackHandler without the overwrite

reviewer_lesson: Test prefixed/unprefixed pairs in both orders, with and without targets, and run the output in an engine that supports only the unprefixed form.

title: Make inputSourceMap available via CLI
trigger: CLI run on CSS produced by another compiler (Sass) with its own source map
expected: an --input-source-map flag like the inputSourceMap API option
actual: CLI drops or overwrites the upstream mapping
root_cause: src/main.rs has no input source map argument; only the Node API exposes inputSourceMap (node/index.d.ts:18).
reviewer_lesson: Keep CLI flags in parity with node/index.d.ts options, and test source-map chaining end to end.

title: Unknown at-rules, are incorrectly hoisted
trigger: unknown at-rule (e.g. @apply mixin) nested in a style rule when targets lack nesting
actual: v1.32.0: .foo{text-decoration-line:underline}@apply --my-mixin-1; (hoisted to the top level)
root_cause: StyleRule::to_css_base printed every nested rule after the parent when nesting is compiled; #1233 keeps CssRule::Unknown children inside the declaration block (src/rules/style.rs). Residual in v1.33.0: an unknown at-rule inside a nested @media is printed without the parent selector (@media (min-width:1px){@apply --x;}).
reviewer_lesson: Nesting-lowering fixes must cover every nesting context (direct child, nested @media/@supports/@container/@layer, nested declarations), not only the reported one.

title: Transpile font-width <-> font-stretch
trigger: font-width (new name of font-stretch) with or without targets
expected: font-width <-> font-stretch translated per targets; order kept
actual: font-width is an unknown property: moved before the buffered font shorthand (.a{font-width:condensed;font:12px serif}) and before font-stretch (font-stretch:expanded;font-width:condensed -> font-width:condensed;font-stretch:125%)
root_cause: No FontWidth property; FontHandler buffers font/font-stretch and lets unknown font-* through immediately (src/properties/font.rs:855-888).
reviewer_lesson: Property aliases (font-stretch/font-width) share one cascade slot; handlers must treat them as one property for ordering and dedupe.

title: Stale StyleRuleKey hash after merge_style_rules causes missed dedup and nondeterministic minified output
trigger: rule merging that mutates or pops an indexed rule, followed by a later rule with the same selectors and property ids
actual: .a,.q{color:red}.q{color:#00f}: the nested .n rule is erased (Chrome 156 green -> blue). The issue's own repro misses a dedup (.a{border-radius:16px}.x{color:red}.a{border-radius:16px}, removed only on a second pass); reporter saw 1-2.5% run-to-run differences in rspack
root_cause: style_rules: HashMap<StyleRuleKey, usize> caches rule.hash_key() at insert (src/rules/mod.rs:1222-1235) while PartialEq reads the live rule (:1237-1250). merge_style_rules mutates rules in place and the cascade loop rules.pop()s (:808) without removing the index, so a later rule pushed into that slot (with nested rules, never inserted) is compared by is_duplicate, which ignores nested rules, and marked Ignored. AHasher::default() uses per-process random seeds (ahash runtime-rng), so probe collisions vary between runs (not reproduced locally).

regression.introduced_by: dedup aa083a7 (v1.20.0) combined with cascade pop e9277fd (2022)
regression.evidence: nested-rule drop seen in v1.21.0-v1.33.0 (tested); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Changes to rule merging/dedup must keep index-based side tables in sync after mutation or pop; test with nested rules and cascading merges, run minify twice, and run it in several processes to catch nondeterminism.

title: Pseudo-element arg inside `:has()` / `:is()` / `:where()` is dropped, leaving an empty `()` and an invalid output selector
trigger: pseudo-element argument inside :has() (also :is()/:where())
expected: keep the original, drop the rule, or warn
actual: video:not(:has()) silently; a:has(::before,.b) -> a:has(:before,.b); a:is(::before) -> a:is(). Input and output are both invalid in Chrome 156 (empty :is() is valid and matches nothing)
root_cause: parse_has (selectors/parser.rs:2832-2852) uses is_and_where_error_recovery() (IgnoreInvalidSelector), i.e. forgiving parsing, although :has() now takes an unforgiving <relative-selector-list>; invalid arguments are silently dropped.
reviewer_lesson: Distinguish forgiving (:is/:where) from unforgiving (:has/:not) lists: an invalid argument in an unforgiving list must invalidate the rule (with a warning), not vanish.

title: Selecting `::details-content::before` pseudo element errors
trigger: pseudo-element after the element-backed ::details-content
expected: accepted (element-backed pseudo-elements allow any following pseudo; Chrome, Firefox and Safari accept)
actual: ERROR 'Invalid state' (hard error)
root_cause: Every known pseudo-element other than ::part()/::slotted() sets AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT (selectors/parser.rs:2778-2786), which forbids further pseudo-elements; there is no element-backed notion for ::details-content. PR #1308 open.
reviewer_lesson: Model element-backed pseudo-elements (::part, ::details-content, future ones) explicitly and check each new pseudo-element against the spec's allowed-after rules.

title: Logical border radius polyfill is hoisted into pseudo classes, breaking base styles
trigger: logical property in nested declarations (after a nested rule) lowered for targets without logical support, followed by another nested style rule
actual: fallback rules attached to .btn:hover only; base .btn loses the radius (Chrome 156 8px -> 0px)
root_cause: NestedDeclarationsRule::minify (src/rules/nesting.rs:72-84) minifies with the shared handler_context but never calls get_additional_rules()/reset(), so the ltr/rtl declarations it produced are consumed by the next StyleRule's minify (&:hover) with that rule's selectors (src/rules/mod.rs:820-838).

regression.evidence: v1.29.1/v1.29.3 attach the fallbacks to .btn; v1.30.0-v1.33.0 to .btn:hover (tested); bisect: 1.22.1..1.29.3 .btn, 1.30.1..master .btn:hover

reviewer_lesson: Shared minify state (handler_context) must be drained by the rule that filled it; test logical, light-dark() and @supports fallbacks inside nested declarations followed by sibling nested rules.

title: Colour precision too high
trigger: achromatic oklch() converted to a lab() fallback
root_cause: f32 error through the OKLab -> XYZ -> Lab conversions leaves ~1e-5 residues and serialization does not snap near-zero channels (src/values/color.rs). Visual difference is nil; output size only. PR #1332 (float precision) open.

regression.evidence: bisect: <=1.29.3 left oklch() unlowered for chrome 100 (no fallback at all); 1.30.0+ lower it with f32 noise in the channels (size only, visually identical)

reviewer_lesson: Color conversion changes should be checked for achromatic inputs producing exact zeros and for output size.

title: Expose current filename to visitors
trigger: JS visitor that must resolve relative paths (e.g. an @value from implementation)
expected: visitor options expose source file names (sources)
actual: loc has only source_index; names reachable only through the StyleSheet visitor, which serializes the whole AST
root_cause: The visitor factory (node/index.js wrap) passes only addDependency (#1170).
reviewer_lesson: Visitor API additions must work for bundle(), where one pass covers several stylesheets (Devon's objection).

title: Support Relative Alpha Colors(CSS Color 5 alpha() function)
trigger: alpha(from <color> / <alpha>) (css-color-5 relative alpha)
expected: resolved, or lowered for old targets
actual: v1.33.0 resolves static origins (#ff000080); currentcolor/var() origins pass through unchanged; reopened for spec follow-ups
reviewer_lesson: New color functions must preserve unresolvable origins (currentcolor, var(), light-dark()) and should come with WPT parsing/computed tests.

title: `view-transition-name: match-element` is incorrectly transformed
trigger: view-transition-name: match-element with cssModules
actual: view-transition-name:<hash>_match-element (v1.33.0)
root_cause: ViewTransitionName had no MatchElement variant, so the reserved keyword parsed as <custom-ident> and was scoped; #1274 adds the variant (src/properties/transition.rs), on master only (unreleased as of 2026-10-25).
reviewer_lesson: When a spec reserves a new keyword in a <custom-ident> slot, add it explicitly; otherwise CSS modules hashes it and ident-based optimizations treat it as a name.

title: Incompatible selectors can be dropped after rule merging when targets require selector splitting
trigger: selector list containing a target-incompatible selector whose compatible part merges into the previous rule
actual: .a:last-child{border-bottom:none;display:flex}; Chrome 156 display flex -> block. Same with :focus-visible at chrome 85
root_cause: CssRuleList::minify partitions incompatible selectors (src/rules/mod.rs:758-790), merge_style_rules then drains the rule's declarations into the previous rule (:796-818), and only afterwards clones the drained rule per incompatible selector (:824-838); the empty clones are skipped by is_empty().

regression.introduced_by: 5c105fb 'Split selector lists when some selectors aren't supported by targets' (v1.21.0)
regression.evidence: v1.20.0 keeps .a:last-child,.a:has(+.b){display:flex}; v1.21.0-v1.33.0 drop :has() (tested); bisect: 1.14.0..1.20.0 kept, 1.21.0..master dropped

reviewer_lesson: When a minify step derives new rules from a rule, derive them before any step that consumes the rule's declarations, and test with a preceding mergeable rule.

title: Add prebuilt riscv64 (linux-gnu) binary
trigger: require('lightningcss') on linux riscv64
actual: loader throws; no package or wasm fallback on that path
root_cause: No riscv64 target in the release matrix; PR #1268 open, Devon hesitant (low usage, no way to test).
reviewer_lesson: Same as #1186: new platforms need CI coverage before shipping.

title: Error: [lightningcss minify] Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-arm64-musl.node'
trigger: Vite build on linux arm64 musl when lightningcss-linux-arm64-musl is not installed
expected: binding loads, or a clear error naming the missing optional package
actual: Error: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-arm64-musl.node'
root_cause: node/index.js:18-21 catches the failed require of lightningcss-<platform> and retries a local ../lightningcss.<platform>.node, so the user sees the misleading second error; the optional dependency itself was not installed. PR #1282 (better message) closed.
reviewer_lesson: Native-loader changes should surface the original require error and the expected package name; test on musl and with lockfiles created on another platform.

title: Make the `mod parser` public.
trigger: Rust user wants crate-internal parser::NestedRuleParser / AtRulePrelude to build a custom TopLevelRuleParser
expected: public access to the nested rule parser, or an extension point for non-standard syntax
actual: `mod parser` is private (src/lib.rs); only StyleSheet::parse_with + custom AtRuleParser are exposed
root_cause: By design: parser.rs holds internals; Devon asked for the use case (non-standard syntax), no decision yet.
reviewer_lesson: Changes that widen the Rust public surface (pub mod/pub fields) are semver commitments for the 1.0.0-alpha crate; require a concrete use case and docs.

title: Support for `<color-interpolation-method>` in gradients
trigger: linear-/radial-/conic-gradient() with a leading `in <colorspace> [<hue-method>]`
expected: typed parse of <color-interpolation-method>; colors minified; lowering that keeps interpolation semantics
actual: not parsed as Gradient, falls back to an unparsed token list (verbatim with no targets). With targets chrome 100 the token-list colors are still lowered: `linear-gradient(in oklch, #d2849c, #00747a)` plus `@supports (color:lab(0% 0 0))` copy with lab() colors, so `none` is lost and the fallback is unusable by browsers that lack `in oklch`
root_cause: src/values/gradient.rs has no <color-interpolation-method> grammar; the TokenList color-fallback path (custom.rs get_fallbacks) converts colors without knowing they sit in an interpolation context.
reviewer_lesson: When colors are rewritten inside an unparsed value, check whether the surrounding function interpolates (gradients, color-mix): converting `none` or the color space changes the result.

title: Lightningcss unable to parse TinyMCE 8.5.1 minified oxide skin CSS
trigger: `:nth-child(2of.x)` from a minifier that removed the whitespace before `of`
expected: parse error (correct): `2of` tokenizes as one <dimension-token>, which is not An+B
actual: Unexpected token Ident("of") (rule rejected; whole sheet fails without errorRecovery)
root_cause: Input is invalid per css-syntax-3 (numeric token consumes the ident `of` as a unit); browsers also drop the rule. Reporter filed tinymce/tinymce#11146.
reviewer_lesson: Do not make the parser 'tolerant' of tokenization-level invalid input: accepting it turns a rule browsers drop into a live one.

title: Value calculations not reducing when using Node API
trigger: calc() written as the value of a custom property is not simplified
actual: --x:calc(2 * 1rem); width:2rem
root_cause: Working as designed: custom property values are unparsed token lists (no grammar), so math is not evaluated; tracked in #506. Reporter closed it.
reviewer_lesson: Any PR that starts simplifying values inside custom properties must prove the token list has a known type at every use site; registered @property syntax is the only safe source of that.

title: Publish the rust crate please
trigger: crates.io lagged behind master
actual: release published
root_cause: Release request; closed with v1.33.0 (tag commit 1d680fa).
reviewer_lesson: Downstream Rust users consume the crate directly; behaviour changes land for them on the crate release, separately from npm.

title: Parsing issue min-zoom in media query
trigger: unknown media feature whose value is not an <mf-value> (percentage): `(min-zoom: 120%)`
repro_css: @media screen and (min-width: 700px), screen and (min-zoom: 120%) { .root { color: red; } }
expected: accept: the second query matches <general-enclosed> and evaluates to false, the list still matches screen >= 700px
actual: hard error `Unexpected token Colon`; with errorRecovery the tokens are kept verbatim with a warning
root_cause: MediaCondition::parse_with_flags (src/media_query.rs:614-628) only falls back to MediaCondition::Unknown (general-enclosed) when error_recovery is on. Reporter closed it believing the CSS was invalid.
reviewer_lesson: For media/container query changes, check both modes: strict mode rejects <general-enclosed>, errorRecovery must print it verbatim, and neither may rewrite an unknown feature.

title: Simplify division of like units to unitless constant
trigger: division of like units: calc(4px / 2px), calc((8px / 16px) * 1rem)
actual: kept verbatim (typed parse fails, value stays an unparsed token list)
root_cause: Calc only supports number divisors (src/values/calc.rs); css-values-4 now allows typed arithmetic (dimension / dimension -> number). Only absolute, same-dimension units can be folded at build time.
reviewer_lesson: Folding typed division is only safe for absolute units (px/in/cm...); em/rem/%/viewport units must stay symbolic, and the result can make a declaration valid for engines that rejected the original.

title: Support multiple input files to single output file with CLI
trigger: lightningcss --output-file=all.css --bundle a.css b.css c.css
expected: concatenate/bundle several inputs into one output
actual: `Cannot use the --output-file option with multiple inputs. Use --output-dir instead.`
root_cause: src/main.rs rejects multiple inputs with --output-file; workaround is an entry file with @import + --bundle.
reviewer_lesson: Concatenating independent sheets changes @import/@charset/@layer ordering semantics; a CLI change here needs the same ordering rules as the bundler.

title: `animation-timeline: view()` added to `animation` shorthand
trigger: `animation` shorthand plus `animation-timeline` longhand in one rule, targets Chrome >= 115 (or no targets)
actual: .a{animation:1ms linear both parallax view();animation-range:exit} — every engine rejects the shorthand, so the animation is lost
root_cause: AnimationHandler::flush folds timelines when targets.is_compatible(AnimationTimelineShorthand) (src/properties/animation.rs:957-965); the compat data comes from MDN animation-timeline_included, whose Chrome 115 entry is partial_implementation (reset-only), and scripts/build-prefixes.js:337 does not filter partial entries.

regression.evidence: <=1.24.x already broke it differently: the unknown animation-timeline was moved before the shorthand, which resets it; >=1.25.0 fold it into the shorthand

reviewer_lesson: Every compat key generated from MDN must ignore partial_implementation entries (Devon on #1306: 'partial support should not imply full support'); check the BCD notes before trusting a version.

title: Error: [lightningcss minify] Cannot find module '../lightningcss.openharmony-arm64.node'
trigger: npm install on OpenHarmony arm64 (process.platform 'openharmony')
expected: a native binary or a clear fallback
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.openharmony-arm64.node'
root_cause: No openharmony target in .github/workflows/release.yml / scripts/build-npm.js; node/index.js only knows linux/darwin/win32/freebsd/android. lightningcss-wasm is the only option.
reviewer_lesson: Changes to node/index.js platform detection must keep a readable error (and the wasm fallback hint) for unsupported platforms.

title: Unexpected transformation of x units in image-set()
trigger: image-set() with `x` resolutions inside a value that also contains var() (unparsed), targets lacking the `x` alias (Safari < 16)
actual: image-set(url(a.png) 1dppx, url(b.png) 2dppx), var(--c) — Safari < 17 and Chrome < 113 do not accept dppx inside image-set()
root_cause: TokenList::parse_into turns dimension tokens into TokenOrValue::Resolution (src/properties/custom.rs:442) and Resolution::to_css prints dppx when XResolutionUnit is unsupported (src/values/resolution.rs:86); the typed ImageSetOption path (src/values/image.rs:477-483) deliberately ignores targets but the token-list path cannot know it is inside image-set. Also rewrites `--s: 2x` to `--s: 2dppx`.

regression.evidence: 1.16.1 keeps 1x; 1.17.0 prints 1dppx for the same input

reviewer_lesson: Unit or keyword rewriting in token lists is context-free; a rewrite that is right for one property (media resolution) can be wrong inside another function (image-set) or a custom property.

title: Unexpected behavior when transforming `display: flex` with vendor prefixes
trigger: `display:flex` followed by legacy prefixed values (-webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox) in the same rule, with targets
expected: display:flex kept (Chrome ignores -ms-flexbox, so the input is a flex container)
actual: .foo{display:-ms-flexbox} — Chrome/Firefox/Safari get no flex layout. Cross-rule variant (no targets): `.t{display:flex}.u{}.t{display:-ms-flexbox}` drops the first rule via duplicate-rule removal
root_cause: DisplayHandler::handle_property (src/properties/display.rs:380-392) treats a later prefixed-equivalent value as overriding and, with targets, discards the earlier unprefixed one; prefixes are only re-added for an unprefixed value. StyleRule::is_duplicate (src/rules/style.rs) compares property ids only, so the cross-rule case drops the real value too.

regression.evidence: 1.19.0 already outputs display:-ms-flexbox; logic dates from f200cbe (2021); bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: A prefixed value is only a safe override of the unprefixed one in engines that understand the prefix; any dedupe of 'equivalent' prefixed values must keep the unprefixed declaration.

title: Chaining a pseudo-class after the '::picker' pseudo-element is not allowed.
trigger: non-user-action pseudo-class after ::picker(): `select::picker(select):not(:popover-open)`
actual: Invalid pseudo class after pseudo element, only user action pseudo classes (e.g. :hover, :active) are allowed
root_cause: Known pseudo-elements set AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT and only is_user_action_state() pseudo-classes may follow (selectors/parser.rs:3129). Devon: not in the spec; w3c/csswg-drafts#10775 is unresolved. Workaround `select:open::picker(select)`.
reviewer_lesson: Which pseudo-classes may follow a pseudo-element is per pseudo-element (::part, ::search-text, ::picker, view transitions); a generic allowlist change affects all of them.

title: Consider adding an explicit copyright notice to the LICENSE file
trigger: LICENSE (MPL-2.0) lacks a copyright line
actual: none in repo
root_cause: Housekeeping request; no maintainer response yet.
reviewer_lesson: License/notice edits need the maintainer's decision; not a code-review item.

title: Unbounded recursion in selector, math-function and rule-nesting parsing overflows the stack
trigger: deeply nested :is()/:not(), calc()/min(), nested style rules, @media/@supports blocks
actual: stack overflow -> abort (not catchable by catch_unwind). Master CLI (16 MB stack): :is() x5000, a{ x20000, calc( x20000 abort; thresholds are much lower on 2 MB threads
root_cause: Only TokenList parsing has a depth guard (src/properties/custom.rs, MaximumNestingDepth since 1fd5b4e); Calc::parse_sum, SelectorList::parse and the rule-body parser recurse without a limit.
reviewer_lesson: Any new recursive parse path (math functions, selector arguments, nested rules) needs a depth limit and a deep-nesting test, because an abort takes down the host bundler.

title: Gamut mapping returns at the first under-JND chroma, producing desaturated sRGB fallbacks
trigger: out-of-gamut color lowered to sRGB for old targets (gamut mapping)
actual: #fffbac in 1.33.0 (stops at the first chroma under the JND; no pre-loop clip check)
root_cause: map_gamut (src/values/color.rs) returned at the first in-loop delta_e < JND and lacked the min_inGamut flag and the initial clip check; fixed by #1323 (ab14f90, master, unreleased). Devon's review of #1323 caught a side effect on the white/black cut-offs (oklch(99.995% .01 0) became white).

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Diff color-lowering output against a reference implementation (colorjs.io 'css' method) over a corpus; shared epsilon constants also feed the black/white shortcuts.

title: [Bug] 'highlight' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-element, even though it is present in `src/selector`
trigger: `::highlight(name)`
actual: 1.32.0: UnsupportedPseudoElement warning/error. 1.33.0 and master: accepted, no warning (issue is stale)
root_cause: Support landed in #970 (df63db2, merged 2026-03-12, first released in v1.33.0); the reporter tested the playground/1.32.0 (fumadocs on Next.js used 1.32.0).
reviewer_lesson: Check which release contains a merged fix before triaging; the playground and bundlers pin older versions.

title: [bug] v1.33.0 rejects valid ::search-text:current and ::search-text:not(:current) selectors
trigger: `::search-text:current`, `::search-text:not(:current)`
actual: Invalid pseudo class after pseudo element, only user action pseudo classes (e.g. :hover, :active) are allowed
root_cause: #1213 made ::search-text a known pseudo-element, so the generic AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT rule (selectors/parser.rs:3129) now applies; as an unknown pseudo-element in 1.32.0 anything was allowed after it.

regression.evidence: 1.32.0 accepts with an 'unknown pseudo-element' warning; 1.33.0 errors; bisect: 1.21.0..1.32.0 accepted with a warning, 1.33.0 error

reviewer_lesson: Promoting a pseudo-element from unknown to known tightens validation; test every pseudo-class combination the spec/WPT allow after it (here :current, :not(:current)).

title: Minifier silently drops a rule when a selector list is split and another selector in that list duplicates an earlier rule
trigger: selector list with one target-incompatible selector of different specificity, whose compatible half duplicates the previous rule's selector; any targets (incl. {})
actual: a:hover{color:red;background:#00f} — the split-off rule disappears silently
root_cause: In CssRuleList::minify the compatible part is merged into the previous rule first; merge_style_rules drains style.declarations, and only afterwards incompatible_rules clones `style` (now empty), so `!rule.is_empty()` drops it (src/rules/mod.rs:800-838, 900). Pseudo-classes without compat data (:open, :modal, :popover-open, :defined, unknown) always count as incompatible.

regression.introduced_by: 5c105fb (v1.21.0) Split selector lists when some selectors aren't supported by targets
regression.evidence: 1.19.0 keeps the list; 1.21.0+ drops the rule; bisect: <=1.20.0 kept (with a warning), >=1.21.0 dropped

reviewer_lesson: When a pass mutates or moves a rule's declarations, check that every later use of that rule (clones for split selectors, @supports/logical copies) happens before the move.

title: Percentage math functions panic in percentage-typed contexts
trigger: abs()/sign()/mod()/rem()/round()/hypot() with percentages in percentage slots (opacity, hsl/hwb/lab channels, alpha)
actual: 1.33.0: panic at src/values/percentage.rs:30 (unreachable!()); master: value kept verbatim, no panic
root_cause: Percentage::parse assumed every Calc<Percentage> folds to a value (`Ok(_) => unreachable!()`); newer math functions can leave a non-value Calc. #1329 (b0939ab, master, unreleased) replaced it with Err(InvalidValue).
reviewer_lesson: Treat every unreachable!()/unwrap() on parse results as a fuzz target; adding a math function or value type can make 'impossible' branches reachable.

title: Abort trap: 6 on url(data:)
trigger: CLI given CSS with a parse error (here a stray top-level `a:url(data:...)}`)
expected: a parse error message and non-zero exit
actual: panic at src/main.rs:196 `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: EndOfInput` (abort, exit 134); still on master
root_cause: src/main.rs unwraps StyleSheet::parse, Bundler::bundle, Browsers::from_browserslist, minify and to_css instead of reporting errors. Input is invalid CSS (browsers produce an empty sheet). Closed as stale by the reporter.
reviewer_lesson: New CLI code paths must map errors to messages/exit codes, never unwrap().

title: Selector silently dropped from a nested selector list when an earlier rule shares a prefix
trigger: nested rule list with an earlier `&:hover` sibling and a later `&:hover, &:open:not([x])`; any targets
options: targets {} or chrome 111; minify on or off
actual: .card{&:hover{--a:1;--b:2}} (or .card:hover{--a:1;--b:2} when nesting is lowered)
root_cause: Same as #1310 inside the nested CssRuleList::minify: merge drains declarations before the incompatible clone is made (src/rules/mod.rs:800-838). Rule-level minify runs even with minify:false, which is why the unminified output is affected too.

regression.introduced_by: 5c105fb v1.21.0 path; nesting variant reproducible since 1.22 (first version that parses bare nesting)
regression.evidence: same mechanism as #1310; bisect: 1.22.1..master drop the branch with targets

reviewer_lesson: transform() always runs rule-level minification (merging, dedupe, splitting) regardless of `minify`; test merging changes with minify:false too.

title: Two-value `overflow` shorthand is emitted for targets that don't support it
trigger: overflow-x/overflow-y merged into `overflow: hidden scroll` for Safari 14
actual: overflow:hidden scroll — valid there: MDN multiple_keywords gives Chrome 68, Firefox 61, Safari 13.1; caniuse marks 13.1-15.x partial only for the `clip` value
root_cause: Reported versions (Chrome 90 / Safari 15.4) come from a checker that keys on caniuse css-overflow full support, which needs `clip`. Real related bug (unfiled, also raised in #292's comments): the overflow handler has no compat check for `clip`, so `overflow:hidden;overflow:clip` becomes `overflow:clip` and `overflow-x:clip;overflow-y:auto` becomes `overflow:clip auto` for Safari 15 / Chrome 80.
reviewer_lesson: Verify claimed browser floors against MDN BCD and caniuse notes before accepting a compat bug; check new keyword values (clip) separately from the syntax.

title: CLI panics on Browserslist Baseline queries
trigger: CLI --targets 'baseline newly available' or BROWSERSLIST=... --browserslist
expected: resolve Baseline queries, or print a parse error
actual: 1.33.0: panic `Nom("")` at src/main.rs:200/202. master: Baseline queries resolve (browserslist-rs 0.21.2); an unknown query still panics at main.rs:200
root_cause: browserslist-rs 0.19 had no Baseline queries; #1322 (ac64925, master, unreleased) bumped it to 0.21.2. The unwrap() on Browsers::from_browserslist/load_browserslist remains.
reviewer_lesson: Rust-side browserslist (CLI, Rust users) and JS browserslist (Node API) resolve queries independently; a dependency bump changes CLI targets without touching JS users.

title: Minifier wraps a selector list in `:is()` when a target lacks `:has()`, which changes the specificity of every other selector in the list
trigger: selector list containing a :has() selector, targets with :is() but without :has() (Firefox 114 in Vite's baseline-widely-available)
expected: list left unwrapped (or split), specificities unchanged
actual: :is(.a,.b:has(>i)){color:red}.c{color:#00f} — `.a` rises to (0,1,1) and beats `.c`
root_cause: selectors/builder.rs:358 gives Component::Has zero specificity, so CssRuleList::minify's all_equal() check (src/rules/mod.rs:765-769) wrongly decides the :is() wrap is specificity-neutral. The issue's two-rule input merges into one list in a no-targets pass (Vite transformer) and is wrapped in the targeted minify pass.

regression.evidence: 1.19.0 keeps `.a,.b:has(>i)`; 1.21.0+ wrap the list in :is() (b5 local run; the important agent's run did not reproduce it)

reviewer_lesson: Any rewrite that relies on specificity equality must use spec specificity (:is/:not/:has take the max argument, :where zero, nesting `&` like :is); add a cascade test with a competing rule.

title: [bug] Syntax error for container query var evaluation
trigger: var() as the value in a container size query: `@container (width >= var(--x))`
actual: Unexpected token Function("var"); errorRecovery keeps it as unknown tokens with a warning
root_cause: Container (and media) feature values are parsed as typed MediaFeatureValue; css-conditional-5 explicitly allows var() in container queries (resolved against the container, csswg #8088). The issue's own snippet also lacks a closing paren.
reviewer_lesson: Query preludes that can contain arbitrary substitution functions must fall back to token lists, not errors, and must never be range-lowered or simplified.

title: engines.node says >= 12.0.0 but node/index.js uses ??= (Node 15) — main entry is a SyntaxError on 12/13/14
trigger: engines.node >= 12 while node/index.js uses ??= (Node 15) and ?. (Node 14)
actual: SyntaxError on require() for Node < 15
root_cause: package.json engines was stale. #1367 (transpile for Node 12) was closed by Devon ('Node 12 is not supported'); #1388 (c72e6e3) set engines to >= 24.0.0.
reviewer_lesson: An engines bump is itself a breaking change for consumers that use engine-strict installs on older Node LTS lines (tools that still support Node 20/22); flag it in release notes. UNVERIFIED impact.

title: `backdrop-filter` is dropped when it precedes a hand-written `-webkit-backdrop-filter`
trigger: `backdrop-filter` followed by `-webkit-backdrop-filter` in the same rule (no targets needed)
expected: unprefixed backdrop-filter kept (prefix added/removed per targets)
actual: .a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(4px)} — Chrome and Firefox (no -webkit- alias) lose the blur
root_cause: FallbackHandler (src/properties/prefix_handler.rs:93-123) keeps one slot per property for every prefix and, because FilterList::is_compatible is always true (src/properties/effects.rs:410), writes the later prefixed declaration over the earlier unprefixed one at its index. Same for filter/-webkit-filter.

regression.introduced_by: 2694a18 (v1.21.0) Handle properties with auto fallback implementation
regression.evidence: 1.20.0 keeps both declarations; 1.21.0+ keep only the prefixed one; bisect

reviewer_lesson: Compare FallbackHandler-managed properties (color, text-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, fill, stroke, caret-color, caret) against PrefixHandler-managed ones when touching prefix logic.

title: Compatibility with 32-bit system
trigger: install on 32-bit Windows (win32-ia32)
actual: Cannot find module '../lightningcss.win32-ia32-msvc.node'
root_cause: release.yml builds only x86_64/aarch64 Windows; lightningcss-wasm is the fallback.
reviewer_lesson: Platform additions belong in release.yml + scripts/build-npm.js + node/index.js together.

title: Merges animation-timeline for scroll driven animations into invalid shorthand
trigger: `animation: cloud-pan ease-in-out both; animation-timeline: scroll(root y)` (no duration)
options: minify, no targets or Chrome-only targets
actual: animation:ease-in-out both cloud-pan scroll(root y) (invalid in every engine)
root_cause: Same root cause as #1283/#1369 (timeline folded into the shorthand; partial MDN data, no-targets = compatible).
reviewer_lesson: See #1283: never fold a longhand into a shorthand unless real engines accept it in the shorthand.

title: transform() merges an unrelated rule's selector into another rule via an incorrect :is(...) descendant combinator
trigger: input stylesheet with two unclosed `{` (rule inside `@media print` missing `}}`)
actual: :is(.a,nav) .buy{...} inside @media print — the correct nesting interpretation
root_cause: Not a LightningCSS bug: the gist input has an unclosed block at line 2867 (`nav, header, footer, aside { display: none !important;` without `}}`), so per css-syntax + css-nesting every following rule is nested; LightningCSS output matches browser parsing. (Verified locally with the gist and 1.33.0.)

regression.evidence: bisect 1.14.0..1.33.0 + master: same output in every version tested

reviewer_lesson: Before treating a 'selector corruption' report as a bug, check brace balance: implicit nesting of an unclosed block is spec behaviour.

title: Option to allowlist custom (non-standard) pseudo-classes/elements to suppress "not recognized" warnings
trigger: framework pseudo-classes (:global, :deep, :slotted) reaching lightningcss inside Vite
expected: option to declare custom pseudo-classes/elements so no warning is emitted
actual: `'global' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class...` warning per occurrence (output correct)
root_cause: Unknown pseudo-classes become PseudoClass::Custom with an UnsupportedPseudoClass warning (src/selector.rs:210); #871 position is that framework CSS should be compiled first.
reviewer_lesson: Warnings are part of the API surface: Turbopack/Next treat them as errors, so new or reworded warnings are breaking for some hosts.

title: transform() drops !important (or the important value) when merging non-adjacent rules that share a selector
trigger: two non-adjacent rules with the same selector and property, earlier one !important
actual: 1.33.0: .foo{color:red}.a{overflow:auto} (important declaration deleted); master: fixed
root_cause: Duplicate-rule removal (StyleRule::hash_key/is_duplicate, src/rules/style.rs) ignored importance, so the earlier rule looked 'completely overridden'. Fixed by 93b9e66 on master (also fixes #1109), unreleased.

regression.evidence: 1.19.0 keeps both rules; 1.20.0-1.33.0 drop the important one; bisect

reviewer_lesson: Any 'this declaration is overridden' reasoning must compare importance (and layer, origin, prefix) — not just property id and selector.

title: Misleading warning: "'empty' not recognized as a valid pseudo-class" on `::part(foo):not(:empty)`
trigger: tree-structural pseudo-class after ::part(): `a::part(foo):not(:empty)`, `a::part(foo):first-child`
expected: rule kept, and either no warning or a 'not allowed after ::part()' message
actual: rule kept with warning `'empty' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class. Did you mean '::empty'...`
root_cause: AFTER_PART state makes allows_tree_structural_pseudo_classes() false (selectors/parser.rs:175), so the name falls through to parse_non_ts_pseudo_class, which does not know tree-structural names and warns UnsupportedPseudoClass (src/selector.rs:210).
reviewer_lesson: Parser state flags (AFTER_PART, AFTER_PSEUDO_ELEMENT) leak into nested :not()/:is() arguments; test pseudo-classes inside logical combinators after each pseudo-element.

title: @custom-media is not substituted unless targets is set
trigger: drafts.customMedia without targets
actual: emitted verbatim
root_cause: Intended: with no targets lightningcss assumes a browser that implements every spec feature, so nothing is compiled (Devon on #1350). should_compile!(CustomMediaQueries) goes through Targets::is_compatible, which is true without browsers (src/targets.rs:227). Workaround: include: Features.CustomMediaQueries.
reviewer_lesson: 'No targets = perfect spec browser' is the design rule; a PR that compiles something without targets contradicts it unless the output is valid for that perfect browser.

title: `::placeholder` gets incorrectly turned into `:placeholder-shown`
trigger: legacy `:-ms-input-placeholder` / `:-moz-placeholder` (e.g. autoprefixer output for ::placeholder) in a selector list, modern targets
actual: :is(a:-ms-placeholder-shown,b:-ms-placeholder-shown){...}:is(a:placeholder-shown,b:placeholder-shown){...} — the unprefixed copy hides the whole input in modern browsers; `:-ms-placeholder-shown` does not exist anywhere
root_cause: #929 (b93c9c5) mapped `-moz-placeholder`/`-ms-input-placeholder` to PseudoClass::PlaceholderShown(prefix) (src/selector.rs:168-169); these names were legacy placeholder-text styling hooks, are printed back under a different name, and prefix merging adds an unprefixed :placeholder-shown. Related (since dd73b66, 2021): the pseudo-element table maps `::-ms-input-placeholder` to Placeholder(Moz) (src/selector.rs:291), so it prints as `::-moz-placeholder`.

regression.evidence: 1.29.2 keeps :-ms-input-placeholder; 1.29.3+ print :-ms-placeholder-shown plus an unprefixed copy

reviewer_lesson: Mapping a vendor alias onto a standard feature must round-trip the original spelling and match the alias's real semantics; check autoprefixer's mapping before claiming equivalence.

title: errorRecovery: an at-rule not allowed in a style rule drops every declaration before it
trigger: errorRecovery with any recoverable error inside a style block: an at-rule not allowed there (@keyframes, @font-face), the IE `*zoom:1` hack, `!;`, an invalid nested selector
actual: .a{height:2px} (same for `.a{color:red;*zoom:1;width:1px}` -> `.a{width:1px}`)
root_cause: NestedRuleParser::parse_nested clears iter.parser.declarations and important_declarations on every error (src/parser.rs:494-498) — a pattern ported from Servo where the cleared buffer held only the failing declaration, here it is the whole block.

regression.introduced_by: a8b7ea0 (v1.22.0) Update cssparser..., relax nesting rules and enable by default
regression.evidence: 1.21.0 keeps color/width; 1.22.0+ drop them

reviewer_lesson: Run error-recovery tests with an error in the middle of a block and assert that what came before survives; recovery must discard only the bad construct.

title: An earlier filter is dropped when a later one's drop-shadow() color isn't supported by the targets
trigger: `filter: blur(1px); filter: drop-shadow(... oklch(...))` with targets lacking oklch
expected: blur(1px) kept as the fallback (and/or generated sRGB drop-shadow fallbacks)
actual: .a{filter:drop-shadow(0 0 2px oklch(25% .05 30))} — no fallback at all for Chrome 90 (a lone drop-shadow declaration does get #361713 + lab fallbacks)
root_cause: FilterList::is_compatible always returns true (src/properties/effects.rs:410), so FallbackHandler overwrites the earlier filter at its index; fallbacks are only generated for the first occurrence of a property (prefix_handler.rs:100-111). Same for backdrop-filter.

regression.evidence: 1.19.0 outputs blur(1px) + #361713 + lab fallbacks; 1.21.0+ output only the oklch filter

reviewer_lesson: Every value type used by FallbackHandler needs a real IsCompatible (colors, lengths, functions inside it); a stub `true` silently deletes author fallbacks.

title: Media query range syntax transpilation doesn't work for iOS <=16.3
trigger: range media query with < or > lowered for targets without range syntax (iOS/Safari <= 16.3, Chrome < 104)
expected: MQ3-compatible output, e.g. `not all and (min-width:1024px)` at top level or a max-width step
actual: @media screen and not (min-width: 1024px) — MQ3 parsers (the same engines that lack range syntax) reject `not` before a condition, so the rule never applies
root_cause: write_min_max (src/media_query.rs:1522-1575) emits `not (min-/max-...)` for strict comparisons since 7f29035 (fix for #864); MediaRangeSyntax and MQ4 boolean `not`/`or` shipped together (MDN or_syntax: Chrome 104, Safari 16.4).

regression.introduced_by: 7f29035 (v1.29.0) Compile media query range syntax with boolean logic instead of fractional pixels
regression.evidence: 1.28.2 printed (max-width:1024px) (off-by-one, #864); 1.29.0+ print `not (min-width:...)`

reviewer_lesson: Lowered output must use only syntax the lowered-for targets can parse; check the compat of every construct the lowering emits, not just the one it removes.

title: caret, caret-color and caret-shape are reordered when interleaved, changing which one wins
trigger: interleaved caret / caret-color / caret-shape declarations
actual: .a{caret:green;caret-color:#00f} — blue wins instead of green
root_cause: FallbackHandler gives CaretColor and Caret separate slots and writes a repeated property back at its first index (src/properties/prefix_handler.rs:120,151), reordering it across the related shorthand/longhand; caret-shape is not in the handler at all.

regression.evidence: 1.20.0 keeps source order; 1.21.0+ reorder; bisect: 1.14.0..1.20.0 kept order, 1.21.0..master reorder

reviewer_lesson: Writing a later declaration back at an earlier index is only safe if nothing in between sets the same longhands; check shorthand/longhand families (same class as #572/#1084/#1207).

title: `@media (min-width)` is rewritten to `@media (width)`, which always matches
trigger: min-/max- prefixed feature without a value: `(min-width)`, `(max-height)`, `(min-color)`; also in @container
expected: rule stays inert (`not all`, or `(min-width)` kept)
actual: @media (width){...} — matches every viewport with nonzero width
root_cause: MediaFeatureName::parse strips min-/max- (src/media_query.rs:1259-1266) and QueryFeature::parse_name_first returns Boolean{name} when no colon follows, discarding the legacy comparator (src/media_query.rs:1042-1046).

regression.introduced_by: a84fbdb (v1.20.0) Parse media query features according to specified type
regression.evidence: 1.19.0 keeps (min-width); 1.20.0+ print (width)

reviewer_lesson: When parsing normalizes syntax (prefix stripping), confirm the normalized form keeps invalid input invalid; an invalid query must never print as a valid one.

title: color-mix() treats `none` as 0 when the color carrying it is in a different space than the mix
trigger: color-mix() where a color with `none` is in a different space than the interpolation space; also `hsl(none ...)` inside an unparsed color-mix() with var()
actual: #4b2d26 (none treated as 0). Token-list variant: `color-mix(in hsl, hsl(none 50% 50%), var(--c))` -> `color-mix(in hsl, #bf4040, var(--c))`
root_cause: interpolate() converts both colors into the mix space first (From<HSL> etc. call resolve_missing, NaN -> 0) and only then runs fill_missing_components (src/values/color.rs:3534-3556); css-color-4 requires carrying analogous missing components forward. The token-list path serializes hsl(none ...) as hex, losing `none`. 71/89 cross-space WPT cases fail (reporter).

regression.introduced_by: v1.30.0 (exposed by 4ebcb45/#465 parser changes; interpolate() logic dates from 5079e35)
regression.evidence: 1.29.3 left these color-mix() values verbatim (correct); 1.30.0+ resolve them to the wrong color

reviewer_lesson: A parser change that makes more inputs 'typed' also routes them into simplifiers; run the WPT color-computed suites through minify before accepting color parsing changes.

title: Minifier folds animation-timeline into the animation shorthand when no targets are set
trigger: animation shorthand + animation-timeline with no targets (Vite default minify path); thread adds `animation-timeline:none` and nameless `animation: .5s ease-out both`
actual: .reveal{animation:linear both fade view()} (dropped by browsers); `animation:x 1s;animation-timeline:none` -> `animation:1s x none` (none read as fill-mode); `animation:.5s ease-out both` -> `animation:none` (duration/easing/fill lost when the name comes from another rule)
root_cause: Targets::is_compatible returns true without browsers (src/targets.rs:227), so the AnimationTimelineShorthand check never blocks the fold (src/properties/animation.rs:957-965). Separately Animation::to_css prints only `none` when the name is none (src/properties/animation.rs:668-711), dropping the other longhands.

regression.evidence: fold present since f4408c7 (v1.25.0); nameless-shorthand serialization unchanged since 2022

reviewer_lesson: For shorthand serialization, round-trip through a browser: the shorthand must reset/set exactly the same longhands as the input declarations, including when the name is `none`.

title: `errorRecovery` reports a false `EndOfInput` warning for name-only `@container` rules
trigger: name-only @container with errorRecovery
actual: EndOfInput warning and `@container scroll-content  {` (empty Unknown condition printed)
root_cause: ContainerCondition::parse_with_options never returns Err in recovery mode (it warns and returns Unknown with an empty token list), so the name-only branch in the "container" prelude (src/parser.rs:669-682) is unreachable.

regression.evidence: name-only support arrived in #1125 (0e7301a, v1.31.0) without errorRecovery coverage; 1.30.2 dropped the rule entirely under errorRecovery

reviewer_lesson: errorRecovery changes control flow (errors become Ok(Unknown)); every new parse branch keyed on Err must be tested with error_recovery on as well.

title: `height: stretch` causing panic and crashing with vendor prefixes enabled
trigger: `height/width/min-*/max-*: stretch` with include: Features.VendorPrefixes (rspack/vite 'vendor prefixes enabled')
actual: panic: internal error: entered unreachable code at src/properties/size.rs:124 (MaxSize: :257); still on master
root_cause: targets.prefixes() returns VendorPrefix::all() when VendorPrefixes is included (src/targets.rs:245-246); SizeFallback::prefixes passes -o-/-ms- through and Size/MaxSize::to_css only handle None/WebKit/Moz for Stretch (unreachable!()).

regression.evidence: code from 63c4e24 (2022); only reachable with include: VendorPrefixes

title: Excluding DirSelector also disables unrelated selector-list splitting and autofill prefixing
trigger: exclude: Features.DirSelector (or any Selectors member) with targets
repro_css: .a, .x::-webkit-scrollbar { color: red; } input:autofill { color: blue; } .d:dir(rtl) { color: green; }
expected: only :dir() lowering disabled; list splitting and :-webkit-autofill still applied
actual: all selector compat work disabled: list not split, no -webkit-autofill
root_cause: Targets::should_compile_selectors (src/targets.rs:238-241) returns false when exclude intersects Features::Selectors; it gates the whole selector pass (src/rules/mod.rs:758-793, StyleRule::update_prefix). Tailwind v4 (per the optimizeCss options quoted in #1345) passes exclude LogicalProperties|DirSelector|LightDark, so its users never get selector prefixing/splitting.

reviewer_lesson: Feature-flag checks must use the specific flag (should_compile(feature, flag)); intersects() on a group mask silently couples unrelated transforms.

title: Minify: whitespace around * and / in calc() with var() is no longer removed (size regression since 1.31)
trigger: math function containing var(): calc(var(--spacing) * 4), max(0px, var(--y))
actual: whitespace kept (~1% larger Tailwind 4 sheets)
root_cause: 32f1f52 (v1.31.0) stopped removing whitespace in token lists because the grammar is unknown (fixed #1005/#1001/#976/#980/#646/#579). Inside math functions only + and - need whitespace, so a grammar-aware printer could drop it around * / , and inside parens.

regression.introduced_by: 32f1f52 (Do not remove whitespace in token lists), v1.31.0
regression.evidence: 1.30.2 prints calc(var(--x)*2); 1.31.0+ keep the spaces (intentional size/correctness trade-off); bisect: <=1.30.2 compact, >=1.31.0 spaced

reviewer_lesson: Whitespace removal in token lists is only safe where the grammar is known (inside math functions, around * / and commas); never around + / - or in unknown syntax, and custom visitors rely on the whitespace tokens.

title: Custom property color fallbacks (@supports) are dropped for declarations after a nested rule
trigger: custom property with a wide-gamut color declared after a nested rule (CssRule::NestedDeclarations), targets lacking lab()/oklch()
repro_css: :root { --before: oklch(0.96 0.08 58); @supports (color: color-mix(in lab, red, red)) { --x: red; } --after: oklch(0.96 0.08 58); }
expected: --after gets the sRGB value plus an @supports (color: lab(0% 0 0)) override, like --before
actual: --after only gets the gamut-mapped sRGB value; capable browsers render a desaturated color
root_cause: NestedDeclarationsRule::minify applies the lowest fallback in place and queues the @supports rules in a child context, but CssRuleList::minify only calls context.handler_context.get_supports_rules for CssRule::Style, never for CssRule::NestedDeclarations (src/rules/mod.rs:928-932), so they are discarded.

regression.introduced_by: 6c465c1 (v1.30.0): custom-property @supports color fallbacks and NestedDeclarations arrived together
regression.evidence: 1.22.1..1.29.3 lower nothing for this input (unsupported color kept); 1.30.0..master lower it without the @supports copy

reviewer_lesson: Features that emit side rules (@supports overrides, logical-property rules) must be wired for every rule kind that holds declarations: style rules, nested declarations, @starting-style, @page, keyframes.
